reports.program: Survivor legal advocacy, trauma counseling and family safety
reports.priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: AVDA provides legal advocacy and trauma support for domestic-abuse survivors in Greater Houston and neighboring counties.
Its attorneys and advocates help with safety planning, protective orders, divorce, custody and access to practical resources.
The deep review assesses both health and net household resources, using a newer Harris County support reference and full client burdens.
strengths: Primary grant and service records identify a local legal-advocacy delivery route and concrete resource mechanisms.
Randomized intensive advocacy research supports possible lasting safety and wellbeing gains, while its transfer to AVDA remains a judgment.
The model keeps household costs and transfer-payer losses even when outcomes would also occur through alternatives.
reservations: Supported adults and children are not deduplicated households, completed cases or clinical responders.
The exact current recipient outcomes and donation-sensitive capacity remain unverified, and the latest reviewed cost is FY 2023.
Income research is observational; local utility, earnings, overlap and burden values remain conditional hypotheses.

sections.what: AVDA provides legal advocacy and trauma support for domestic-abuse survivors in Greater Houston and neighboring counties. Its attorneys and advocates help with safety planning, protective orders, divorce, custody and access to practical resources. The deep review assesses both health and net household resources, using a newer Harris County support reference and full client burdens.
sections.monitoring: A primary Impact100 Houston 2025 award entry describes more than 2,500 Harris County survivors supported in 2024 and a $24,666 legal-advocacy grant. We use 2,500 as a rounded lower descriptive reference, not an exact observed unique cohort or successful legal outcome. It includes women and children. Request distinct adult households, completed cases, counseling dose, time to safety, retained earnings and payer incidence. The official 2024 report is linked through Canva but its body was inaccessible; current homepage 2025 counters also lack retrievable numbers. Neither is treated as reviewed output. BIPP and outreach are not added to this cohort.
sections.qualitative: The 1994 randomized intensive postshelter advocacy study found better quality of life but no significant between-group physical-abuse difference at six months. The larger 1999 randomized study followed 278 women over two years and found less violence, better quality of life and improved resource access. Both used intensive ten-week advocacy, not AVDA’s measured legal/counseling dose; neither supplies a local QALY coefficient. The Iowa legal-aid panel followed 150 women initially, 85 at one year and 32 at two years; it found favorable changes but no relationship with type or amount of legal services and no untreated comparison. A later income paper reports about $5,500 total annual income change after private/public components, not causal disposable earnings or a charity-return estimate. The model therefore retains uncertain finite health and net-resource judgments and tests the observational figure separately. Houston legal services include Harris, Fort Bend, Austin, Waller, Grimes and Washington; the current numerator is Harris-only, so it uses local share 1 rather than attributing all regional activity to Houston.
sections.cost: Initial $3,105,274.58 becomes $13054938.99 per better life (ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents). The change comes from replacing the historical regionwide reference with a newer Harris-only support reference and correcting burdens to include all exposed households, not just additional outcomes. Whole FY 2023 cost remains $4,051,637; this partial local channel is not a measured whole-portfolio or marginal-gift return. Health is 4.230100 QALYs, signed income/consumption is -1.126572 welfare equivalents, and combined benefit is 3.103528. Income is assessed, not set to zero or omitted because it is negative. Judgments: 2,500 supported adults/children × 0.5 household mapping gives 1,250 exposed household proxies. Additional case response 0.3 gives 375 incremental outcome households; conditional clinical response 0.25 gives 93.75 responders. Utility 0.03 for two years, half-year delay and 3% discount are retained transfer judgments; clinical utility covers physical/trauma symptoms only, not the same financial security already in resources. All 1,250 households retain full 0.001 QALY harm and $100 incremental access burden, including clients whose outcomes alternative aid might produce. Of the 375 additional outcomes, resource response 0.3 gives 112.5 households with one-year net work resources $1,500, otherwise-paid medical costs $100 and external support resources $800. Positive-only overlap 0.5 leaves $1,100 after the separate full access cost; the remaining 1,137.5 households incur the full $100 burden. These are not observed success rates or causal dollar gains. The $1,500 is disposable after tax, withdrawn benefits and recurring work costs; access burden is a distinct cost, not deducted twice. Existing AVDA emergency cash is excluded as a new gain because it is already financed through the numerator. Full $800 counterpart losses per successful recipient are spread over a judged distinct 10,000 payer households at $35,000 baseline, with geographic share applied once. Payer distribution is uncertain, including whether the abuser and recipient remain one consumption unit. No property award, retail legal fee or ordinary survivor earnings is a new income gain. Negative components and full external/retaliation costs are not overlap-discounted. The $5,500 sensitivity is an unadjusted historical association, not a causal after-cost income prediction; overlap and explicit burdens still apply. Zero additional outcome retains harms/costs; no-exposure is tested separately. Shorter duration, clinical-null, financial-only, adverse, payer-loss and full-resource cases remain inspectable. At the unchanged historical regionwide cohort and local share, correcting all-exposed burdens alone gives $5,696,855.08, versus the initial $3,105,274.58; the remaining change to $13,054,938.99 is chiefly the narrower newer Harris reference. This is not evidence that AVDA’s whole portfolio became four times less effective: other counties, BIPP, prevention and child-specific effects remain unmeasured, not assumed zero.
sections.funding: Current expanded working-poor representation is free, while clients may contribute court costs and fees; AVDA validates legal clients’ parking, so the $100 burden is an uncertain combined court/travel/time increment rather than an asserted parking fee. Other legal aid, public protections, compensation programs, private counsel where affordable and family support form the alternative. The new grant shows support for legal advocacy, not measured extra completed cases or an unrestricted gift bottleneck. Nine current attorney/paralegal teams do not establish spare capacity. A newer FY 2024 audit is listed but its original body was not retrieved; its index flags a material weakness, not verified cost or fraud. Full opportunity costs and other portfolio outcomes remain unresolved.

model.costScope: Whole reviewed FY 2023 AVDA annual cost versus a conditional newer Harris-only survivor support channel; unmatched vintage and partial portfolio, not marginal gift EV.
model.geographicAttribution: Rounded 2024 Harris County support reference only; g=1 for this local cohort. Whole recipient cost also covers nonlocal and unmodeled programs.
model.formula: Exposed = N × unique. Incremental outcome households = exposed × b. Health = (clinicalN × unique × b × clinicalResponse × q × finite discounted duration − exposed × full union harm discounted at onset) × g. Resources = one signed household log for successful/other exposed households plus full distinct payer/provider incidence with geography once. Price = 10 × annual cost / positive combined health and resources.
model.counterfactual: Other legal aid, public protection and benefit systems, affordable private counsel where available, alternative counseling, family support and case outcomes without this provider.
model.attribution: b is the share of supported household proxies whose outcomes improve beyond alternative providers; clinicalResponse and resource success are distinct conditional outcomes, not marginal-gift probability. Harms and access costs cover all exposures irrespective of b.
model.uncertainty: Rounded supported survivor count is source-based; household mapping, causal response, utility, duration, resource gains, payer incidence and capacity remain judgments. Randomized external advocacy does not identify AVDA causal effects; observational income change does not identify attributable disposable earnings.
model.nativeOutcomes: Primary grant-maker describes over 2,500 adult/child Harris survivors supported in 2024; not unique households, completed cases or causal health/resources. BIPP, outreach, other counties and child-specific effects remain unmodeled, not zero-valued.

inputs.rationale: Same supported-survivor reference used as opportunities, with household/response judgments; not a separate observed clinical cohort.

inputs.name: unique

inputs.name: b

inputs.rationale: Harris-only modeled reference is inside Houston MSA, so no population or second geographic multiplier.

what: Easter Seals Greater Houston provides disability services for children, adults, veterans and their families.
Programs include early intervention, therapy, respite, assistive technology and family support.
Our initial model combines a conditional child-health and caregiver-resource channel, not every program’s value.
strengths: A plausible connection between completed therapy, function and caregiver resources.
Local services and public-insurance alternatives are described in current primary sources.
Latest audited whole-recipient costs include fundraising costs without adding donor benefits twice.
reservations: Our child reference is historical, and household deduplication and causal response are judgments.
Existing Medicaid, CHIP, insurers and school services reduce additional impact attributable to this provider.
Whole annual cost versus a partial channel does not identify the next unrestricted gift’s return.

sections.what: Easter Seals Greater Houston provides disability services for children, adults, veterans and their families. Programs include early intervention, therapy, respite, assistive technology and family support. Our initial model combines a conditional child-health and caregiver-resource channel, not every program’s value.
sections.monitoring: Request current unique ECI households, completed therapy and incremental function against public and school alternatives, plus caregiver net resources. The 2023 annual report describes 7,662 ECI children and 81,078 hours; hours are not additional people. Current homepage lists over 14,500 disability and military neighbors, not all clinical successes. Audit page labels an annual report 2024, but the linked annual-report page exposes a 2023 PDF.
sections.qualitative: A plausible connection between completed therapy, function and caregiver resources. Local services and public-insurance alternatives are described in current primary sources. Latest audited whole-recipient costs include fundraising costs without adding donor benefits twice. Our child reference is historical, and household deduplication and causal response are judgments. Existing Medicaid, CHIP, insurers and school services reduce additional impact attributable to this provider. Whole annual cost versus a partial channel does not identify the next unrestricted gift’s return. Local operating EIN 74-1238418, not the national Easterseals affiliate. The official donation route supports Greater Houston services.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $22.21 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 12.083563 clinical QALYs and 1.401940 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.004502 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $29,957,609. Judged mapping: historical 7,662 ECI child opportunities × household uniqueness 0.9 × incremental access 0.25 gives 1,723.95 exposed households. Clinical response 0.3 gives 517.185 child health responders at utility 0.015 for two years after a half-year delay. All exposed households retain a full 0.0005 QALY harm and $100 access burden. A 20% caregiver resource response gets $1,500 one-year disposable work resources and $100 otherwise-paid household medical savings; positive components alone receive overlap 0.5. No child lifetime earnings are counted. Houston share 0.85 is a catchment hypothesis, not observed geography. Union 1723.95 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 517.185; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $30,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Caregiver work resources are after taxes, benefit withdrawals, commuting and childcare, not gross wages or time valued twice. Access fees and foregone access time remain in the full separate burden. Household medical savings must be actual otherwise-paid cash, not insured reimbursement or retail therapy value. Insurer, public-payer and substitute-provider opportunity costs remain unknown centrally and have adverse scenarios; recipient recognized spending is already in the numerator and must not be subtracted a second time as the same cost. External payer costs scale by Houston-attributed recipient exposures once, then a distinct dispersed payer pathway uses editionShare 1; no second local haircut removes those costs. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: Public contributions cover gaps alongside government grants, insurer reimbursements and fees. The homepage’s $100 therapy-hour appeal is not a verified marginal clinical outcome. No additional donor-funded completed cohort has been demonstrated. The FY 2025 audit has an unmodified opinion but identifies significant deficiencies involving recording support, conditional grants and opening balances; these are control findings, not a fraud finding.

model.costScope: Full audited FY 2025 operating recipient expenses, including direct donor benefits, versus a partial child-health and caregiver-resource channel.
model.geographicAttribution: ECI’s twelve-county catchment exceeds Houston MSA; judged local share 0.85.
model.formula: Health = (clinicalN × unique × b × clinicalResponse × q × finite discounted duration − N × unique × b × union harm discounted at onset) × edition share. Income = signed joint household log welfare equivalents with positive-only overlap and full costs. Better-life cost = 10 × full annual cost / (health + income), only when combined benefits are positive.
model.counterfactual: Medicaid, CHIP, private insurance, other therapists, school and early-intervention providers and family support retained.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Historical children served and service hours; current disability services, not observed causal QALYs or earnings.

reports.program: Civil legal aid for housing, safety, benefits and economic security
reports.priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: Lone Star Legal Aid provides free civil legal assistance to eligible low-income people in Texas and southwest Arkansas.
It handles housing, family safety, public benefits, consumer, disaster and employment matters.
Our deep model examines a conditional housing-health and household-resource channel, including full client burdens and distinct payer losses.
strengths: Legal barriers can affect both health and net household resources.
Matched 2024 recipient finances and case categories support a coherent annual reference.
Controlled legal-aid evidence and eviction research clarify mechanisms, alternatives and signed financial incidence.
reservations: Cases, categories and individuals are not deduplicated completed representation or causal successful households.
The reported economic awards and savings are not causal net consumption or all new government benefits.
Houston share, additional outcomes and health effects are unmeasured hypotheses; marginal donation response is unknown.

sections.what: Lone Star Legal Aid provides free civil legal assistance to eligible low-income people in Texas and southwest Arkansas. It handles housing, family safety, public benefits, consumer, disaster and employment matters. Our deep model examines a conditional housing-health and household-resource channel, including full client burdens and distinct payer losses.
sections.monitoring: The matched 2024 report records 25,111 cases, 61,289 individuals, 12,400+ housing cases and $15.3M awards/savings. Current 2025 homepage records 27,973 cases, 67,153 individuals, 6,099 housing cases and $12.69M awards/savings. Differences in definitions/vintages are not demonstrated effectiveness changes. No newer audited 2025 cost is imported. Request Houston unique households, service intensity, controlled outcomes, cash-versus-stock awards, payment timing, payer source and donation-funded capacity.
sections.qualitative: A selected Massachusetts District Court randomized offer of full representation improved housing retention versus already-unbundled assistance. A companion Housing Court trial found no substantial incremental outcome against forms help and lawyer-for-day assistance. These contrasting trials make alternative aid and client selection decisive; neither measures LSLA health or net dollar resources. Judge-leniency instrumental-variable research in Chicago and NYC links eviction to hospital visits and earnings losses over two years, but estimates eviction consequences rather than legal representation. Earnings are not after-tax consumption and retained housing is not measured QALYs. Current LSLA eligibility may result in advice/brief help rather than full representation. Housing and domestic-violence categories overlap; they are not added as distinct health beneficiaries.
sections.cost: The conditional annual reference changes from $22.50M to $90.05M per better life: 6.513049 health QALYs and -1.690935 signed resource equivalents. Original coefficients with only full-exposure burdens give $59.17M; the subsequent case-scope and additionality judgments give $90.05M. This is a modeling correction/refinement, not evidence whole-portfolio effectiveness fell fourfold. Full matched FY2024 cost remains $43,421,735. N=25,111 case opportunities, unique=.8 and Houston share=.5 are judgments, not observed unique local clients. ClinicalN=12,400 is the reported housing-case envelope rather than an arbitrary quarter of all cases; no separate DV count is added. Additionality .2 replaces .3 as a research-informed mixed-case judgment considering divergent controlled evidence and alternative aid, not an empirical LSLA coefficient. Clinical response .3, utility .02 and two-year persistence remain conditional hypotheses; they are not trial-calibrated QALYs. All 20,088.8 exposed household proxies bear full .0005 QALY harm and $50 access/time burden, independent of additional benefit. Resource successes are 25% of additional households, receiving one-year $2,000 net benefit/settlement resources, $500 disposable work and $100 otherwise-paid care saving. These are hypotheses, not the reported $15.3M awards divided into consumption; property stocks, rent waivers and public-benefit awards differ. Positive components alone receive .5 overlap; negatives and burdens remain full in one joint household log at $20,000 consumption. Work is net of taxes, withdrawn benefits and ordinary work costs. Distinct public/counterparty households bear $1,000 per Houston-attributed success at $50,000 baseline, applied locally once with payer share one; full transfer loss and additional work displacement are stressed. External provider costs attach to all exposed, not only successful cases. Financial-only, clinical-null, adverse, alternative-representation null, short persistence, opportunity costs, no transfer and no-exposure scenarios remain. Missing broader legal/family effects and marginal capacity are unmeasured, not zero. Full annual recipient cost against this partial channel is not complete portfolio EV or an established gift price.
sections.funding: State and federal grants fund most work. Official donation route supports operating EIN 74-1537787, not other justice recipients. Free client eligibility does not establish completed full representation or zero client time costs. This matched 2024 annual reference is not the audited 2025 budget or a verified cost to expand case capacity.

model.costScope: Whole FY 2024 annual legal recipient cost versus one conditional legal-safety and signed-resources channel; not complete portfolio or marginal gift EV.
model.geographicAttribution: 2024 case and housing categories cover broad Texas/Arkansas recipient area; Houston .5 is a judgment, not observed local cases. Counterparty costs allocate local recipient-linked amounts once.
model.formula: exposed=N*unique; incremental=exposed*b; health responders=clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse; health=(responders*q*discounted T - exposed*harm)*g; joint household net resource logs for disjoint successes/other exposed; locally allocated distinct payer loss once; price=10*C/(health+signed income equivalent)
model.counterfactual: Public-funded aid, pro bono and alternative legal providers, self-help, existing benefit eligibility and case resolution retained; only incremental outcomes count.
model.attribution: Mixed-case additionality .2 is judgment informed by contrasting controlled legal-aid regimes; no trial coefficient imported universally. Full client harms/burdens persist without benefit response.
model.uncertainty: Clinical response, utility/persistence, unique households, mixed service dose, net resources, payer mix, Houston share and marginal donation capacity unmeasured.
model.nativeOutcomes: Matched2024 25,111 cases, 12,400+ housing cases, 61,289 individuals and gross awards/savings; not unique incremental outcomes.

sections.what: Bayou City Waterkeeper uses science, law and community partnerships to protect water and reduce flooding in the Lower Galveston Bay watershed. Its work includes sewage accountability, wetlands protection and advocacy for infrastructure in underserved communities. This deep review models a conditional sewage-accountability channel, not all flood, wetland or industrial-risk work.
sections.monitoring: Ask for completed lateral repairs or improved public milestones, distinct affected households, repeat exposure episodes and residual repair spending versus mandatory city action. Verify the campaign’s public appropriation, delivery, coalition contribution and net utility-bill or taxpayer costs. The 2025 report pages 10–12 and 29 were visually reviewed; no recipient causal clinical cohort was found.
sections.qualitative: A specific implementation and affordability gap remains beyond mandatory public sewer upgrades. Current monitoring, legal advocacy and community coalition work provide a plausible accountability mechanism. Original epidemiology supports sewage exposure as an acute health risk, although it does not measure this charity’s effect. The $20 million lateral-repair fund is a campaign demand, not delivered repairs or proven cash capacity. Household reach, clinical utility, implementation probability and recipient additionality remain judgments rather than measured causal outcomes. The full annual recipient cost is compared with one partial channel; public costs, other portfolio benefits and the next gift response are unresolved. The legal recipient remains EIN 26-0187498.
sections.cost:
Initial $28.28M → current $26.69M per better life (ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents), with health 0.259638 and signed net resource equivalents 0.222612. The small improvement reflects separating actual advocacy burdens from potential downstream beneficiaries, not evidence of higher effectiveness or a delivered $20M fund. Full FY2024 recognized recipient cost remains $1,287,349. The baseline is public enforcement, required city investment, other advocates and ordinary repair decisions. The 20,000 household opportunity envelope, 0.2 policy success × 0.5 implementation × 0.1 recipient attribution, 30% clinical response, 0.002 utility gain and three years of avoided recurring exposure after a two-year delay are retained transparent hypotheses. Original South Carolina case-crossover evidence links overflows to acute GI diagnoses over 0–4 days, not a measured QALY coefficient. Atlanta infrastructure lowered overflow frequency, but the study did not establish a protective change in the per-event GI association; neither study directly estimates Houston advocacy effects. A one-season clinical sensitivity challenges durability rather than assuming acute illness lasts three years.

Of 200 expected additional household exposures addressed, 40 have a hypothesized $1,000 one-time otherwise-paid repair saving; positive gains receive 0.5 overlap adjustment. This is genuine avoided resource expenditure only if households would otherwise pay, not public expenditure or a subsidy automatically treated as net welfare. One welfare adult-equivalent per household and $30,000 annual consumption are judgments. An independently judged 100 engaged household-equivalent cohort bears $20 effort costs and 0.00005 process-stress harm regardless of success; potential beneficiaries are not automatically advocates. Random-overlap judgment partitions households into 0.2 changed participants, 39.8 changed nonparticipants and 99.8 other participants. Same-household same-year gains and costs enter one joint log, with all negative costs retained. Immediate effort costs are logged at year zero for all 100 engaged households, while repair savings are logged at year two for 40 expected responders. Different-year welfare is discounted separately, never capitalizing costs inside a future log. When costs and gains occur in the same year, overlapping household and payer components are jointly logged. Houston share 0.8 is applied once.

Distinct payer losses test repair subsidies, compliance resources, taxes and utility bills; central zero external loss is unknown-neutral, not measured absence. The historical $2B over 15 years is required public investment, neither charity income nor household benefit. The advocacy-only recognized cost sensitivity $309,173 excludes overhead, education and other services and is not a verified sewage allocation or marginal gift. The 2025 report’s rounded revenue less net asset change implies roughly $1.138M expense only as an unaudited inference sensitivity. Wetlands, flood resilience and industrial-risk outcomes remain unknown, not zero. The reference is full recipient cost versus partial sewage benefits, not complete portfolio EV.
sections.funding: Current donations use the official legal recipient. Rounded 2025 net assets and cash indicate organizational resources, not unrestricted capacity or the marginal effect of another donation; request a restricted campaign budget, delivery milestones and alternative funding.

model.costScope: Full FY2024 recipient cost versus one annual conditional sewage-compliance channel; not complete portfolio EV or marginal gift.
model.geographicAttribution: Lower Galveston Bay watershed with judged Houston metro share 0.8.
model.formula: Health = clinicalN × unique × b × clinicalResponse × q × finite discounted years minus full independent engaged-cohort process harm, localized once. Resources = disjoint household joint logs with positive-only overlap, full negative burdens and distinct payer incidence. Price = 10 × annual cost / combined equivalents only if positive.
model.counterfactual: Federal/state enforcement, mandatory city upgrades, other advocates and ordinary privately paid repairs without BCWK; existing public $2B obligations are baseline, not the recipient’s new benefit.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded annual finance and campaign stage; every reach/probability/utility/duration/resource mapping remains judgment. Clinical studies establish risk mechanisms, not local charity causal coefficients. Complete portfolio and marginal-gift EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Monitoring and coalition advocacy; $20M lateral fund is demanded, not delivered. The 2025 annual report describes public implementation gaps and statewide funding possibility, not unique completed recipient-caused household outcomes.

what: The Lighthouse of Houston provides low-vision health services, assistive technology, training and community programs.
It also offers employment through business services and supports independent living.
The deep review uses separate low-vision and training contact envelopes, full consolidated annual costs, and signed health plus net household resources.
strengths: A randomized low-vision rehabilitation trial supports functional improvement beyond basic care, although it does not measure Houston QALYs.
Current course descriptions identify training content, fees and public workforce referral alternatives.
Consolidated audited accounts make it possible to avoid counting related-entity transfers twice.
reservations: The report chart gives 500 clinic and 411 training contacts, not unique clients or incremental placements.
Current employment shares do not establish additional jobs or earnings caused by donations.
Whole consolidated cost versus the narrow modeled channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift estimate.

sections.what: The Lighthouse of Houston provides low-vision health services, assistive technology, training and community programs. It also offers employment through business services and supports independent living. The deep review uses separate low-vision and training contact envelopes, full consolidated annual costs, and signed health plus net household resources.
sections.monitoring: The 2025 annual report chart records 500 low-vision clinic and 411 technology education/training contacts within 24,084 mixed impacts; neither chart nor total is a deduplicated outcome cohort. Its employee statement explicitly refers to 2024. Ask for dated unique clients, completed certifications, referral funding, retained after-tax earnings and comparison outcomes. Contact counts, employees and certification launch do not establish additional jobs.
sections.qualitative: LOVIT II randomized 323 predominantly elderly male veterans to rehabilitation or basic low-vision care. Four-month functional improvements support a mechanism, while the generic health measure did not differ; Houston utility gain, clinical response and persistence remain judgments. Device-only, insurance, workforce referral and other training providers remain alternatives. Operating EIN 74-1146781 differs from Foundation 74-1618607; the consolidated boundary includes living centers and removes internal grants and management fees once.
sections.cost: The conditional annual two-channel estimate changes from $9.81M to $38.94M per better life: 1.872733 health QALYs and -0.023191 signed income equivalents. This is mainly a cohort and burden-accounting revision, not evidence the whole organization became four times less effective. The old-cohort burden-only case isolates accounting from the narrower current reference. Full FY2025 consolidated annual cost remains $7,201,649. N=911 is the chart contact envelope (500 clinic plus 411 training), not unique people; unique=.8 and Houston share=.95 are judgments. Clinical responders equal 500 × .8 × .5 additionality × .4 response; utility .015 for two years and half-year delay remain hypotheses, not trial QALYs. Resource successes are 411 × .8 × .5 × .15; only this training subgroup can receive $4,000 disposable earnings after tax, benefits withdrawal and recurring work costs. Joint $100 otherwise-paid care saving is a conservative hypothesis limited to that same household subgroup, not a separate duplicated population. Positive components alone retain .75 overlap; every exposed household incurs $100 access burden and .0005 QALY harm, even if b=0. One joint log per household uses $25,000 annual consumption. Central assumes funded training but not free public resources: payer and training-time effects are unresolved and tested separately. Full self-pay sensitivity charges $2,495 tuition plus 150 hours at judged $15/hour only to the training subgroup, in addition to access cost. Partial certification, short health persistence, clinical null, lost work, displaced workers and payer/provider losses are explicit scenarios. Payer losses allocate Houston recipients once then apply editionShare=1. A no-exposure case is distinct from ineffective existing services with burdens. All other programs remain unmeasured, not zero; full organization cost against two partial benefit channels is neither total portfolio EV nor verified next-gift capacity.
sections.funding: Official donations support the operating charity. Current course fees and TWC referral routes establish funding alternatives, not a charitable marginal placement price. Public or employer costs and displaced-worker losses require evidence before asserting complete net welfare.

model.costScope: Full consolidated FY2025 expenses including merchandise costs and direct donor benefits, net of internal transfers, versus a partial health and training channel.
model.geographicAttribution: Greater Houston services with judged local share 0.95; consolidated living-center coverage may differ.
model.formula: exposed=N*unique; clinical responders=clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse; health=(responders*q*discounted T - exposed*harm)*g; training successes=trainingN*unique*b*success; joint signed household log gains and full all-exposure burdens; local payer allocations once; price=10*C/(health+income-equivalent)
model.counterfactual: Basic low-vision care, public workforce and insurance funding, other training providers, and ordinary earnings retained. Trial effects cannot be imported as Houston utility or placement estimates.
model.attribution: Additional benefits apply to b responders; all service exposure burdens and harm remain full. Training earnings only for its own subgroup.
model.uncertainty: Unresolved unique clients, Houston share, placement response, generic utility, persistence, payer costs and gift capacity; source-scope change separated from accounting correction.
model.nativeOutcomes: 2025 report chart: 500 low-vision clinic and 411 training contacts; 24,084 mixed impacts are not unique clients or successful placements.

sections.what: Brighter Bites distributes fresh produce to families through schools and community partners. Nutrition education and cooking demonstrations help children and caregivers use that produce. Its Houston program is part of a broader multiregional nonprofit.
sections.monitoring: The 2025 annual impact report records 264,354 students, teachers and families impacted, not unique households. It reports a 40% SNAP-Ed funding loss and the closure of Austin in December 2025. Houston's 2024–2025 school locations are published, but we did not verify an annual Houston household cohort or local budget. Current descriptions of 20-pound weekly bags differ from the original return's 25-pound, 50-serving description. The 2025 Cambridge paper uses three Houston focus groups conducted in 2022, with single-group purposive and convenience sampling. Participants described buying new produce; the study does not establish controlled clinical or expenditure effects. Useful follow-up would include distinct households, pickup frequency, geographic budgets, causal health effects and actual cash expenditure.
sections.qualitative: Recurring distribution combines food access with practical preparation skills. Houston schools and food-bank partners provide an established delivery network. Published research examines dietary behaviors and family shopping mechanisms. Mixed counts of students, teachers and families do not identify unique annual households. Dietary behavior studies and focus groups do not measure clinical QALYs or causal net cash gains. National costs, Houston allocations, funding cuts and donated resources require careful boundaries. The original IRS return identifies Brighter Bites, EIN 47-4070026, headquartered in Houston. The current Houston page lists local partners, schools and donation links. The official donation page embeds Blackbaud. No transaction was performed.
sections.cost: Our conditional reference is approximately $88.83 million per better life: ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents. It combines 0.992638 clinical QALYs with 0.825477 signed income/consumption equivalents. The denominator is the full national annual recognized cost of $16,150,774; only a hypothetical Houston nutrition and household-resource channel enters the benefit numerator. This is not a matched Houston program cost, complete organization expected value, restricted-gift price or demonstrated next-dollar return. A proportional $10,000 share corresponds to approximately 0.001126 combined equivalents under this accounting hypothesis, not proven marginal expansion. We use 25,000 national annual family opportunities and 0.8 distinct-household mapping as explicit unsupported judgments, not a conversion of the mixed 264,354-person count. Additional annual response of 0.5, relative to food banks, SNAP, school meals and existing purchases, leaves 10,000 household proxies. One child per household supplies the clinical proxy: response 0.3, utility improvement 0.01 for half a year, and full union harm of 0.001. These are nutrition hypotheses, not measured mortality or QALY effects. A judged Houston share of 0.2 is applied once to health and resources; we have not verified the geographic allocation. Half of exposed households are assumed to avoid $200 of otherwise-paid food costs after benefits and replacement support. A 0.5 positive-only overlap discount precedes the full $25 pickup, preparation and foregone-time burden, leaving $75 for successful households and −$25 for the others. Resources use one adult consumption-equivalent per household at a $30,000 annual baseline, with components netted before one logarithm. Increased produce purchases can raise spending; adverse cases retain negative gains, full costs and union harms. Retail bag value, donated-produce valuation, gross wages and property wealth are not added. Food-bank inputs, volunteer time, public funding and other provider opportunity costs remain unknown centrally; higher-cost and payer/provider-loss cases test their incidence. Benefits outside Houston and from other programs are omitted from this partial-channel reference, not judged zero.
sections.funding: The original FY2024 functional expense is $15,948,524. Adding $202,250 of direct event expenses netted from revenue gives $16,150,774. FY2023 is $15,132,611 plus $20,814, or $15,153,425; FY2022 is $15,514,468 plus $188,812, or $15,703,280. The FY2025 impact report's unaudited financial table reports $16,383,946 of expenses, including $6,883,080 in kind. We have not verified that figure as an event-inclusive denominator or complete social cost, so it remains financial-vintage context rather than the central cost. The latest index also flags FY2025 audit control issues that need further review. The current $350-per-family annual solicitation is not a measured next-gift price.

model.geographicAttribution: Judged .2Houstonshare once; nomatchedobservedlocalcostallocation
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Foodbanks,SNAP,schoolmeals,existingfamilyproducepurchasesandotherprovidersretained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.

what: Air Alliance Houston researches air pollution and supports communities exposed to industrial and transport emissions.
It monitors local air and helps residents engage with permits, regulators and public planning.
Its campaigns seek cleaner air and stronger protections for Houston-area neighborhoods.
strengths: Current reporting identifies named local permit and monitoring mechanisms with coalition partners.
Original finance separates advocacy and research costs from wider recipient work.
Primary quasi-experimental pollution evidence supports potential health and work channels when pollution actually changes.
reservations: Sensors, notifications and permit holds do not establish attributable sustained pollution reduction.
Potential benefit residents are not automatically advocates bearing process costs; participation is separately judged.
Local dose, net resources, implementation probability, displacement and gift-driven expansion remain unknown.

sections.what: Air Alliance Houston researches air pollution and supports communities exposed to industrial and transport emissions. It monitors local air and helps residents engage with permits, regulators and public planning. Its campaigns seek cleaner air and stronger protections for Houston-area neighborhoods.
sections.monitoring: FY 2025 reports 56,519 AirMail households across 12 permits, two concrete facilities on hold and over 70 sensors across 14 neighborhoods; current September 2026 monitoring 100+sensors/10 communities uses a later scope. Neither sensors nor households notified establish unique health beneficiaries. Current report explicitly explains ozone patterns through weather and maintenance, not recipient causality. Its cleaner metal-recycler anecdote after a press event is not a controlled measured emissions change. The cancelled EPA grant cannot be delivered capacity. The October 2025 Julpit recipient statement describes a voided permit and homes nearby, not permanent prevention; the current updates index includes reapplication. Request permit conditions, actual enforcement/operations dates, pollutant-specific exposure before/after versus weather and alternative regulation, active participant households, net household resources and displaced worker/provider incidence.
sections.qualitative: Current campaigns name port partners, industrial permits and transport mechanisms. Original Chay/Greenstone Clean Air Act research uses regulatory nonattainment variation to study infant mortality; this supports an implemented-pollution health mechanism, not a generic adult QALY coefficient or AAH attribution. Original Hanna/Oliva author-hosted refinery-closure study examines actual pollution changes and labor hours with neighborhood comparisons; it is not local after-tax income, does not make every resident employed and cannot import gross wages or closure effects into advocacy. Reading focused on its abstract/introduction and identification discussion, not all 58 pages. No national population or mortality statistic is multiplied into a local impact claim. Cleaner air can improve health and work, while compliance, product prices or displaced employment can offset net resources. Implementation, pollutant dose, alternative regulator/industry action and recipient causal share remain explicit uncertainties.
sections.cost: Initial $21.37 M per better life is preserved: health 1.147147 plus income .067097. Revised conditional reference $20.56 M combines health 1.165056 and signed resources .096914 =1.261970 equivalent years against $2,594,790. This modest change separates the engagement population and joint resource incidence; it is not a measured effectiveness improvement. The original policy factor .3 enactment*.5 implementation*.2 recipient attribution=.03 is retained judgment, with 10,000 potential resident opportunities,150 clinical responders, q.003 for 3 finite years after 2-year delay and .95 local share. These are not sensor, permit or trial coefficients. A separate illustrative 100 engaged household-consumption proxies, not observed 100 unique bus-attendee households, bear full $10 process/time and .0001 stress harm independent of b. Assumed random overlap splits 150 resource-success proxies into 1.5 engaged and 148.5 not-engaged;98.5 unsuccessful engaged proxies retain full costs. Each overlapping household has one joint log, not averaged $0.10 cost applied to all 10,000;100/300/1000/full-resident burdens are distinct sensitivity regimes. $100 otherwise-paid medical/foregone-work resource hypothesis, success.5 and positive-only overlap.5 yield 50 net positive resources before full participant costs, not healthcare retail price or duplicated clinical welfare. Unknown workgain zero is not evidence no income benefit; positive and negative cases are explicit. Distinct displaced workers are separate assumed people whose losses occur conditional on additional implemented policy b, not on failed policy. External payer/compliance incidence is localized once; negative costs are never removed by positive overlap. Actual b 0 leaves advocacy effort burdens; N 0 with burdenN 0 means no exposure and is different. Full annual recipient cost includes other channels not modeled. Advocacy+research recognized $558,209 sensitivity gives $4.42 M, excluding overhead, fundraising and regulator/industry resources and not establishing a single campaign cost; all-program $2,082,550 is also broader than the channel. Whole portfolio EV and marginal gift response remain unknown.
sections.funding: The latest original return covers July 2024–June 2025: $2,588,981 of functional expenses plus $5,809 of direct event expenses netted from revenue gives $2,594,790. The years ending June 2024 and June 2023 report $3,200,249 and $2,785,438, with unpopulated direct-event expense lines. FY 2025 education expense of $1,524,341 and air-quality advocacy expense of $180,396 are activity costs, not measured health returns. The annual report records the cancellation of an EPA grant; its intended funding cannot be counted as delivered capacity. The conditional benefits are finite future effects attributed to one annual work hypothesis, not perpetual policy credit. Original advocacy $180,396 plus research $377,813 = $558,209; these cannot be assigned wholesale to one permit campaign. Total program expense $2,082,550 is an additional partial numerator, not full resources. Current funding loss and coalition/public baseline prevent an automatic proportional next-gift claim.

model.costScope: Full annual recognized recipient expense against hypothetical single implemented local permit/mitigation channel; other campaign, education and monitoring benefits unknown, not zero. Not complete portfolio EV or marginal donation.
model.geographicAttribution: Houston metro-focused campaign envelope; N10,000 potential residents and .95 local share are judgments, not sensor or AirMail beneficiary counts. No national regulatory benefits credited.
model.formula: Potential residents=N*unique; incremental policy benefit union=N*unique*b (.3 enactment*.5 implementation*.2 recipient attribution). Clinical=clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse*q*discounted finite years minus independent engaged-population process harms. Joint resource logs partition changed engaged, changed non-engaged and unchanged engaged households; costs stay full for actual engaged cohort even b0. Distinct payer losses localized once; displaced worker losses conditional on additional implementation b. Headline=10*C/(health+signed resources).
model.counterfactual: EPA,TCEQ,industrycompliance,othercoalitionactors andbaselinepolicy retained; .3change*.5implementation*.2recipientattribution
model.attribution: Separates enactment .3, implementation .5, recipient attribution .2 against regulator/industry/coalition alternatives; multiplicative .03 is explicit judgment, not estimated local success frequency. Participant effort burdens have their own population, not policy-success probability.
model.uncertainty: Implemented local emissions/dose and population remain unverified; causal pollution studies inform mechanisms, not local QALYs, income or recipient attribution. Participation overlap, net resources, compliance/displacement and marginal capacity are uncertain.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional implemented emissions reduction and actual exposure change, not sensors, households mailed, testimony, permit hold or grant award.

reports.program: Home repair, disaster readiness and community recovery
reports.priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: West Street Recovery repairs disaster-damaged homes in Northeast Houston.
It also equips neighborhood disaster-response hubs and supports resident-led organizing and research.
The work combines practical recovery assistance with efforts to improve drainage and public disaster aid.
strengths: Repair work addresses unsafe homes and loss of essential water access.
Local survivor and contractor participation connects recovery work with community capacity.
Original financial returns separate repair activity from organizing and broader services.
reservations: Historical unique homes and cumulative families do not establish current annual completed repairs.
Clinical changes and actual avoided household expenditure are not causally measured.
Organizing, disaster aid, partner labor and marginal cash capacity require distinct attribution.

sections.what: West Street Recovery repairs disaster-damaged homes in Northeast Houston. It also equips neighborhood disaster-response hubs and supports resident-led organizing and research. The work combines practical recovery assistance with efforts to improve drainage and public disaster aid.
sections.monitoring: The 2023 year-in-review self-report gives over50 unique homes,32 restored-water families, one full rebuild and two large projects. Its CMS date is February2022 despite a2023 narrative; publication vintage is inconsistent. Current service copy gives28 studs-up repairs,130 water restorations and300 families since2017, all cumulative. Do not add overlapping counts. Request recent dated completions, residual hazards, household costs and follow-up.
sections.qualitative: Repair work addresses unsafe homes and loss of essential water access. Local survivor and contractor participation connects recovery work with community capacity. Original financial returns separate repair activity from organizing and broader services. Historical unique homes and cumulative families do not establish current annual completed repairs. Clinical changes and actual avoided household expenditure are not causally measured. Organizing, disaster aid, partner labor and marginal cash capacity require distinct attribution. Original FY2024 return confirms West Street Recovery, EIN82-2708194, Houston. Current official donate page embeds Donorbox and links PayPal; no transaction performed.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $157.93 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 0.097278 clinical QALYs and 0.057712 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.000633 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $2,447,774. Historical-reference judgment50 annual unique repair-household opportunities, not current annual measured completions. Alternative aid, contractors, insurance and family replacement leave annual additional response .4, yielding20 exposed households. Clinical response .3, utility .02 for one year and full union harm .001 are unsupported safety/comfort priors, not mortality estimates. Resource success .5 gives$1,000 otherwise-paid repair, temporary displacement or care expenditure genuinely avoided after insurance, transfers and maintenance. Positive overlap .5 then full$100 process/time burden yields$400 for successful households and minus$100 for others. Property appreciation, full retail repair value and local contractor payments are not extra net household income. Union 20 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 6; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $25,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Outside volunteers, contractors paid elsewhere and public relief opportunity costs are unknown centrally; explicit larger-cost/provider-loss cases preserve their possible incidence. Policy and organizing benefits are unknown and omitted from this partial-channel reference, not judged zero. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: FY2024 original whole recipient functional expense$2,447,774; no populated netted event or inventory expenses. FY2023$1,172,801 and FY2022$1,103,993 are original prior-year cost references. FY2024 repair program expense$861,109 is not the whole recipient denominator; voter engagement$323,352 and other services explain why this repair-only model is not total portfolio EV. Unknown donated labor and government-incidence costs prevent a complete social-cost claim.

model.costScope: Whole annual recognized recipient cost versus conditional repair safety and net household-resource channel; policy and other programs unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Northeast Houston repair channel; judged .98 metro share once
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Public disaster aid, insurance, paid contractors, other nonprofits and family recovery retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Completed safer homes and actual household costs avoided, not cumulative repairs, public appropriations or contractor revenue

reports.priceScope: Conditional full annual recipient cost versus limited home-delivered nutrition/connection and net food-resource channel; not complete portfolio EV or verified marginal gift.

what: Meals on Wheels Montgomery County brings meals and friendly wellbeing checks to homebound older residents.
Its separate transportation program provides accessible rides to essential appointments and errands.
Congregate meals and other support help local seniors maintain nutrition and independence.
strengths: Latest original return distinguishes unique home-delivered recipients from meals and transport trips.
Primary randomized evidence supports a connection mechanism against a waiting-list alternative.
Signed food resources and exposure costs are modeled separately from clinical health, with complete original diagnostics.
reservations: Meals, survey satisfaction and independence claims are not causal clinical outcomes.
Service duration is a meal-density proxy, not observed completed dose for each person.
Net grocery savings, household overlap, volunteer costs and next-donation response remain unmeasured.

sections.what: Meals on Wheels Montgomery County brings meals and friendly wellbeing checks to homebound older residents. Its separate transportation program provides accessible rides to essential appointments and errands. Congregate meals and other support help local seniors maintain nutrition and independence.
sections.monitoring: Fresh original FYending September 2025 return: 227,136 home-delivered meals to 1,178 seniors; 19,145 trips to 493 people; 781 congregate dinners. Transport and meal recipients may overlap and are not added. Homepage's 340,000 meals and story's self-reported emotional health/main meal claims use different scope and no controlled counterfactual. Average 192.82 meals per annual unique recipient corresponds to 38.56 five-meal weeks, or .7416 year of weekday exposure. This is not a verified enrollment-duration distribution, daily contact frequency or causal health dose. Request entry/exit, meal uptake, actual unique household/spouse overlap, nutritional risk and loneliness before/after against alternatives, net grocery expenditure, SNAP and family substitution, caregiver resources and access harms.
sections.qualitative: The original More Than a Meal randomized study assigned 626 waiting-list seniors across eight programs to daily delivery, weekly delivery or waiting list; loneliness was lower in meal groups at 15 weeks, with delivery modality important. This supports one combined nutrition/connection clinical stream, not added separate loneliness utility or a local .02 QALY coefficient. The original falls-trial abstract covers 371 people: daily RR .83 (CI .55–1.25), weekly .96 (CI .63–1.45), so no established overall falls reduction is imported. Original HOMEFOOD full PDF studied 106 post-discharge at-risk adults with six-month individualized nutrition, home visits, calls and enriched food/supplements; endpoint EQ-5D difference .102 is not integrated QALYs or the effect of this local weekday meal program. Its endpoint-transfer sensitivity is explicitly hypothetical. Current local eligibility excludes an existing resident caregiver/family member except spouse and an authorized meal-preparation provider, constraining large generic caregiver-labor claims. Household or spouse resource changes are joint-netted; distinct external caregivers cannot be added without their own incidence ledger. Existing SNAP, family meals, delivery options and public nutrition are retained alternatives.
sections.cost: Initial $17.86M per better life is preserved, with 1.753991 clinical QALYs and 1.044375 signed resource equivalents. Applying full exposure burdens alone gives $36.59M; using native meal-density exposure to refine health and net-resource duration gives current $49.68M: health 0.911877, income 0.093974, total 1.005850 equivalent healthy years. Current full annual cost $4,996,818 versus this limited channel is not whole portfolio EV or demonstrated next-dollar impact. The .3 additionality, .4 clinical response and .02 utility remain judgments, not survey or trial coefficients. T and fraction of annual resource gains move from .75/1 to .741596/.741596 using 227,136/(1,178*260); averaging meals cannot establish equal duration or delivery contact, so trial-length 15-week and other finite sensitivities are explicit. Full .001 health harm and $30 one-off access/preparation/time cost apply to all 1,178 individual-consumption proxies, independent of b; benefit union remains 353.4 and resource-success group 176.7. Native seniors are unique people, not verified unique households: spouse and household mapping sensitivity remains. One welfare-equivalent adult allocation per recipient at $20,000 baseline prevents adding all family members. The $600 annual net-food-resource hypothesis means genuinely avoided grocery/care cash after SNAP, alternative family purchases, food replacement and benefit withdrawal—not retail meal price, medical savings or gross subsidy. Only .741596 year's amount is realized and positive overlap .5 removes duplicated nutrition welfare before full $30 cost; unsuccessful recipients retain costs. Medical savings and caregiver/work gains are unknown-neutral zero centrally, with positive and negative hypotheses tested, not assumed survivor salaries. All gains/costs within overlapping recipients use one log. Distinct public/private payer and volunteer losses are localized once and not discounted as positive overlap. Payer/provider incidence remains unknown; recipient-paid meal expense already in C is not charged twice. Transportation, congregate meals, other portfolio channels and paid-caregiver effects remain unknown, not zero. Clinical-null, financial-only, no-benefit with costs, true no-exposure/no-gift, adverse, low/high burden, negative gains, payer incidence and economic-cost scenarios remain finite/testable. A recognized home-delivery program-cost sensitivity uses $2,206,008 against the same meal-only benefits, giving $21.93M per better life. That boundary excludes allocated fundraising, overhead and volunteer resources; it is not full resource cost, whole portfolio EV or a verified marginal donation offer.
sections.funding: Latest original tax period October 2024–September 2025 (form tax label 2024): functional expense $4,626,696 plus netted direct event expense $370,122 gives $4,996,818. FYending 2024 $4,236,946+$526,825=$4,763,771; FYending 2023 $3,752,082+$198,150=$3,950,232. FY2025 home-delivery expense $2,206,008, transport $1,161,088 and congregate $469,223 explain why full cost exceeds this meal-only benefit channel; none is gross-summed again. Current $2,600 care solicitation and 100-day waitlist are not verified marginal price or funded capacity. Volunteers and external care opportunity costs remain unknown; $6.5M full-resource scenario is a judgment, not observed accounting. Fresh original source confirms EIN 23-7310650; official donor route was checked without a transaction. The program-aligned sensitivity quantifies the cost-boundary effect without attributing unknown transportation or congregate benefits to meals.

model.costScope: Whole annual recognized recipient cost versus conditional meal nutrition/check-in and netcash channel; otherprograms and externalcost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Montgomery County inHouston metro; full1.0 localshare once
model.formula: Exposed=N*unique; benefit union=exposed*b. Clinical=(clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse*q*finite discounted T − exposed*harm/onset discount)*g. Changed=union*success; one joint household log of positive-only overlap net food/medical/work/transfer resources*resourceYears minus full cost; other exposed retains full cost. Distinct payer loss localized once. Price=10*C/(health+signed resources).
model.counterfactual: Family/caregiver meals, SNAP/publicnutrition, grocerydelivery and paidmeal alternatives retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Unique recipient and full finance source-grounded; households, causal fraction, local utility and net cash unmeasured. Average meal-density is a duration proxy, not matched dosage. Trial evidence supports mechanisms and bounds, not automatic local coefficients. Other portfolio and current gift EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Unique oldermeal recipients, finite nutritional/connection utility and actual cashcosts avoided; notmeals,retailvalue or self-reportedcausality

what: Daya supports South Asian survivors of domestic and sexual violence in the Houston region.
It combines confidential crisis support, licensed counseling, housing assistance and economic empowerment.
Culturally specific advocacy and legal referrals help survivors pursue safety and practical stability.
strengths: Culturally specific advocacy addresses language and access barriers.
Freshly checked program counts support distinct counseling, housing and work-resource mechanisms.
Comparative primary evidence informs integrated safety scenarios without treating services as causal outcomes.
reservations: Service groups overlap and completed dose, households and local causal effects remain unobserved.
Current costs and newer outputs differ in vintage; monetary assistance is not net new income.
The limited modeled reference is nonpositive under retained burden priors; broader safety and whole portfolio remain uncertain.

sections.what: Daya supports South Asian survivors of domestic and sexual violence in the Houston region. It combines confidential crisis support, licensed counseling, housing assistance and economic empowerment. Culturally specific advocacy and legal referrals help survivors pursue safety and practical stability.
sections.monitoring: Freshly fetched and visually checked 2025 official report: 683 clients, 564 crisis/safety,75 counseling,75 housing,109 economic users; these overlap and are not distinct households or completed effective doses. County shares 63% Harris+20% Fort Bend+4% Brazoria/Galveston/Montgomery give .87 local share once; other Texas/out-of-state excluded. Assistance spending includes $110,000 housing, $28,000 legal, $12,000 transport and $47,000 essentials, not measured causal net resources. Request an overlap/dose ledger, local unique households, housing retention, symptom/utility follow-up, after-tax earnings and benefits lost, alternative services, exposure cost and retaliation/privacy outcomes.
sections.qualitative: The original 2023 JAMA DVHF study compared 219 housing-first and 125 usual-service participants in a weighted nonrandom analytic cohort of 344 over two years. Housing, safety and mental-health advantages support integrated mechanisms, but confounding, Washington setting and few Asian participants limit transfer. Symptom scales are not measured QALYs or Daya income. PATH's original 2018 randomized trial compared specialist psychological advocacy with usual advocacy; improved distress/depression at 12 months but no demonstrated further-abuse difference, with 64% retention. Dose 8 sessions plus 2 follow-ups is not Daya's unspecified counseling dose. These results motivate overlap-bounded counseling/housing and broad-safety scenarios, not assigning full DVHF to all 683 or summing depression, anxiety and housing utility. Current services include licensed therapy, practical assistance, job-search support and legal referral, not staff attorneys. Existing victim agencies, public aid, family and employer support remain alternatives. Culturally appropriate access may add value without proving universal response.
sections.cost: Initial $265.40 M is retained as the complete historical health-and-income diagnostic: health +0.076447 and income −0.003090. Burden-only correction gives combined −0.852807; additional native-program restriction gives current health −0.077592, income −1.134818, total −1.212410, so no finite positive current price. This is not a measured harm finding about Daya or its whole portfolio. Full FY 2024 annual $1,946,855 expense is matched conditionally to FY 2025 service outputs; unmodeled legal, safety, other housing and prevention benefits remain unknown, not zero. Clinical envelope 75 assumes maximum overlap of 75 counseling/75 housing; range 75–150 is tested, replacing rather than adding two utility streams. Retained .8 household mapping, .35 additionality, .35 clinical response, .05 utility for .5 year are judgments, not trial coefficients. Broader 564 safety/crisis utility replaces that stream; low-response and high-intensity hypotheses bound possibilities but none establish that every brief-contact user got a housing-first dose. Central gain groups are bounded to 109 economic and 75 housing users with 75 assumed overlap; .8*.35*.25 resource-response scale gives 5.25 joint resource-success and 2.38 work-only proxies, not successes on all 683. Net work $300 and assistance $500 after alternative aid, taxes and benefit withdrawals remain hypotheses; positive overlap .5 before joint log, then full $100 participation/safety/opportunity costs. Other exposed household proxies retain negative costs; clinical harm .0005 applies all 546.4 exposures even when b=0. These unmeasured burdens are decisive; weighted burden (109 intensive proxies at$100, remaining at$10) still has nonpositive combined reference. The $100 uniform prior is not an observed average for brief helpline users. Distinct transfer counterparties and provider losses are localized once, with full losses, no overlap haircut. No grants' face value, gross salary or ordinary survivor earnings is counted as new social income. Payer zero is unknown-neutral, not measured zero. No-exposure/no-gift, financial-only, clinical-null, adverse, alternative, finite duration, overlap and volunteer-cost regimes are explicit. Broad high-dose positive sensitivity remains a hypothesis rather than a favorable central chosen to rescue price. Work resources are after childcare, commute, taxes and benefit withdrawal; the separately modeled participation cost must exclude any work expense already deducted. The income model uses one welfare-equivalent adult per household at $20,000 baseline, not every family member.
sections.funding: FY 2024 $1,928,451 tax expenses plus $18,404 netted direct event cost gives $1,946,855. FY 2023 $1,694,184 plus $18,861 gives $1,713,045; FY 2022 $1,417,570 plus $16,537 gives $1,434,107. Schedule D reconciles expense totals without a populated additional donated-resource adjustment. This is not evidence that volunteer resources cost zero. Newer FY 2025 outputs versus FY 2024 cost are a conditional scope mismatch. Reserves do not demonstrate an expansion bottleneck. Fresh root verification of the FY 2024 original confirms the accepted full-cost numerator. Fresh 2025 output PDF has no matching audited FY 2025 expense or current marginal-gift bottleneck. Recipient assistance expense is already in C; separate payer-incidence scenarios represent displaced public/private alternatives, not adding the same recipient grant expense twice.

model.costScope: Full annual recipient expense versus overlap-bounded counseling/housing and restricted economic channels; other portfolio and next gift unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Reported 2025 county shares imply .87 Houston MSA; applied once
model.formula: Exposed=N*unique; union=exposed*b; clinical=(clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse*q*finite discounted T − full exposed*harm)*g. Work/assistance success partitions=program counts*unique*b*success with intersection once. One joint log per disjoint household partition of overlap-adjusted positive resources minus full costs; all other exposure retains costs. Distinct transfer payer loss local once. Price=10*C/(health+signed income) only if positive.
model.counterfactual: Other victim services, public benefits, legal aid, family support and employment alternatives retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Primary comparative evidence supports mechanisms, not local utility or net income coefficients. Household/program intersection and full exposure burdens unmeasured; no finite positive current conditional reference. Unmodeled channels and marginal-gift EV remain unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional integrated safety/mental-health, stable housing and net disposable work/assistance resources; output counts not causal outcomes.

sections.what: The Restoration Team repairs homes for vulnerable Houston homeowners. Volunteers and partners address disaster damage, unsafe structures and accessibility barriers. Its repair and recovery work helps families preserve a safe place to live.
sections.monitoring: Current applications are closed while the queue is served, with reopening anticipated January 2027. The homepage reports cumulative 565 families and 100,000 volunteer hours since 2017; older 275-family copy is inconsistent. The VEVOR story reports priority repairs for the 500th family but remaining work before return to occupancy. A goal of 100 families annually by 2028 is not current annual throughput. Request dated unique completed homes, hazards resolved, occupancy timing, actual cash savings and worker/material opportunity costs.
sections.qualitative: Current repair stories show concrete safety and accessibility work. Volunteers, congregations and material partners provide practical delivery capacity. Original latest returns and expense-side event costs identify a transparent annual denominator. Cumulative families and volunteer hours do not establish annual completions or causal health gains. Applications are currently closed; added gifts are not demonstrated to overcome project-capacity limits. Unrecognized volunteer and partner resources, alternative funding and household savings remain uncertain. Current official giving page and original return confirm The Restoration Team, EIN 83-2427982, Houston. Current giving route was checked without a transaction. Donated equipment and professional services must not be counted as both free inputs and household retail benefits.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $68.09 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 0.097278 clinical QALYs and 0.019262 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.001469 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $793,541. Annual 50 repair-household opportunities are a judgment, not an observed annual count. Full annual response .4 gives 20 exposed households after alternative contractors, insurance, disaster aid and partner replacement. The same union supplies clinical .3 meaningful safety/comfort response, .02 utility for one finite year, with full .001 safety harm per exposed household. This is an unsupported acute safety/comfort prior, not repair-trial calibration or mortality. Independent .5 resource success receives $600 net otherwise-paid repair, temporary displacement or care costs actually avoided, after maintenance and alternative support. Positive overlap .5 precedes full $100 one-time disruption, foregone time and process burden; successful households net $200 and others lose $100. No house value or retail repair-value multiplier enters resources. Union 20 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 6; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $25,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Outside volunteer labor, donated equipment and partner time are unknown economic resources centrally, not free. Larger annual-cost and explicit provider-incidence cases stress them. Insurance/public-budget replacement or displaced beneficiaries require matched payer incidence; existing recipient costs are not charged twice. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: FY2025 tax expenses $787,489 plus $6,052 netted direct event cost gives $793,541. FY2024 $1,019,204 plus $6,564 gives $1,025,768. FY2023 $889,875 has no populated event expense. Schedule D audited/donated expense reconciliation lines are unpopulated, not evidence of zero volunteer opportunity costs. Recognized whole recipient annual resources versus the narrow hypothetical repair channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal donor price.

model.costScope: Whole annual recognized recipient resources versus conditional repair safety and cash-resource channel; outside volunteer labor, other programs and next gift unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Houston repair delivery; judged .98 metro share applied once
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Insurance, public disaster aid, city repair programs, paid contractors, other nonprofits and family/partner work retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Completed safer and more accessible homes, finite safety/comfort improvement and actual net avoided household costs; not cumulative families, volunteer hours or retail repair value
