reports.priceScope: Initial $15.38M annual diagnostic retained for comparison; current signed conditional channel has no finite positive price. Not complete portfolio EV or a verified marginal gift offer.

what: Crisis Intervention of Houston provides free, anonymous crisis counseling through telephone and teen text services.
Trained volunteers listen, help callers stabilize emotionally and connect them with other support.
Its programs also include suicide-bereavement groups, education and community crisis response.
strengths: Current recipient-owned pages identify a concrete local hotline and trained volunteer service.
Primary caller studies support a plausible short-term distress mechanism without treating calls as lives saved.
The recalibration preserves health and signed resources and distinguishes exposure from benefit.
reservations: Historical contacts are not current unique households, and 988 support may substitute.
Counselor-training evidence does not identify CIH-versus-988 QALYs or net earnings.
Full exposure burdens make the short-duration reference nonpositive; other programs and unpaid resources remain unmeasured.

sections.what: Crisis Intervention of Houston provides free, anonymous crisis counseling through telephone and teen text services. Trained volunteers listen, help callers stabilize emotionally and connect them with other support. Its programs also include suicide-bereavement groups, education and community crisis response.
sections.monitoring: The FY2024 return explicitly dates 35,812 calls, texts and chats to FY2022–2023; the current site's 3M since 1970 is cumulative. Neither supplies a current annual unique household cohort. Request deduplicated adult/teen callers, repeat contact, residence, alternative 988 use, referral uptake, completed follow-up, validated distress/utility measures, privacy/escalation harms and incremental volunteer hours. The .2 adult-household mapping and .9 Houston share remain judgments.
sections.qualitative: Gould 2007 followed 380 of 1,085 selected adult suicidal callers, with nonrandom attrition and no untreated comparator; improvement cannot fix CIH's causal fraction or utility duration. Gould 2013 examined 1,507 calls from 1,410 callers at 17 centers and found better end-call outcomes with ASIST-trained counselors: this compares counseling approaches, not hotline versus no care. Its Wiley abstract was read, not blocked PMC full text. Gould 2025 interviewed 437 adults at 12 centers in 2020–2021; perceived benefit is not measured mortality or a randomized effect. These primary studies support a short-term distress mechanism, not local causal QALYs or income coefficients. Existing 988, providers and family assistance remain the baseline. Recipient identity and owned donation form are unchanged; donation checkout/payee and current volunteer capacity need confirmation.
sections.cost: The initial $15.38M per better life remains a historical diagnostic, with 0.106330 clinical QALYs and +0.012011 income equivalents. The corrected reference retains all initial coefficients but applies full $2 one-off incremental time/access burden and .00001 health harm to all 7,162.4 distinct household proxies, not only 1,074.36 benefit-attributed proxies. Health is 0.051554 QALYs and signed income −0.261883 equivalents, total −0.210329; no finite positive current price follows. This conditional partial-channel reference is not evidence that CIH's whole portfolio harms people. Whole annual $181,993 expense is divided by limited hotline benefits; bereavement, education, crisis response and mortality channels remain unknown, not zero. The .3 clinical response, .02 utility, .02-year duration (7.3 days), .15 additionality and .9 local share remain judgments. Original studies do not justify more favorable local coefficients, so no price was forced. Positive total would require about 20.54 days at unchanged utility and other inputs; 13.5-day follow-up sensitivity is still nonpositive, while hypothetical one-month benefit gives $12.10M. A follow-up date is not observed benefit duration. Zero incremental time cost gives $16.26M but is only an alternative-burden sensitivity. $2 is per deduplicated household proxy beyond substitute service burdens, not per contact; $10/proxy represents $2 on each of five contacts implied by .2 mapping. The 53.718 resource-success proxies receive $100 net usable work/referral resources after taxes, benefits and alternative providers; overlap .5 adjusts only positive components before one household log, then full $2 cost. Other exposed proxies lose $2. No survivor wages or free-service retail value are counted. Benefit failure retains exposure burdens and harms; no exposure is distinct. Distinct payer/provider loss is localized once. Negative gains and harms are never overlap-discounted. Payer zero and $500,000 volunteer-inclusive expense are unverified hypotheses. Clinical-null, adverse, strong 988 substitution, unknown, finite duration, incidence and volunteer-cost cases remain testable.
sections.funding: FY2024 original recognized tax expense $181,993; FY2023 $181,602; FY2022 $226,567, all twelve-month June fiscal years. No populated event, rental or inventory expense addback recovered. Schedule D requests returned HTTP 404 rather than evidence of zero donated services. Unrecognized volunteers and partner care remain unknown. Historical FY2022–2023 contacts paired with FY2024 cost are an explicit mismatch. Whole-recipient cost versus this narrow hotline hypothesis is not a complete portfolio EV or verified marginal offer. No new volunteer-inclusive economic resource total, matched current unique cohort or funded marginal expansion was established. The $500,000 economic-cost sensitivity is not an observed budget.

model.costScope: Whole recognized annual tax recipient expense versus narrow historical hotline channel; unpaid/partner resources unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Local Houston reference with .9 judged MSA share; callers and teens not verified local adult households
model.formula: Exposed=N*unique; benefit union=exposed*b. Clinical=(clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse*q*discounted finite T − exposed*harm/onset discount)*g. Changed=union*success; one joint household log of overlap-adjusted positive net resources minus full costs; other exposed households retain full negative costs. Payer loss localized once. Current price=10*C/(health+signed income) only when positive. Historical-alpha-central reproduces complete initial health and income.
model.counterfactual: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, other hotlines, 911 when appropriate, community mental health and family support retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Services and accounting cost source-grounded; N historical contacts, not current unique people. All deduplication, additionality, utility, duration, income response and burden coefficients remain judgments. Primary studies do not identify CIH's causal increment versus 988. Current total nonpositive; omitted portfolio channels and next-gift response unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional short-term stabilization and useful support linkage; contacts not deaths prevented

what: Fort Bend Women’s Center supports survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault in the Houston region.
Its services combine crisis response, shelter, longer-term housing, counseling and legal advocacy.
Practical support and life-skills programs help survivors work toward safety and self-sufficiency.
strengths: Original latest returns expose inventory and event costs rather than a cheap net-expense denominator.
Dated adult housing outputs provide a narrower reference than repeated calls or shelter nights.
Housing, childcare, counseling and employment support connect clinical recovery with household resources.
reservations: Housing outputs do not establish additional safe housing, causal trauma improvement or net earnings.
Adult-household deduplication, outside grants and the Rio Bend property boundary remain uncertain.
Market-value impact ratios and monthly demand increases cannot establish marginal donor returns.

sections.what: Fort Bend Women’s Center supports survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault in the Houston region. Its services combine crisis response, shelter, longer-term housing, counseling and legal advocacy. Practical support and life-skills programs help survivors work toward safety and self-sufficiency.
sections.monitoring: Original 2025 annual report image page 4 shows 526 housing/utility-assisted individuals: 199 adults and 327 children, alongside 422 sheltered survivors, 9,763 calls and 8,111 therapy sessions. These are not disjoint or completed causal outcomes. Only the 199 adult housing/utility-assistance reference is used; nights, children, therapy sessions and hours are not added. The first 183-adult 2024 model is frozen as a diagnostic. Current monthly demand 410 versus 267 is not annual unique throughput or a doubling. Request distinct adult households, assistance persistence, actual safe housing changes, completed trauma care, incremental earnings and safety/privacy incidence.
sections.qualitative: Original latest returns expose inventory and event costs rather than a cheap net-expense denominator. Dated adult housing outputs provide a narrower reference than repeated calls or shelter nights. Housing, childcare, counseling and employment support connect clinical recovery with household resources. Housing outputs do not establish additional safe housing, causal trauma improvement or net earnings. Adult-household deduplication, outside grants and the Rio Bend property boundary remain uncertain. Market-value impact ratios and monthly demand increases cannot establish marginal donor returns. Original latest Form 990 confirms EIN 76-0032451. Rio Bend property affiliate EIN 83-1388793 is distinct and not substituted as a cheaper services denominator. Recipient-owned donor route was checked without a transaction. Capital/property cash costs and partner resources require separate marginal analysis.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $128.63 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 1.067133 clinical QALYs and 0.148671 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.000777 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $15,639,175. Observed 2025 199 adults receiving housing/utility assistance are a limited reference, not confirmed newly housed or completed clinical beneficiaries. Judged .9 adult-household mapping times .35 additional annual response yields 62.685 exposed households. Clinical .3 meaningful safety/trauma improvement times .06 utility for one finite year is a weak hypothesis, not validated shelter efficacy or mortality. Full one-off .0005 privacy/safety harm applies to the entire exposed union. Independent .5 resource success receives $800 net incremental usable housing/essential resources after alternative aid and benefit withdrawal plus $400 net work resources after taxes, childcare, commute and displaced earnings. Positive components separately receive overlap .5 before full $200 moving, application, attendance and foregone-pay burden: successful households net $400; others lose $200. Union 62.684999999999995 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 18.8055; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $20,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Housing and donated goods are not automatically new net social resources. Matched payer/displaced-beneficiary stress applies only to truly additional budget or displacement, not identical recipient grants charged twice. Provider burden is independently stressed. Property-affiliate and volunteer opportunity resources are unknown centrally, and central payer/provider zero is not observed zero or complete world benefit. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: FY2025 original tax expense $12,537,293 plus $83,678 direct event cost and $3,018,204 netted inventory cost gives $15,639,175. FY2024 $11,224,046 plus $32,828 and $2,694,431 gives $13,951,305. FY2023 $10,895,549 plus $100,102 and $2,746,340 gives $13,741,991. The inventory resource cost is included once, not also credited at retail value to households. No populated expense-side donated addback recovered; this is not proof of zero outside resources. Full recognized annual services recipient versus current narrow adult housing/utility-assistance numerator has an explicit whole-recipient/partial-channel scope mismatch. The public $8–$10 community benefit ratio, retail counseling value and avoided rental subsidy valuation are not used as clinical or household consumption estimates.

model.costScope: Whole recognized annual services recipient resources versus narrow current adult housing/utility-assistance recovery channel; other portfolio and marginal gift unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Fort Bend County and Houston MSA support; .98 local share judged, not measured household residence
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Existing public grants, victim compensation, other shelter/housing/counseling providers, employment programs and family support retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional housing/utility security and trauma recovery plus usable net household resources; not shelter nights, market therapy value or gross wages

what: The Rose provides breast screening and diagnostic care through Houston-area centers and mobile units.
Its patient navigators help uninsured patients arrange cancer treatment and practical support.
Sponsored care, translation, transport and childcare assistance seek to reduce barriers from diagnosis through recovery.
strengths: Original return distinguishes unduplicated uninsured people and insured versus uninsured treatment navigations.
Primary controlled navigation evidence gives both positive and null alternative-provider regimes.
Current BCCS, transport and childcare mechanisms connect care access to signed household resources.
reservations: The conditional price combines full annual recipient cost with only a limited modeled uninsured channel.
Small positive health-plus-income denominator is sensitive to unmeasured utility, burden and partner cost.
Navigation counts and faster resolution are not proven stage-shift, survival or QALY gains.

Its patient navigators help uninsured patients arrange cancer treatment and practical support. Sponsored care, translation, transport and childcare assistance seek to reduce barriers from diagnosis through recovery.
sections.monitoring: Original FY 2025 return reports 8,571 individual unduplicated uninsured women and 187 patients navigated into treatment:177 uninsured and 10 insured. The visually checked FY 2025 annual report page 22 instead lists 178 uninsured cancers and 588 support patients, versus original return 177 uninsured cancers and 812 support; definitions differ and are not combined. Neither source establishes completed appropriate treatment, unique households or causal stage improvement. Repeated interactions, screening exams, biopsies and insured/mobile services are not added as disjoint beneficiaries. Mobile residence spans 62 counties; .8 Houstonshare is a retained judgment, not measured MSA residence. Request unique local household histories, usual-provider access, time-to-treatment, completed treatment, stage-specific clinical outcomes, false-positive/overdiagnosis effects, and net patient/caregiver cash/time burdens.
sections.qualitative: Original DenverRCT randomized 993 abnormal screens (628 breast) and found diagnostic-resolution effects varied by abnormality, with no significant breastBIRADS 4/5 improvement. Original LosAngelesRCT 1,708 women found no six-month overall resolution improvement (55% versus 56%). Original multisite PNRP showed no first 90 daybenefit and later 91–365 day improvements in resolution/treatment initiation, especially where usual care delayed; it does not measure local survival, utility orQALYs. These support positive and strong-alternative/null regimes, not empirical .25/.3 multipliers. Original 2024 CISNET screening decision analysis includes false positives, benign biopsies and overdiagnosis alongside lifetime screening benefits; serial screening against no screening cannot calibrate one annual local navigation cohort. No diagnosis count, apparent survival from earlier detection or time-to-treatment hazard ratio is directly converted into lives saved. The finite .2 utility/two-year trajectory remains judgment and its null/weak/strong sensitivities are visible.
sections.cost: Initial $42.02 M per better life (health 4.008925 plus signed income−.204127) is preserved exactly. Full exposure burdens alone, keeping 187 clinical subgroup, give $178.84 M. Mapping to observed 177 uninsured navigations gives current $238.29 M: health 3.300950 plus signed income−2.630090 =.670860 healthy-year equivalents. This is not evidence the whole portfolio became 5.7 times worse; it corrects exposure accounting and a subgroup boundary in a deliberately partial conditional reference. Full cost $15,986,247 includes insured imaging and other activities whose benefits are not estimated here. All-program recognized-cost sensitivity is $13,174,486 but remains broader than the modeled channel. A judged uninsured-patient-share allocation ($13,174,486*8,571/41,186) yields $40.87 M; this is not observed navigation cost, full resource cost or an eligible marginal offer. .95 individual-to-consumption mapping and .8 local share are judgments. Full exposure 8,142.45 proxies each retain $20 incremental access/time cost and .0001 one-off harm independent of b; judged changed union 2,035.6125, resource-success 203.56125, clinical trajectory 12.61125 are subsets not added cohorts. Only positive medical/work/practical aid receives .5 overlap reduction; negative amounts remain full and all recipient household amounts enter one log at $20,000 baseline. Net practical support$300 excludes displaced charity/family aid, benefit withdrawals and taxes; medical and caregiver earnings zero are unknown-neutral, not measured zero. No retail charity bill, gross salary or full lifetime survivor wages are income. External BCCS/partner treatment resources and aid transfers have distinct payer/provider incidence, localized once; $5,000 per incremental clinical trajectory stress is explicit judgment, not measured cost. Clinical-null, financial-only, failed-benefit b 0 with full negatives, actual no-exposure, adverse, weak-alternative, low/high burdens and payer loss cases remain separate. Whole portfolio EV and donor-funded additional capacity remain unknown.
sections.funding: FY 2025 original expense $15,866,042 plus $120,205 netted event cost gives $15,986,247. FY 2024 $16,471,873 plus $96,459 gives $16,568,332. FY 2023 $15,265,960 plus $81,601 gives $15,347,561. Expense-side Schedule D removed expenses are zero in these returns; no populated rental-expense addback recovered. Partner treatment and unrecognized volunteers remain unknown. Paid clinical revenue, BCCS and CPRIT grants are baseline funding, not proof of gift-driven expansion. Original return all-program expense $13,174,486 includes insured and uninsured medical work; no observed uninsured navigation budget allocation is established. Public and partner treatment opportunity costs are outside the recipient budget and central zero is unknown-neutral. Insured program revenue subsidizes care but does not prove donation responsiveness.

model.costScope: Full annual recipient expense against limited uninsured navigation/access hypothesis; all insured screening, other medical and education benefits unknown, not zero. Not whole portfolio EV or marginal gift.
model.geographicAttribution: Original uninsured women and navigation counts span recipient Southeast Texas services; mobile residence62counties. Houston .8 share is retained judgment, not observed MSA residence; .5 sensitivity.
model.formula: Exposed=N*unique; benefit union=N*unique*b. Clinical=clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse*q*discounted finite years minus all exposed harms; geography once. Resources are joint household logs, positive-only overlap, full exposed costs; distinct payer treatment/transfer costs localized once. Headline=10*C/(health+signed resource equivalents).
model.counterfactual: Existing insurance, BCCS, Harris Health, other screening/navigation providers and family support retained
model.attribution: The .25 additional response and .3 clinical-benefit response are explicit hypotheses against public/partner alternatives; original trials support variable navigation mechanisms, not local coefficients. No HR-to-QALY or diagnosis-to-survival shortcut.
model.uncertainty: Current cohort mapping improved from original return; utility, response, resources, public treatment opportunity costs, localshare and gift capacity remain unmeasured. Small positive conditional denominator is sensitive and not empirical portfolio EV.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional timely appropriate treatment/access, after false-positive and overdiagnosis harms; current187 nav includes177uninsured and10insured in original return, not187new uninsured lives saved.

sections.what: Houston Area Women’s Center provides confidential support to survivors of domestic and sexual violence in Houston. Its services include crisis response, supportive housing, counseling, advocacy and help navigating legal and social resources. Economic empowerment and practical family support aim to make safety and recovery sustainable.
sections.monitoring: Official 2025 reporting gives nearly 2,700 women, men and children counseled or advocated for, 913 women, children and families housed, 134 longer-term housing placements and 35,446 calls. They may overlap; calls, apartment capacity and nights are not added as unique beneficiaries. Request annual adult household deduplication, actual counseling dose, safe housing persistence, privacy incidents, net earnings and usable assistance versus alternative supports. A search result annual report for Family Service League in New Jersey was rejected as the wrong recipient.
sections.qualitative: Current official reporting distinguishes counseling, housing placements and repeated hotline contacts. Original returns and a consolidated audit make resource and affiliate boundaries inspectable. Financial coaching, housing advocacy and practical support provide a resource mechanism beyond free retail counseling. Nearly 2,700 counseling and advocacy clients include children and do not establish adult completed treatment. Incremental symptom utility, safety and disposable resource gains remain unsupported priors. Public assistance, partner services, capital expansion and marginal funding require further counterfactual work. Original Form 990 confirms EIN 74-2029166 and current recipient identity. Recipient-owned giving route was read without a donation transaction. The audit consolidates HAWC ESH LLC; no separate affiliate grants are double counted.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $42.23 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 3.545801 clinical QALYs and 0.281596 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.002368 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $16,163,406. Nearly 2,700 mixed counseling/advocacy clients supply only an approximate annual reference. Judged .6 adult-household mapping and .3 additional annual response give 486 exposed households. The clinical subgroup is within that union: .2 meaningful symptom/safety improvement times .08 utility for .5 finite year; this is not an RCT-calibrated recipient effect or assumed mortality gain. Full one-off .0005 clinical harm per exposed household represents a weak privacy/safety deterioration prior. Independent .25 resource success receives $600 net additional work resources after taxes, benefit withdrawal, childcare, commute and displaced earnings, plus $400 usable assistance after alternative funding; each positive component receives overlap .5 before subtracting full $100 attendance, privacy-related process and foregone-pay burden. Successful households net $400; others lose $100. Union 486 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 97.2; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $20,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Assistance can transfer resources from taxpayers or displaced recipients rather than create social income. A distinct payer stress prices additional budget/displacement, not the same donation cost again. Provider stress covers genuinely external opportunity resources only. Central external incidence zero is unknown-neutral. Housing and child benefits outside this narrow adult household channel remain unknown, including associated burdens. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: Original FY2024 tax expense $16,076,053 plus $28,035 donated services removed from expense reconciliation and $59,318 netted event cost gives $16,163,406. FY2023 $14,814,054 plus $67,723 donated services and $54,181 event cost gives $14,935,958. FY2022 $17,276,637 plus $165,995 donated services and $30,242 event cost gives $17,472,874. The 2024 consolidated audit reports $16,116,236 including event cost, a different entity/reconciliation scope; tax-based full recognized recipient cost is used consistently, not that audit total plus intercompany costs. Current 2025 activity is paired with latest read 2024 original cost, explicitly a timing mismatch. Capital assets are not treated as a repeated annual expense. A later audit index lead was not used as verified current expense.

model.costScope: Full recognized recipient annual cost versus limited adult counseling/economic-support channel; capital and other portfolio outcomes/marginal gift unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Houston-area adult households; .98 local share judged, not verified patient residence
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Existing public victim compensation, shelter/counseling providers, housing grants, community employment support and family help retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional safety and reduced trauma burden plus usable household work/assistance resources, not hotline calls or housing nights

what: Avenue 360 provides primary, dental, behavioral and HIV healthcare across Houston-area clinics.
Its HIV services combine rapid treatment linkage, medication support, PrEP and case management.
Housing assistance and supportive services seek to reduce barriers to continuing care and stable daily life.
strengths: Original returns distinguish the healthcare recipient from a related zero-expense affiliate.
HIV treatment, housing and transportation barriers provide concrete connected mechanisms.
Historical original housing payments identify a resource channel rather than merely retail medical value.

sections.what: Avenue 360 provides primary, dental, behavioral and HIV healthcare across Houston-area clinics. Its HIV services combine rapid treatment linkage, medication support, PrEP and case management. Housing assistance and supportive services seek to reduce barriers to continuing care and stable daily life.
sections.monitoring: Original 2023 reports 13,232 unduplicated healthcare individuals and 41,870 visits, plus housing assistance for 521 clients and others in their households. These groups may overlap and are not added. Current 2024 return describes HIV/intensive case management and CoC/HOPWA housing but no recovered numerical current housing cohort. Request current distinct households, additional stable housing, ART retention, utility follow-up and actual payment/disruption incidence. Public housing and insurance alternatives are baseline.
sections.qualitative: Original returns distinguish the healthcare recipient from a related zero-expense affiliate. HIV treatment, housing and transportation barriers provide concrete connected mechanisms. Historical original housing payments identify a resource channel rather than merely retail medical value. Current unique housing and completed HIV treatment cohorts are not verified. Clinical utility and additional net housing resources are unsupported local priors. Public housing grants, insurance and other HIV providers complicate additionality and marginal funding. Original HACS EIN 76-0549240 doing business as Avenue 360 matches the historical recipient-owned 990. BeringOmega EIN 76-0589592 is a related recipient, not zero cost for this clinical operation. Donation route checked, not transaction/payee restrictions.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $231.36 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 0.982612 clinical QALYs and 0.482176 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.000432 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $33,889,527. Historical 521 housing clients are a reference proxy, not current independent households: judged .8 mapping ×.25 additional annual implementation. Clinical .25 improvement ×.04 utility ×1 finite year is a weak HIV-care/housing morbidity hypothesis, not ART trial calibration, PrEP infection-count conversion or mortality credit. Independent .5 resource success with $1,000 net additional housing resources after tax/benefit offsets and alternative assistance uses positive overlap .5 minus full $100 one-off application, move, travel or foregone-pay burden. Successful households net $400; others lose $100. Union 104.2 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 26.05; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $15,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Housing payments are transfers, not new production. Full matched counterparty incidence is stressed separately; annual grants already included in recipient cost are not charged a second time as identical provider expense. Separate taxpayer/displaced-beneficiary loss applies only to truly additional budget/displacement, unknown centrally. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: FY 2024 recognized tax expense $33,889,527;FY 2023$34,952,120;FY 2022$40,128,430. No populated event/rental/inventory addback recovered, and current ScheduleD expenses removed 0; unrecognized volunteers or partner resources are not provenzero. FY 2023 housing payments $4,608,711 for 521 clients/othersHH are historical gross transfers, not net current consumption gain. Current whole-recipient cost and historical proxy mismatch is explicit. Other clinical, prevention, hospice and housing outcomes remain unknown.

Income-based fees, public insurance acceptance and multidisciplinary care aim to make continuing treatment accessible.

reservations: Clinical quality recognition does not establish additional health effects or household savings.

sections.what: Vecino Health Centers provides medical, dental and counseling services in northeast Houston. Its Denver Harbor family center and Airline children’s and women’s center serve insured and uninsured families in English and Spanish. Income-based fees, public insurance acceptance and multidisciplinary care aim to make continuing treatment accessible.
sections.monitoring: Original FY2024 reports 11,453 medical patients and 29,099 encounters, including children. The 1,070 behavioral clients and 330 dental patients may overlap and are not added. Request unique adult households, clinical completion, measured patient utility, actual incremental payments and partner resources. HRSA quality awards indicate clinical process performance, not causal donation-funded QALYs. Both Houston locations accept Medicaid, CHIP, Medicare and private insurance; alternatives and reimbursement are part of the baseline.
sections.qualitative: Original recipient returns distinguish medical patients from encounters and overlapping service groups. The official donor page and original return agree on the healthcare recipient EIN. Current locations and insurance/sliding-fee arrangements make service access and counterfactuals inspectable. Clinical quality recognition does not establish additional health effects or household savings. Adult household mapping, response, utility and net resources remain unsupported local priors. Public reimbursements, partner clinical resources and a property affiliate complicate marginal funding and full resource scope. Official donor EIN 76-0622208 matches Houston Community Health Centers Inc; facility affiliate 82-5421842 is not the donation healthcare recipient. Denver Harbor is a Houston neighborhood, not Colorado. Recipient-owned giving route is verified, not checkout or marginal capacity.
sections.cost: The conditional annual limited-channel reference is $47.32 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 2.673913 clinical QALYs plus -0.335658 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.002113 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not verified next-gift response. Whole-parent recognized annual resources are $11,065,389. Observed 11,453 medical patients × judged .6 adult-household mapping × .2 additional annual response yields 1,374.36 household proxies; .6 is not an observed unique adult count or extra clinical success rate. The clinical subset of 274.872 receives judged .02 utility for .5 finite years, not a process award-to-QALY conversion. Independent resource success .2 with hypothetical $200 actual otherwise-paid expenses avoided after alternative providers, taxes and benefits uses positive overlap .5 minus full $30 one-off travel, childcare, foregone-pay or copay burden. Success households net $70; others lose full $30. One welfare-equivalent adult per household, $20,000 annual consumption and one joint log. No retail medications, gross salary or ordinary survivor wages. Clinical failure retains resources and burdens; union harms are full and positive-only overlap never discounts negative resources. ResourceYears means realized fraction of one year’s gain, not perpetual savings. Provider/property opportunity costs are distinct from participant costs; central external zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero. Whole-parent expense versus narrow adult channel is not complete portfolio or marginal-donation EV.
sections.funding: FY2024 parent tax expense $10,482,273 plus Schedule D excluded donated resources $583,116 = $11,065,389; FY2023 $10,613,110 + $700,118 = $11,313,228; FY2022 $11,696,526 + $702,798 = $12,399,324. This is a consistent parent recognized-expense plus donated-resource basis. FY2022 audit reconciliation also identifies property-affiliate expense $546,553 less intercompany rent $140,548 and asset-disposal loss $4,836; these are not blindly added again. Bad debt $992,399 is in tax expense; it is not recipient household loss or provided-care retail benefit. Affiliate consolidated economic scope and partner opportunity costs remain unknown/stressed. FY2024 program service revenue $6,407,003 underscores insurance reimbursement rather than pure donation-supported access.

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient recognized resources; limited clinical/resource numerator; marginal additional cost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Both healthcare centers are in Houston; .98 local patient share is an explicit judgment, not measured county distribution.
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Medicaid, CHIP, Medicare, private insurance, other FQHC/charity care, sliding fees and partner-supported treatment remain baseline; only additional annual appropriate care and actual net resources count.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded cost and service description; numerical clinical and disposable-resource effects are unsupported conditional hypotheses. Complete total EV remains unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Medical patients, additional appropriate completed care and finite adult symptom relief; encounters and overlapping dental/behavioral groups are not additional people.

what: AccessHealth provides primary, dental, behavioral and other healthcare services to low-income families in Fort Bend and Waller counties.
Its integrated clinics also offer pharmacy, nutrition, HIV and hepatitis care, with insurance acceptance and income-based fees.
The organization connects patients with continuing treatment and assistance rather than relying only on episodic medical visits.
strengths: Current primary services identify insurance, sliding fees and medication-access mechanisms.
Three original annual returns verify recipient identity and current recognized cost.
Original service counts distinguish encounters and nutrition recipients rather than claiming all contacts are unique treatment completions.
reservations: Repeated visits, household duplication and clinical treatment completion are not verified.
The modeled adult utility and actual net household resource effects are unsupported priors.
Whole-recipient cost includes additional services and geography beyond this narrow adult medical channel.

sections.what: AccessHealth provides primary, dental, behavioral and other healthcare services to low-income families in Fort Bend and Waller counties. Its integrated clinics also offer pharmacy, nutrition, HIV and hepatitis care, with insurance acceptance and income-based fees. The organization connects patients with continuing treatment and assistance rather than relying only on episodic medical visits.
sections.monitoring: FY2025 original reports 51,493 medical encounters, 6,670 dental encounters, 8,146 behavioral encounters and additional nutrition/optometry contacts. These are not unique patients and are not added into one cohort. WIC recipients across five counties are not extra independent Houston clinical or cash beneficiaries. Request medical visit-to-unique-adult and household ratios, completed dose, clinical utility follow-up, actual household net payments and alternative-care use. Current Medicaid/Medicare/private insurance, sliding fees and 340B arrangements form the reimbursement counterfactual.
sections.qualitative: Current primary services identify insurance, sliding fees and medication-access mechanisms. Three original annual returns verify recipient identity and current recognized cost. Original service counts distinguish encounters and nutrition recipients rather than claiming all contacts are unique treatment completions. Repeated visits, household duplication and clinical treatment completion are not verified. The modeled adult utility and actual net household resource effects are unsupported priors. Whole-recipient cost includes additional services and geography beyond this narrow adult medical channel. Original EIN 74-1951476 matches the AccessHealth recipient. Fort Bend and Waller clinical target is within the Houston MSA; service locations do not prove all patients reside there. Recipient-owned giving route is checked, not a transaction, funding restriction or donation-sensitive expansion.
sections.cost: The conditional limited-channel annual reference is $125.74 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 2.913491 clinical QALYs plus -0.365733 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.000795 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not verified next-gift response. Full recognized annual current expense is $32,035,425. Observed 51,493 encounters × judged .15 adult household opportunities per encounter × .2 additional annual response gives 1,544.79 exposed household proxies. The .15 mapping explicitly combines .25 distinct medical episodes per encounter with .6 adult-household share, neither observed. The clinical subset of 308.958 adults receives judged .02 utility for .5 finite years; this is not a trial-calibrated effect or visit-to-health conversion. Independent resource success .2 with hypothetical $200 actual otherwise-paid care expense avoided after alternative provider, taxes and benefits uses positive overlap .5 minus full $30 one-off copay, travel, childcare or foregone-pay burden. Success households net $70 and other exposed households lose full $30. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $20,000 annual consumption is modeled with a single joint log. Retail 340B medicine value, gross wages and ordinary survivor earnings are excluded. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens; positive-only overlap preserves full negative resources and union harms. ResourceYears means fraction of one year's gains, not repeated lifetime savings. Partner/payer opportunity costs are distinct from participant burdens; central external zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Whole expense versus narrow adult medical numerator leaves other portfolio benefits, burdens and marginal financing unknown.
sections.funding: Current fiscal year ends June 30, 2025. Original recognized current expenses are FY2025 $32,035,425, FY2024 $30,581,547 and FY2023 $27,842,283. FY2025 Schedule D audited expense $32,061,430 less $26,005 PRIOR YEAR ADJUSTMENT reconciles to $32,035,425; this is not an omitted donated-service expense or new current service cost. No populated netted event/rental/inventory or excluded donated-service fields were recovered; unrecognized volunteer/partner resources remain unknown, not factual zero. Reimbursements, public grants, 340B and WIC funding are baseline mechanisms; donations are not assumed to create all existing services.

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient recognized resources; limited clinical/resource numerator; marginal additional cost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Narrow Fort Bend/Waller adult medical channel inside Houston MSA; .95 local share is judgment, not inferred from five-county WIC coverage.
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Insurance, Medicaid/Medicare, other FQHC and public/charity treatment, sliding fees, 340B access and partner funding remain baseline; only incremental annual care and net household resources count.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded cost and service description; numerical clinical and disposable-resource effects are unsupported conditional hypotheses. Complete total EV remains unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Medical encounters mapped by explicit weak priors to unique adult household opportunities; additional appropriate treatment and finite symptom relief, not visits as QALYs.

sections.what: Christ Clinic provides primary, preventive and specialty care to uninsured and underinsured people in the Katy area. Its Total Care program combines chronic disease care, medication assistance, laboratory services and limited behavioral health treatment. Express Care, employer memberships and the church-linked 2535 initiative provide additional routes to accessible care.
sections.monitoring: Current primary sources describe services, not unique annual completions or causal improvements. Request unique adults and households, repeated visits, clinical follow-up, medication adherence, alternative care use and recipient-specific net household expenses. Verify membership revenue, current partner capacity and whether new donations expand appropriate care rather than replace public or employer funding.
sections.qualitative: Current eligibility and service descriptions are specific about low-income access. Three original annual returns support a consistent recognized-expense series and verified recipient identity. Medication assistance and multidisciplinary care offer plausible health and household resource mechanisms. No current unique completed treatment cohort or causal outcomes were verified. All numerical health and resource response parameters are unsupported local priors. Unrecognized donated clinical resources and marginal funding capacity remain unresolved. Original FY2024 EIN 90-0789318 and Katy address identify the recipient. Official donation route is checked, not a transaction or restriction. The 2535 initiative is part of this recipient, not a separate benefit added to the cohort.
sections.cost: The conditional limited-channel reference is $19.27 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents, with 0.933873 clinical QALYs and -0.039834 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.005189 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not verified next-gift response. Annual recognized recipient cost is $1,723,027. The 1,000 annual patient opportunities are a judgment; .8 distinct household share and .4 counterfactual annual response yield 320 household proxies, including 64 judged clinical improvers. Utility .03 for .5 years is a weak morbidity hypothesis, not an empirical average or cardiovascular/mortality conversion. Resource success .3 is independent of clinical success. $300 otherwise-paid care avoided is a hypothetical actual payment avoided after alternative-provider substitution, not retail care value; positive overlap .5 and full $50 incremental travel, work disruption or contribution burden give success households $100 net and other households −$50. A single joint household log uses $20,000 annual consumption and one welfare-equivalent adult per household. Gross wages, ordinary survivor earnings and retail medication value are excluded. Positive components alone receive overlap reduction; negative resources and all union harms remain full. ResourceYears is a fraction of one year's gain, not recurrent lifetime savings. Provider/payer costs are separate from participant costs; central external zero is unknown-neutral, not evidence of zero or complete world net benefit. Whole annual recipient cost supports a narrow conditional numerator; complete portfolio and marginal funding EV remain unknown.
sections.funding: Original recognized expenses are FY2024 $1,723,027, FY2023 $2,297,861 and FY2022 $1,912,440. No populated netted event, inventory or rental expense field was recovered in these originals; this is not a claim that unrecognized donated professional resources cost nothing. FY2024 program service revenue $482,099 indicates patient/employer payment mechanisms alongside donations. All recognized expense is retained; additional partner opportunity costs are separately stressed. No arbitrary match is applied to the full denominator or annual numerator.

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient recognized resources; limited clinical/resource numerator; marginal additional cost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Katy delivery is within the Houston MSA; .98 patient share is a judgment, not measured county distribution.
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Alternative charity clinics, FQHC/public care, insurance eligibility, household payments and employer funding replacement; additional annual care response remains a prior.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded cost and service description; numerical clinical and disposable-resource effects are unsupported conditional hypotheses. Complete total EV remains unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional appropriate care and finite symptom relief in a judged annual patient cohort; visits and medicine retail values are not outcomes.

Full recognized annual resources $4,169,236 are divided by a judged 150 annual household opportunities × .4 additional implementation = 60 household proxies. One welfare-equivalent adult per household is modeled; clinical subgroup 15 is within the resource union, avoiding additional population inflation. .01 clinical utility for one finite year is a weak symptom/heat-exposure hypothesis, not a trial-derived injury, mortality or home-life conversion. Independent resource success .5 with $1,000 actual otherwise-paid repair, relocation or care expense avoided is a judgment after alternative public repairs, assistance, taxes and substitution; it is not donated repair retail value, capital asset appreciation or property wealth. Positive overlap .5 minus full $100 one-off disruption, increased energy, maintenance or foregone-work burden gives successes $400 net, other exposed households −$100. The same household components are netted before a single log at $20,000 annual consumption; negative gains and all costs remain full. ResourceYears is fraction of one year's gains, not repeated repair spending. Clinical failure retains household resources and burdens; union harms are retained independently. Provider/contractor opportunity costs are distinct from household disruption. Matched counterparty/provider scenarios are explicit stresses; central unknown-neutral zero does not claim complete world net benefit. Whole recipient annual denominator versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio or marginal gift EV.
sections.funding: Full recognized resource cost is FY2024 $4,013,888 tax expense + $155,348 donated services = $4,169,236; FY2023 $3,575,146 + $109,150 = $3,684,296; FY2022 $3,809,994 + $343,901 donated services + $31,576 direct event expense = $4,185,471. Schedule D donations are added once because excluded from tax expense. Recognized materials and labor already included are not added again. Rental revenue is not a gain or a cost. Root checked the original alternate LessRentalExpensesGrp/RealAmt field: netted rental expenses are reported as $0 in 2024, 2023 and 2022; no rental addback is needed. City construction contracts and grants are counterfactual capacity, not automatic donation credit. Current cost, unrecognized volunteer labor and marginal project capacity require due diligence.

sections.what: San Jose Clinic provides medical, dental, pharmacy, vision and behavioral care to low-income uninsured patients. It operates in Houston and Fort Bend, with eligibility screening and patient financial contributions. Its multidisciplinary services seek to improve access to treatment for people who cannot obtain conventional insured care.
sections.monitoring: The 2025 report shows 4,893 patients and 38,108 appointments. Four confirmed MSA counties account for 4,691 patients; Wharton is excluded. These figures do not demonstrate causal health improvement. Request unique annual households, treatment completion, health outcomes, current audited expenses and alternative-care use.
sections.qualitative: The current annual report identifies 4,893 patients rather than only appointment volume. Original audited statements identify recognized donated medicines and professional resources. The Houston and Fort Bend delivery locations and uninsured eligibility are clear. No current audited expense was recovered; the center transfers a 2022 full-cost denominator to the 2025 patient cohort. Clinical response, household duplication and resource savings are unmeasured hypotheses. Existing charity providers, donated-resource capacity and next-gift additionality remain unresolved. No external trial is used to assert local effect size. Public funding and alternative providers may replace donation-funded care; this requires direct verification.
sections.cost: The conditional reference is $64.94 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 4.470204 clinical QALYs plus -2.056082 income equivalents. Full annual recognized cost is $15,677,822; $10,000 corresponds to 0.001540 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not a demonstrated gift response. The exposed union is 1565.760 household proxies and the clinical subgroup is 313.152 adults. Clinical benefit is union × completion × utility × discounted finite years × geography. Financial successes and other exposed households are disjoint; each has one joint net log. Positive components receive the overlap adjustment before adding full negative components and subtracting full burdens. The resource success share is independent of clinical efficacy, so clinical null retains all resources and costs. Baseline consumption is positive even if reported income is zero. Gains are hypothetical otherwise-paid care or disposable resources after taxes, benefit withdrawal, new work expenses and substitution—not retail care values, gross salary or ordinary survivor earnings. One-off participation costs are incremental versus alternative care. Payer stress models distinct counterparty households; central external zero is an unknown-neutral partial-boundary reference, not observed zero or complete world benefit. Unrecognized partner/volunteer costs, broader portfolio benefits and harms, family spillovers and marginal funding response remain unknown.
sections.funding: Original FY2022 expense $15,481,097 plus $196,725 netted donor benefits gives $15,677,822. FY2021 $10,727,257 plus $43,900 gives $10,771,157. FY2020 recognized expense is $10,936,299, but direct-benefit reconciliation remains unverified, so it is not certified comparable. Donated pharmaceuticals, professional services and facility amortization already in the audits are not added again. The current annual report’s $17,185,078 panel is revenue, not expense. Audit opinion dates are not asserted publication dates. Current full costs and marginal capacity are due-diligence blockers. The historical three-year size comparison uses the consistent audited expense series before separate netted donor-benefit addbacks: 2020 $10,936,299, 2021 $10,727,257 and 2022 $15,481,097 (average $12,381,551). This is not an estimate of current 2025 expenses or the full-resource denominator used above.

reports.program: Women’s recovery treatment and support
reports.priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: Santa Maria Hostel provides residential and outpatient substance use treatment for women, including pregnant and parenting women.
Its Houston programs combine counseling, recovery support, childcare, housing assistance and career development.
The deep review uses reported treatment/support activity as a conditional envelope and includes signed health and net household resources.
strengths: Current services address childcare and housing barriers alongside substance use treatment.
The new 2025 impact report separates treatment/support, prevention and unique clinic patients.
Local MIRRORS follow-up and randomized external case-management evidence support recovery and work mechanisms without supplying causal Houston utility or dollar earnings.
reservations: The 1,404 treatment/detox/support women are not verified unique completed treatments, and post-closure throughput remains unknown.
Recovery utility and net earnings effects are unsupported local priors, not measured causal effects.
Whole-recipient costs include prevention, family services and Austin, while this numerator covers a narrow Houston women’s channel.

sections.what: Santa Maria Hostel provides residential and outpatient substance use treatment for women, including pregnant and parenting women. Its Houston programs combine counseling, recovery support, childcare, housing assistance and career development. The deep review uses reported treatment/support activity as a conditional envelope and includes signed health and net household resources.
sections.monitoring: The September 2026 download is titled 2025 Annual Report and records 1,404 women receiving treatment, detox and supportive services, not unique completed care. Its 12,099 mixed family total and 599 unique I-Care patients are different populations, not added beneficiaries. The June 2025 notice projects residential/outpatient capacity at 60% after closures; other programs and Austin continue. Request dated unique completed treatment episodes and unique women, relapse and health outcomes, retained disposable earnings, current Houston share and a post-closure budget.
sections.qualitative: Local MIRRORS research follows 215 pregnant/postpartum women from intake to discharge and six months post-intake, without an untreated control. Improvements are descriptive rather than incremental causal recovery or earnings. A randomized New Jersey TANF intensive-case-management trial supports abstinence and work mechanisms versus screening/referral, but differs from Santa Maria residential care and measures neither Houston QALYs nor net dollar earnings. Current services combine childcare and career support; intensive curricula occupy 30 hours/week, supportive groups at least 10 hours/week. Foregone time, taxes, withdrawn benefits, travel and childcare may offset gains. No retail service values, maternal mortality or ordinary survivor earnings are automatically counted.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $54.45M per better life: 4.633930 health QALYs and -1.570142 signed income equivalents. The original $110.99M becomes $178.37M when only all-exposure burden accounting is corrected at the original 300-person cohort; using the reported 2025 category envelope then gives $54.45M. These are scope/accounting revisions, not measured improvement in whole-portfolio effectiveness. Full recognized FY2025 cost remains $16,681,490. N=1,404 is the reported mixed treatment/detox/support category, unique=.7 a household-mapping judgment, giving 982.8 exposed proxies. Additionality .4 and clinical completion .5 yield 196.56 responders. Original .05 utility for half a year, quarter-year delay and Houston share .95 remain judgments, especially given 15 counties and Austin. A .6 capacity-flow sensitivity is a hypothesis, not a blanket observed multiplier. A quarter of incremental households receives $1,000 one-year disposable resources after taxes, benefit withdrawal and recurring work costs; positive components alone receive .5 overlap. Each exposed household incurs full $100 access burden even without additional recovery. One joint household log uses $15,000 positive baseline consumption; clinical null retains financial exposures and burden. Central zero harm and external losses are unknown-neutral placeholders, tested with full negative harm, lost-work/opportunity cost, payer/provider losses and displaced-worker stresses. Public payer incidence allocates Houston recipients once then uses payer edition share one. No additionality differs from no exposure. Full annual cost against only this finite Houston treatment channel omits unmeasured prevention, clinic, children, Austin and other benefits rather than assuming zero; it is not portfolio EV or verified next-gift capacity.
sections.funding: Gross recognized expenses are FY2025 $16,681,490, FY2024 $15,639,260 and FY2023 $13,307,636, including direct event costs netted from revenue. Schedule D removed expense amounts match these event addbacks; no additional donated-service amount is identified. The series covers the entire recipient, not only Houston residential care. The organization announced a $15 million five-year public funding reduction; this does not prove a particular donation restores a bed or replaces that funding dollar-for-dollar. Current fundraising does not establish a donation restores a particular bed; the five-year funding loss is not an annual expense or a verified replacement ratio. Financial originals were reviewed in the accepted October 5 audit; fresh October 6 IRS retrieval was blocked, so these figures are reused, not claimed newly reverified.

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient recognized resources; limited clinical/resource numerator; marginal additional cost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: The 2025 reported treatment/detox/support envelope spans 15 Texas counties and the whole recipient. Houston share .95 is a retained judgment, not an observed Houston-only cohort; Austin and other non-MSA participants remain uncertain and geography sensitivity applies.
model.formula: exposed=N*unique; incremental=exposed*b; clinical=incremental*completion; health=(clinical*q*discounted finite years - exposed*harm)*g; successes=incremental*success; disjoint household joint signed logs with full exposed costs; locally allocated distinct payer losses once; price=10*C/(health+income equivalent)
model.counterfactual: Alternative charity/public care, recovery supports, insurance eligibility, household behavior and funding replacement; additional response remains a prior.
model.attribution: Benefit additionality is separate from full service exposure burden; current capacity flow is a sensitivity, not observed annual outcomes.
model.uncertainty: Unique households, Houston share, causal utility, completion, persistence, disposable resources, harms, payer losses and marginal capacity remain unresolved hypotheses.
model.nativeOutcomes: 2025 report: 1,404 women receiving treatment/detox/support, not unique completed care. Mixed continuum and clinic populations kept separate.

reports.program: Food access, social services and mental wellness

what: Nourishing Hope provides food, social services and mental wellness support to Chicago residents.
Its counselors offer intake and ongoing care, while case managers help with benefits, transit, housing and employment resources.
Food distribution and individual support address several connected barriers to household stability.
strengths: Current licensed clinical and case-management services establish a plausible mechanism.
Food and benefits access can improve usable household resources.
Multiple access routes serve residents facing practical barriers.
reservations: Food pounds and neighbors served are not additional therapy cohorts or causal outcomes.
Net food substitution, benefit access and clinical effectiveness are unmeasured here.
Whole annual costs and donated food do not establish marginal gift productivity.

sections.what: Nourishing Hope, EIN 36-2734184, operates food markets, delivery, social services and mental wellness in Chicago. Counseling is available to Chicago residents aged 14 or older after intake; alternative referrals and ongoing coordination are offered. Social services include benefits applications, transit, grant eligibility, housing and job-search support. The official donation route is current; no checkout transaction was tested.
sections.monitoring: The organization reports over six million food pounds and 50,000 neighbors in 2025. These are delivery measures, not unique additional therapy participants or avoided illness. Track unique households, additional usable food resources net of substitution, actual benefit receipt, session completion, clinical outcomes and process burdens. Existing SNAP, Medicaid, other food banks and public clinics remain alternatives. Food-service use is not required for social services.
sections.qualitative: A Cochrane review of primary-care counseling found modest short-term mental health advantages over usual GP care, but not long-term superiority or overall healthcare cost reductions. The evidence is dated and from different settings; it does not identify local treatment fidelity, adolescent effects or QALYs. The model's .04 utility increment for six months is a weak separate judgment. No mortality, ordinary survivor earnings or additional food-related clinical benefit is stacked on the same people.
sections.cost:
Original April–March annual recognized expense plus direct event expense gives FY2025 $20,399,467, FY2024 $19,122,654 and FY2023 $16,917,206; mean $18,813,109. Schedule D identifies no additional donated-service expense requiring a second addback. FY2024 reconciliation's $308,941 matches event cost and is counted once. Noncash contributions of $11,222,804, $10,791,364 and $8,878,798 are not automatically another expense added to already recognized food resources. Unrecognized volunteer opportunity costs remain unknown.

A judged 1,000 local household opportunities and .5 additional annual-work response expose 500 households. A .1 clinical share and .5 completion yield 25 clinical residents within the same union. Judged .04 utility for six months, quarter-year delay and 3% discount yield .496319 clinical QALYs. This is a narrow conditional bundled-services channel with the whole annual denominator, not complete portfolio EV or measured marginal-gift productivity.

Two hundred households conditionally gain $300 usable food purchasing resources and $600 benefits in one year, already net of alternative food, substitution, taxes, benefit withdrawal and replacement support. These are actual incremental resource hypotheses, not pounds times retail price or gross salary. Each positive component retains .5 for health overlap; full negatives remain. Full $75 process time/transport burden leaves $375. Three hundred other households lose $75. One welfare-equivalent person per household, $20,000 annual resources and one joint log yield 1.284554 equivalents. Additional family welfare is unpriced. Combined 1.780872 gives $114.547608 million per ten combined equivalents, not ten clinical QALYs.

Clinical failure preserves resource exposure and costs. Full-union harm, negative resources, payer loss and external care burdens are stresses. Public transfers and donated food need counterparty accounting; matched payer incidence is separate, not attenuated by recipient overlap. Central payer and external costs are unknown-neutral references, not factual zero or complete-world benefit.
sections.funding: Original government grants were $1,069,603, $1,018,888 and $406,011. Public benefits eligibility and food alternatives continue without this recipient. The .5 response judges additional annual funded work while retaining full annual expense; b=1 shows full response. Actual unmet expansion, alternative funding, food supply replacement and marginal donor response remain unknown.

model.formula: exposed=N*b; clinical=exposed*clinicalShare*completion; Q=clinical*q*discounted finite years−full union harm. Positive-only overlap per signed food/benefit component, then joint household log once. Price=10*C/(health+resources).

reports.program: Older adult home modification and housing stability

what: North West Housing Partnership helps suburban Chicago homeowners repair homes and navigate housing decisions.
Its older adult program combines occupational therapy, nursing and contractor-installed safety modifications.
Accessible homes can help older residents manage daily activities and remain independent.
strengths: A current local program addresses concrete accessibility barriers.
Randomized CAPABLE evidence supports a short-term functional mechanism in some populations.
Home changes can plausibly protect household resources as well as independence.
reservations: Current annual completions, local utility gains and additional household savings are unverified.
HUD funding and municipal alternatives weaken an unrestricted donation counterfactual.
Trial results are mixed, while full outside resource costs and marginal capacity remain unknown.

sections.what: North West Housing Partnership, EIN 36-3715417, provides housing repair, development and counseling in the Chicago metropolitan area. Current OAHMP eligibility covers homeowners aged 62 or older in Cook, DuPage, Lake, Kane and McHenry counties. Occupational therapists and registered nurses guide contractor-installed modifications. The official support page solicits donations; no checkout transaction was performed.
sections.monitoring: A primary HUD bulletin reports an August 2023 $800,000 award for planned modifications in 75 units. This is a multi-period plan, not 75 verified current annual completions. The current program page establishes a free, HUD-funded service and assessment process, not a deduplicated annual cohort, completed dose, control group or new-donation bottleneck. Municipal and AgeOptions services remain relevant alternatives. The numerical 100 annual opportunities, 0.5 additional funded-work response and 0.6 clinical completion/fidelity are judgments. Cases use 75 opportunities or 25 per year if the historical plan were spread across three years; neither is observed current throughput.
sections.qualitative: The 2019 CAPABLE randomized trial tested up to ten OT, nurse and home-modifier visits over five months in 300 low-income Baltimore residents aged at least 65. The adjusted ADL ratio was 0.70 at five months; the 12-month ratio was 0.90 with a confidence interval including no effect. In the 2025 posthospital trial of 268 adults, overall ADL improvement was not significant, although mobility improved. Local OT/RN involvement does not establish equivalent dose, baseline disability or fidelity. Neither study measures a transferable 0.03 QALY increment, avoided injurious falls, mortality or local household savings. The clinical center retains the original weak utility judgment for a finite five months, not an empirically calibrated estimate. Nonrandomized Medicare expenditure estimates concern payer spending, not household cash or validated social resource savings.
sections.cost:
FY2025 original expense is $642,680; FY2024 is $542,871. FY2023 $902,809 expense plus $729,996 separately netted inventory cost gives $1,632,805 full recognized cost. Schedule D's $390,852 reconciliation is already included, not added twice. FY2024 minus $1 donated-service reconciliation is immaterial, not meaningful negative resources. FY2023 rental gross and net match in retrieved fields; absence of an addback is not proof of zero resources. Three-year mean is $939,452; property activity makes it imperfect operating comparison. Unrecognized volunteer and outside resources remain unknown.

Judged 100 local household opportunities and .5 additional annual-work response expose 50 households. Completion .6 yields 30 clinical residents within that union. Judged .03 utility for five months, quarter-year delay and 3% discount give .372239 clinical QALYs. Whole annual cost remains; this is a narrow conditional channel, not full portfolio or measured marginal-gift productivity.

Fifteen households conditionally avoid $1,000 actual repair spending and $500 net energy/care burdens in one year, net of taxes, benefits, replacement support and maintenance. Each positive component retains .5 for health overlap; negative components remain full. Full $100 disruption/time cost leaves $650. Thirty-five others lose $100. At $25,000 annual resources and one welfare-equivalent person per household, one joint log yields .121467 equivalents. Additional family welfare is unpriced. Combined .493706 gives $13.017467 million per ten combined equivalents, not ten clinical QALYs.

Resource exposure and costs survive clinical failure. Full 50-household harm and distinct local payer/contractor losses are stresses. Central outside incidence and harms are unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete-world benefit. Public and nonlocal opportunity costs remain unpriced.

Deep review keeps the original central price unchanged: $13.017467 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents, comprising 0.372239 clinical QALYs and 0.121467 income equivalents. Income equivalents are not clinical QALYs. The apparent precision comes from arithmetic, not empirical calibration. One modeled welfare-equivalent person per household excludes additional family effects. Fifty household opportunities form the full exposed union; thirty clinical residents are a subset. Resource success among fifteen households is independent of clinical success, and burdens survive a clinical null.

The $1,000 avoided repair spending must be cash the household would actually have paid absent NWHP after HUD, municipal and other support—not retail repair value or property appreciation. The $500 energy/care gain is already net of replacement services; distinct tax, benefit-withdrawal, work and maintenance parameters test missing incidence without asserting observations. Positive components alone receive the overlap haircut before being combined with full negative components and full burdens in one household log. The default one-year resource horizon is finite; extended-horizon cases repeat only energy/care/work changes, benefit withdrawal and maintenance. Repair spending avoided and process disruption are one-off in the first year. Zero resource duration removes gains but keeps full one-off process burden. Counterparty stresses price lost contractor margin or displaced public beneficiaries as distinct households. Those stresses do not double-charge donation expenditure already in the full annual denominator. Nonlocal and whole-portfolio incidence remain unknown; a positive partial ledger is not complete-world benefit.
sections.funding: The original fiscal 2025 Form 990 reports $642,680 recognized expenses and $122,697 government grants. FY2024 gross cost is $542,871; FY2023 includes $902,809 expenses plus $729,996 separately netted inventory cost, totaling $1,632,805. Schedule D's $390,852 reconciliation is already in the 990 expense. The three-year mean is $939,452, but property activity makes it an imperfect recurring operating comparator. The FY2024 minus $1 reconciliation is an immaterial presentation oddity, not negative social resources. The HUD $800,000 award is neither an additional FY2025 expense nor proof of an unfunded current cohort. Whole-recipient annual cost is compared with a limited local channel; the 0.5 response is a conditional annual-work counterfactual, not a measured next-gift multiplier. Marginal donations, public-funding replacement and volunteer capacity require direct follow-up.

model.geographicAttribution: Chicago metro households; clinical residents are a subset of resource exposure.
model.formula: Health = N × b × completion × q × discounted finite health years minus full exposed-union harms. Household resources = 0.5 × disjoint household units × discounted years × log(1 + jointly net signed resources / baseline). Positive overlap applies to each positive component only. Headline = 10 × full annual recognized cost plus separately identified external economic cost / (clinical QALYs + resource equivalents). Repair savings and process costs occur once. Recurring resources and maintenance share one first-year net log and separate later-year joint logs; zero resource duration retains process costs.
model.counterfactual: Existing HUD-funded, municipal and AgeOptions services continue; some households would defer repairs or not purchase them. Conditional annual work adds only incremental outcomes beyond those alternatives. Next-gift response and full portfolio effects remain unknown.
model.attribution: Throughput, additional annual response, completion, utility and actual spending are separate judgments.
model.uncertainty: Conditional original priors retained, not empirically calibrated whole-portfolio expected value. Local cohorts, trial transfer, actual otherwise-paid spending, household baseline and public-resource replacement are unknown. Unknown controls remain null, not factual zero.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional completed home modifications and short-term functional independence, plus actual net household spending avoided; not announced units, repair retail value, property wealth or payer expenditure counted as household income.
