what: Remote Area Medical organizes free dental, vision and medical clinics with volunteer clinicians, staff and local community hosts.
Patients can receive basic dental treatment or eye examination and glasses, often alongside general medical services, without insurance or identification.
Its Tennessee hybrid telehealth service combines an onsite nurse with a remote volunteer physician for acute care and short medication refills.
strengths: Free glasses and adequately completed dental treatment can restore useful vision and relieve painful episodes.
Volunteer clinicians and local hosts provide an established delivery network, supported by current native service records.
Original audited statements and a reproducible model make national support costs, patient benefits and household burdens inspectable.
reservations: The approximately $5.3M per better life estimate depends on judged clinical, funding-response and household assumptions, not measured RAM causal outcomes.
Repeat visits, paired glasses, teeth treated and overlapping medical encounters do not identify unique completed national beneficiaries.
Clinician and host capacity, alternative care, sustained outcomes and net patient costs remain uncertain; additional donation capacity is not verified.

sections.what: RAM's [clinic FAQ](https://www.ramusa.org/frequently-asked-questions/) describes free basic dental treatment, eye examinations and glasses, with general medical services. Patients normally choose dental or vision on a given day. No insurance or identification is required, but first-come access can mean an overnight wait. [Community hosts](https://www.ramusa.org/host-a-ram-clinic/) recruit volunteers, secure venues and arrange lodging; planning may take a year or more. RAM supplies equipment and operating systems and bears most delivery costs. [Tennessee telehealth](https://www.ramusa.org/) connects an on-site nurse with a volunteer physician as a bridge to continuing primary care. The [current telehealth description](https://www.ramusa.org/telehealth/) limits care to short-term needs: no laboratory or X-ray services, no replacement for continuing primary care, and prescription costs remain the patient's responsibility.
sections.monitoring:
The official impact-map dataset places all 7,999 eye exams and 15,013 pairs of glasses reported for 2025 at clinics in 27 USA states. Its total of 32,770 patients matches the headline, but its 7,387 Philippine patients differ from the 990's 7,402, and its 225 event rows do not reconcile to the return's 436 clinics. These are not national deduplicated clinical outcomes. Local reports explicitly show patients receiving multiple services. The [official impact map](https://www.ramusa.org/our-impact/) embeds a [downloadable event dataset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ITDeptAdmin/ImpactMap/main/output/ImpactMap_Dataset.geojson). Independent aggregation found 216 US rows and nine Philippine rows, no duplicate event identifiers, 25,383 US-location patients and 7,387 Philippine-location patients. All named 2025 service counts are in US rows; foreign zero fields do not establish absence of care. US venue is an approximation to residence, not patient-level proof.

The [Erie host report](https://www.builderie.org/assets/RAM-Impact-Report-2025.pdf) lists 224 patients but 188 dental, 86 medical and 35 vision service-patient counts, totaling 309. Its wording about 309 individuals must not replace the lower patient count; the report explicitly notes multiple services. Neither unique event IDs nor local examples establish nationwide deduplication. Pairs do not generate separate vision streams; multiple teeth may belong to one painful episode. Screening and referrals require completed treatment before health can be credited.

The October 2026 recheck reproduces the official map totals: 225 event IDs, 216 U.S. rows and nine Philippine rows. U.S. venue counts are not proof of recipient residence or unique patients. We separately model repeated attendance, dental-or-vision base visits and possible medical overlays; these are mapping judgments rather than a measured joint cohort. Monitoring should link meaningful impairment, treatment completion, later alternatives, household identity, actual travel and lost paid earnings, and filled prescriptions. A clinic encounter is not completed long-term disease control.
sections.qualitative:
The [selected U.S. refractive-correction trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16776781/) randomized 131 older adults with meaningful correctable impairment to immediate or delayed glasses/magnifiers and found better vision-specific function at three months. We checked the primary abstract, not a full dataset. This supports a concrete mechanism but does not establish RAM's generic QALY gain, severity mix or multiyear persistence. The earlier hypothetical utility-loss study is not used as a measured treatment effect. Our 0.035 gross annual utility prior, 50% meaningful impairment, 85% completion/initial uptake and two-year clinical window are explicit judgments. Mortality, loss of useful correction and later alternative care are separate. The two-year window is accounting truncation, not proof that all functioning ends then. The historical VISIBLE falls/adaptation finding remains context; fresh access was blocked, and no broad fall-prevention benefit is credited.

For dentistry, the [original root-canal/extraction cohort](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cre2.759), read through targeted primary results and discussion, compares treated patients rather than untreated RAM alternatives. Its approximately 0.83 annual QALYs is total health, not health gained from extraction. We model one adequately treated symptomatic episode, not every tooth or filling: a judged 0.05 gross utility increment over a quarter-year, attenuated for later alternative care, with separate acute treatment harm. Cleaning and screening do not receive an automatic additional benefit. Long-run tooth loss and other dental effects remain unpriced unknowns; a higher-harm stress is retained.

The [current acute medical service](https://www.ramusa.org/telehealth/) can bridge a short access gap, including simple illness care and short refills. Our 0.08 utility for about 29 days applies only to a judged actionable, adequately completed episode. It is not identified by a matched clinical study. Medical overlays share the patient's trip; positive overlapping health receives a 50% independence allowance while harms are charged fully. Screenings, uncompleted referrals, preventive or systemic effects and survival remain outside this finite selected-pathway model, not proven zero.

The [THRIVE trial](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0296115) found higher self-reported income in selected Bangladesh workers receiving near-vision correction. [PROSPER](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2214109X18303292) found a short-run tea-output effect in selected Indian workers; its primary abstract was available. Neither percentage is transported directly to RAM's mixed population. We instead use small, stated net-pay priors for a subset of genuinely additional corrected or treated households, with time, loss and overlap adjustments. Employer output, gross salaries, leisure values and ordinary earnings of newly surviving people are not household benefits.

Current audited national accounts and advertised clinics establish an operating organization and an accountable payee. They do not establish what another donation would causally unlock. The model is a conditional comparison of plausible mechanisms and costs, not an identified expected unrestricted-donation return or a funding offer.
sections.cost:
GiveBetter views RAM's free vision, dental and acute medical services as plausible ways to improve everyday function and relieve illness. We estimate approximately **$5.3M per better life**, combining clinical health and signed household-resource welfare. One better life is ten combined health/income-equivalent years; the economic part is not measured clinical QALYs.

**What does the money support?** At the $10,000 modeling scale, a judged $500 full national support allowance and 40% funding response imply **8 additional attendance-equivalents**, 7.2 distinct clinical people, 5.76 representative households and two unsuccessful extra attempts. That is approximately $1,250 per added attendance-equivalent after the response assumption, not a quoted appointment price. Support retains administration, fundraising, foreign support, nonclinical work, depreciation and failure overhead. Volunteer clinicians and hosts remain necessary complements.

The modeled meaningful completed outputs are about 0.92 vision corrections, 1.58 symptomatic dental episodes and 0.55 actionable medical episodes. After otherwise purchased or free care, truly additional completions are about 0.47, 0.83 and 0.23 respectively. Medical may overlap other care, so these are not additive unique people. Paired glasses and multiple teeth are never counted as separate people.

**Why might the services help?** Improved vision can make reading and daily tasks easier. Adequately completed dental care may relieve a painful episode; medical care may resolve a short illness or medication gap. Severity, completion, utility, alternatives and persistence are judged separately rather than imported from raw service counts. Purchasers receiving equivalent care anyway receive no additional clinical relief or matching procedure harm. Extra access and failed-attempt burdens remain.

At the modeling scale, vision contributes **0.020042 clinical QALYs**, dentistry **0.008135**, and acute medical care **0.001192**; independent attendance and failed-attempt burden subtracts **0.000980**. Net health is **0.028388 QALYs**, giving a clinical-only donor comparison of about $3.52M per ten. Medical positive overlap is adjusted without erasing harms. The clinical accounting windows do not assert that all useful functioning abruptly ends at their cutoffs.

**Income, savings and household costs.** The [Coefficient Giving reference framework](https://coefficientgiving.org/research/cost-effectiveness/) compares changes in disposable household resources with healthy-year equivalents. Our $22,000 receiving-household and $50,000 volunteer-household baselines are judgments, not measured RAM mean incomes. Receiving households incur a judged $35 extra travel and $20 actual lost net paid work per visit, relative to their no-gift alternatives—not every waiting hour valued at wages. A medical overlay shares the trip. Repeated visits incur cash again but no second clinical or earnings stream; failed extra attempts cost a judged $30 per household.

Otherwise-paying care recipients avoid judged actual payments of $80 for vision, $150 for dental care or $30 for medical care. Those are not donated retail values or savings for every recipient. Sixty percent of newly unlocked actionable medical treatment households are assumed to fill an additional $15 prescription. Filled and unfilled states are distinguished before valuing simultaneous trip, purchase and prescription cash; ordinary prescriptions bought in the comparator are not new costs. The independence of joint state probabilities is itself a correlation judgment.

Newly treated vision and dental households incur $10 or $25 upkeep at year 1.5. This is a **persistent net incremental cash obligation**, survival-weighted even after the clinical valuation window or later alternative care; it is not a measured invoice. If upkeep only exists while treatment remains causally additional, the population rule must change. Volunteers incur a judged $25 extra actual travel cash across 0.4 volunteer households per added attendance-equivalent. Unpaid labor is not automatically free, but lost leisure is not counted as lost household earnings.

The earnings prior applies to 25% of genuinely additional vision households: $300 annual net pay for two years, beginning at year one after the gift. For dentistry, 20% receive $200 annual net pay for a quarter-year beginning at year 0.75. This lagged dental resource flow is distinct from the quarter-year clinical window, not evidence of sustained clinical relief. Common-alive exposure is attenuated for mortality, functioning loss and later alternatives. Only 25% of positive earnings welfare is retained for overlap; **negative wages and direct cash losses are fully charged**. Medical earnings and upkeep remain zero in this scoped comparison; unsupported nonzero overlay parameters are rejected. After-burden income denominators are not a second cash credit.

Direct resource welfare is **−0.009581 equivalent years** and independent earnings add **+0.000222**. Net resources are **−0.009359**, leaving **0.019029 combined equivalents** and an exact donor comparison of **$5,255,154 per ten**. Expected undiscounted direct cash falls about $472 across the modeled cohort; common-alive net pay rises about $41 before the positive-overlap adjustment. These money amounts are not the welfare score itself.

**What changed?** The historical initial **$1.33M** estimate counted only vision, using the old 75% geographic share and clinical product. Correcting service location alone gave a $996K vision diagnostic; a later review left the broader central unknown. We now estimate finite selected pathways explicitly instead of treating missing local causal evidence as a reason not to make a judgment estimate. Vision assumptions were independently reconsidered: lower utility, shorter window, separate completion, repeat-person adjustment, purchaser partition, later alternatives and funding response. Dental and acute medical benefits are added, alongside signed household effects; no old welfare envelope is preserved by construction.

**Uncertainty and associated resources.** The favorable combined stress is about $363K, faster alternatives about $12.0M, and the adverse joint stress has negative combined benefit. These are assumption tests, not confidence intervals. Known zero capacity or no gift means zero demand even if other causal inputs are unavailable. An unavailable funding response remains unknown; its supplied placeholder is not an observed zero. Unknown clinical or dependent resource inputs remain unknown. The $25,000 software domain and 20-attendance capacity limit are not verified donation capacity or linear scaling promises.

The selected gross institutional companion adds recorded labor and host resources, with a central numerator of $13,181 and price about $6.93M per better life. This is not donor cash, actual volunteer lost earnings or a net societal cost-effectiveness ratio. Volunteer household travel is not charged again in that numerator. Long-run dental, prevention, systemic and other portfolio effects remain outside the finite comparison, unknown rather than guaranteed positive.

**Financial appendix.** Three comparable audited expense years, 2023–25, are $12,388,388, $15,134,442 and $19,852,655: mean **$15,791,828**. Recorded donated labor is $3,765,180, $6,307,965 and $9,330,033. Subtracting it gives annual non-volunteer expense proxies of $8,623,208, $8,826,477 and $10,522,622, still partly noncash. The latest proxy divided by U.S.-location people is about $415 per person, not marginal cash cost. The $500 support allowance is a separate judgment. All national expenses remain charged; the $1,001 affiliate expense line is not a separately reconciled affiliate denominator. The fresh original audit and inherited tax reconciliation are distinguished in Sources.
sections.funding:
The [FY2025 audit](https://www.ramusa.org/wp-content/uploads/RAM-Final-2025-Audited-Financial-Statements.pdf) reports $19,852,655 total expenses, including $9,330,033 donated labor, versus $15,134,442 in 2024. [The prior September review of Schedule D](https://www.ramusa.org/wp-content/uploads/RAM-2025-990-Final-Public.pdf) reconciles $10,349,704 tax functional expense plus $172,918 rental expenses and donated labor to the audited total. Thus $10,522,622 is a non-volunteer expense proxy, still including depreciation and some in-kind supplies, not cash flow. General contributions fell from $9.12 million to $7.43 million and operating cash flow was −$1.46 million. Yet $6.91 million of financial assets remained available within a year. RAM acquired two headquarters buildings, spent $7.12 million on property/equipment and took a $2.5 million interest-only loan due December 2027, collateralized by a CD. Asset-sale gains and temporary rent are not repeatable clinic funding. These facts suggest possible funding need but do not establish extra clinician slots or a funding-contingent clinic backlog.

The [current hosting process](https://www.ramusa.org/host-a-ram-clinic/) and [FAQ](https://www.ramusa.org/frequently-asked-questions/) show concrete local-host and clinician constraints. No current funded tranche with confirmed extra appointments, clinical completion or a demonstrated unrestricted-funding response was found. A deficit or capital expansion alone does not establish incremental patient care. Patient alternatives include delayed paid or insurance-funded care, community clinics, dental schools and other charities; access barriers do not quantify their timing or availability.

The October source check targeted original 2025 audit statements and notes, plus the 2024 audit with 2023 comparison. Freshly hashing the scanned 2025 return did not yield readable targeted text; the tax functional-expense/rental/donated-labor bridge remains inherited, not a newly OCR-reviewed Schedule D. Current audit revenue is $18,844,882, net assets $19,060,569, cash $4,154,868, restricted net assets $157,648 and debt $2,500,000. The older operating-cash and available-financial-assets figures above remain dated prior audit findings. Asset-sale gains, capital expansion, volunteer retail valuations and annual deficits do not prove current gift-sensitive clinician slots or a funding offer.

model.costScope: Ordinary national donor support, all non-volunteer functions and foreign support retained. Full donor numerator prices finite selected clinical/resource paths, not identified whole-portfolio return. Gross institutional resources are separate; household cash losses stay in welfare.
model.geographicAttribution: g=.98 applies once to health and each signed receiving/volunteer resource flow. US-location service counts are not measured residence; all national expenses retained. No global patient share applied to vision-only output.
model.formula: N=min(G*b/c,capacity); distinct=N*uniqueShare; base vision/dental/medical visitors partition distinct people, medical overlay overlaps vision/dental. Meaningful completed and additional cohorts separately apply severity, completion, purchaser and unmet fractions. Clinical integrates discounted gross utility with mortality/loss/alternative care and subtracts incremental harms. Joint household care/Rx states net simultaneous cash before signed logarithmic welfare; timed upkeep/earnings use separate flows. Combined=health+resources; positive known donor price=10*G/combined.
model.counterfactual: Committed existing funding, clinicians, hosts, paid/free alternatives and subsequent access remain without the gift. Otherwise purchasers and equivalent free care have no incremental matched treatment benefit/harm; extra access attempts can still incur harm and cash. Screening/referral is not automatic completed care.
model.attribution: One extra attendance is not a deduplicated person, household or treatment. DentalORvision base pathways are disjoint on one modeled visit, medical overlays share trip; repeated attendance carries no extra clinical/earnings stream. Positive earnings overlap is separate; all losses fully debit. Common-alive earnings are not survival-created income.
model.uncertainty: All causal throughput, utility, completion, visitor/counterfactual/household mapping, residence, net cash and earnings priors are judgments. T is a clinical accounting window, not abrupt end of all functioning. Upkeep is persistent net incremental care-induced cash after later alternatives; its assumed incidence is not observed. Known capacity0 overrides funding unknown; supplied b is unavailable when fundingKnown false. Nonzero medical wages/upkeep unsupported until overlay paths are implemented. Unpriced branches remain unknown; fixed limits are not donation room.
model.nativeOutcomes: Native 2025 US-location data: 25,383 patients, 7,999 eye exams and 15,013 glasses; teeth/encounters are different units. Central $10K comparison models 8 attendances, 7.2 distinct clinical people, 0.47 additional vision corrections, 0.83 dental episodes and 0.23 acute medical episodes. Health .028388425278921235 plus resources −.00935948546284748 yields .019028939816073755 combined equivalents.

historicalModel.costScope: Ordinary unrestricted recipient support. All recipient functions, fundraising, rental expenses and depreciation are retained in C; only recorded volunteer labor is removed for a support-dollar throughput anchor. C=10522622 is not marginal cash cost. The full-resource sensitivity restores volunteer labor. Local host costs, volunteer travel, unrecorded supplies and patient waiting/travel are additional societal costs not fully measured. G=10000 is arithmetic normalization only.
historicalModel.geographicAttribution: All 7,999 eye exams and 15,013 glasses in the matched 2025 map occur in the 50-state boundary. A .75 haircut inferred from all-patient mix is unsupported for this vision-specific count. Use g_v=1 only as a USA-residency approximation to service location, and state that qualification. Do not allocate dental/medical health by the same all-patient fraction. Full recipient costs remain charged, including any foreign support. The map sums to 32,770 patients, matching the 2025 headline. Form 990 Part III says 7,402 Philippine patients, leaving 25,368 elsewhere, a 15-patient discrepancy against the map. Its 436 clinics do not equal 225 distinct 2025 map event IDs. The mapping of clinic-days, telehealth sessions and events is not documented. Zero Philippine procedure fields are unreported service data, not proof no procedures occurred.
historicalModel.formula: D=sum(t=1..T)[((1-m)/1.03)^t]; H_v=N_v*(f*s*u*p*D-h); H_USA=g_v*H_v+H_d_USA+H_m_USA-H_cross; Q_USA=(G/C)*b*H_USA; price=10*G/Q_USA if Q_USA>0. This formula defines conditional diagnostic scenarios only. Whole-recipient central health is not estimable from the present evidence.
historicalModel.counterfactual: RAM's host page says planning can take a year or longer, and hosts recruit local volunteers, secure venues and lodging. FAQ explicitly ties the number served to clinician availability. A functioning network and current event calendar are evidence of delivery, not proof that b=.5 of donation-proportional throughput is additional. Patient alternatives include delayed paid care, insurance-funded care, community health centers, dental schools and other charities. Erie lists community health centers on-site for continuing-care resources. RAM's 2024 patient questionnaire summary reports roughly 46% with some insurance; neither insurance nor lack of insurance identifies actual timely alternative access. Counterfactual timing should be pathway-specific. Identical replacement care cancels shared harms; extra duplicative care may retain incremental harms.
historicalModel.attribution: All recipient costs retained. H_d and H_m must be net of alternative care, overlap and pathway harms, with H_cross only for remaining cross-pathway displacement or double counting. Shared b is a simplifying conditional historical-scale response, not measured marginal production. A full-recipient central requires all material health pathways and current cash response. RAM's current FAQ permits medical plus dental or vision on a day. It does not establish cross-day or cross-event deduplication. Count no second vision stream for two pairs, no separate dental QALY for every tooth or filling, no screening benefit without completed treatment, and no addition of overlapping whole-person utilities without adjustment.
historicalModel.uncertainty: No empirical reason found to retain .6 meaningful correction, .5 additional patient benefit, .04 utility, .8 persistence and 3 years as the expected joint product. Full-resource and clinical-yield sensitivity change price greatly. Conversely ignoring all dental/medical health may understate benefit. Neither direction supports preserving the old number by default. N_v and financial expense are observed counts; C construction and every causal/utility/persistence parameter are judgments. g_v=1 is a service-location-based resident-health approximation, stronger than the old global .75, but not observed residence. H_d=H_m=0 is not an expected value.
historicalModel.nativeOutcomes: 2025 US-location map counts: 25,383 patients, 7,999 eye exams, 15,013 pairs, 11,557 extractions, 4,333 fillings, 3,609 cleanings, 5,523 medical exams and 1,315 women's-health services. Different units are not additive people or health outcomes. No observed additional output per unrestricted donation is established.

what: Immunize.org provides vaccination guidance, translated patient information and practical tools for clinicians, including standing-order templates.
It also coordinates coalitions, advises policy makers and helps clinical organizations improve vaccination delivery.
Its potential health value comes from otherwise-missed effective vaccinations and better practice—not from downloads, subscribers or recognition lists alone.
strengths: Standing orders and related workflow changes can increase vaccination in randomized studies, and the recipient has evaluated implementation in actual clinics.
A national library can support many practitioners at low distribution cost while translating changing clinical recommendations into usable tools.
Original financial filings and a recipient-authored five-clinic study make the funding and implementation assumptions inspectable.
reservations: There is no current measured link from unrestricted donations to additional effective practice implementation or completed vaccination.
Large reserves, government and industry support, existing free guidance and clinician capacity complicate next-dollar additionality.
Vaccine, age, season, timing and geography determine health yield; a generic vaccination count cannot support a single defensible QALY conversion.

sections.what: The [current organization](https://www.immunize.org/about/org/overview/) supplies clinician guidance, patient resources and coalition support, including an English/Spanish public-information site launched in 2025. Its [standing-order tools](https://www.immunize.org/clinical/topic/standing-orders-templates/) help authorized personnel assess and vaccinate eligible patients under an approved protocol. The [implementation guide](https://www.immunize.org/wp-content/uploads/catg.d/p3067.pdf) requires leadership support, a responsible champion, training and local legal compliance; downloading a template is not implementation. The [homepage](https://www.immunize.org/) was actively updating 2026–27 resources during review and distinguished professional-society guidance from CDC recommendations. This report evaluates the recipient, not individual clinical recommendations.
sections.monitoring: The [FY2025 original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202640819349300504/IRS990) and [highlights](https://www.immunize.org/wp-content/uploads/2024-iac-major-projects.pdf) report 5.2 million educational downloads,5.7 million VIS/translation downloads and over 50000 newsletter subscribers. These include repeat use and do not count additional vaccinations. The [November appeal](https://www.immunize.org/wp-content/uploads/2025_appeal_letter.pdf) gives different download totals, so definitions or extraction periods need reconciliation. Honor rolls recognize existing policies; membership is not evidence the recipient caused adoption. A [recipient-authored five-clinic study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31630922/) found modest, uneven gains after standing orders. Its [original poster](https://www.izsummitpartners.org/content/uploads/2018/05/VanOss_Impact-of-Standing-Orders-Protocols.pdf) explicitly identifies changing denominators and data-extraction improvements behind some apparent gains.
sections.qualitative: The [five-clinic evaluation](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31630922/) was before/after, not randomized against equivalent support. In contrast, the [BE IMMUNE trial](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamainternalmedicine/article-abstract/2843384) found a 5.1-percentage-point increase in vaccination during visits using reminders, automatically pended orders and clinician feedback; extra bidirectional texts did not add benefit. An [older inpatient randomized trial](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/199810) found 42% versus 30% influenza vaccination with standing orders rather than reminders. These establish a workflow mechanism, not the impact of distributing a template. [Current test-negative evidence](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/75/wr/mm7509a2.htm) estimated 31% effectiveness against hospitalization in adults 65+ in 2025–26. Mortality conversion remains a model judgment: [CDC's methodology](https://www.cdc.gov/flu-burden/php/about-burden-prevented/how-cdc-estimates-vaccinations.html) also transfers inpatient effectiveness to deaths and identifies coverage and surveillance limitations. The BE IMMUNE trial enrolled patients aged 50 and older (mean 65.8), not exclusively those aged 65 and older. The model's three-percentage-point transfer to the older subgroup is an analyst judgment, not a measured subgroup effect. [Trial](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamainternalmedicine/article-abstract/2843384)
sections.cost: Our best estimate: About $101 million per 10 USA QALYs through older-adult influenza protection. We assume 100 otherwise-additional practice implementations, each reaching 1,000 eligible patients with a three-percentage-point uptake increase. After funding response, this gives about 2.3 additional doses per $10,000, at 0.000451 net QALY per dose before geography for one influenza season. We choose 100 otherwise-attributable practice implementations per annual cost equivalent, rather than the earlier 1,000-case probe. For scale, this is 0.2% of roughly 50,000 subscribers; subscribers are not unique practices and this is not measured conversion. The small conversion allows passive use, duplication and equivalent free guidance. A further 25% funding response allows reserves and substitution. Other vaccine health remains unpriced. Favorable, zero and adverse cases remain in the transparent model; positive scenarios are not confidence bounds or verified funding offers.
sections.funding: [FY2025 tax expense](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202640819349300504/IRS990) was $3,181,332; restoring $65,922 cost of goods sold gives $3,247,254. [Schedule D](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202640819349300504/IRS990ScheduleD) adds $81,792 donated services for $3,329,046 gross recognized resource expense, including $10,300 investment-management costs netted in the audited presentation. Payroll/benefits were $1.67 million; partnership and educational programs split most program spending. Contributions fell from $3.57 million to $2.63 million, including $437,500 government grants, yet tax revenue exceeded functional expense by $610,867. June 2025 unrestricted net assets were $6.90 million, with $1.40 million cash and $6.40 million securities. The [2023 audit](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/display_audit/2023-06-GSAFAC-0000019639) found weak financial-statement preparation and segregation controls and an incorrect federal report, but no questioned costs or underlying cash/expenditure discrepancy; management reported correcting that form inDecember 2023. Current remediation needs checking. That audit also reported 47% pharmaceutical-company funding in 2023—not a current share or evidence of improper influence. Reserves and sponsor support require a specific funding-contingent plan before assigning strong marginal additionality.

model.costScope: Ordinary unrestricted recipient support retains all programs, fundraising, administration, merchandise cost and investment-management costs. C=3247254 is FY 2025 tax functional expense plus 65922 COGS, a non-donated-service expense anchor, not cash flow or marginal cost. Annual financial series additionally includes 81792 recognized donated services in 2025. Donated information, external clinician implementation labor, vaccines and administration are not free societal resources. G=10000 is normalization only.
model.geographicAttribution: USA residents of 50 states andDC are the target. US clinical schedules, domestic coalitions and practice guidance support a predominantly domestic pathway, but the public websites and global policy advising also reach abroad. FY 2025 ScheduleF records 26524 international guidance expense inEastAsia/Pacific andEurope; that expenditure percentage does not measure health share. Conditional g=.95, stress.8–.99, is a judgment for the older-adult influenza pathway, not observed outcome attribution. Other geography and vaccine pathways remain unquantified.
model.formula: At annual recipient scale, N=K×V×delta additional at-visit influenza doses from otherwise-attributable implementations. q=tau×(rD×e×L+rH×e×qH+rI×e×qI)−h net QALY per dose. Q_all=(G/C)×b×N×q + Q_other; Q_USA=Q_all×g in conditional homogeneous-geography tests. Price=10G/Q_USA if positive. Central b, K and g are judgments; other health remains unpriced. K discounts adoption that equivalent freely available guidance would cause anyway; b separately discounts donor/sponsor replacement or reserve financing. tau discounts later alternative vaccination and incomplete seasonal protection. h is incremental adverse burden relative to the actual alternative; under identical timely replacement vaccination both incremental protection and incremental harm are zero. Conditional cases set Q_other=0, not as a lower-bound claim.
model.counterfactual: Existing clinic workflows, electronic-record vendors, professional societies, CDC guidance and other coalitions can substitute for Immunize.org materials. Templates already online may remain available without a new gift. K must count implementation actually induced, not honor-roll enrollment, pageviews or workshop attendance. b handles funding source replacement separately. Medicare already covers seasonal flu vaccine without patient payment at participating providers; clinical access and workflow can still limit receipt. tau allows later vaccination elsewhere and dose timing. No public-payer savings are converted to health. Identical timely vaccination elsewhere has the same ordinary adverse effects: set tau=0 and h=0. Negative probes require genuinely additional ineffective or duplicate doses, not shared counterfactual harms.
model.attribution: All recipient cost is retained while the conditional health calculation considers only older-adult influenza. Other vaccines, policies, translated safety information and reduced errors may matter greatly, but require separate age/pathogen-specific clinical bridges and counterfactuals. No generic vaccine QALY coefficient is applied to all output. No herd-immunity multiplier, indefinite recurring practice benefit, honor-roll causation, saved healthcare dollars or productivity is credited. Autonomy and consent concerns in policy advocacy are not erased by this narrow clinical calculation.
model.uncertainty: We choose 100 otherwise-attributable practice implementations per annual cost equivalent, rather than the earlier 1,000-case probe. For scale, this is 0.2% of roughly 50,000 subscribers; subscribers are not unique practices and this is not measured conversion. The small conversion allows passive use, duplication and equivalent free guidance. A further 25% funding response allows reserves and substitution. Other vaccine health remains unpriced. Zero and adverse outcomes remain possible; the quantified pathway is not a complete portfolio valuation.
model.nativeOutcomes: Observed downloads and roughly 50,000 subscribers demonstrate reach, not changed practice. The central judgment uses K=100, V=1000 and delta=.03: 3,000 additional at-visit doses per annual cost equivalent before funding response. With b=.25 and C=3247254 this is about 2.31 doses per $10,000 normalization. Each produces about .000451 net QALY before geography. The earlier 1,000-implementation alternative remains visible.

With V 1000, delta.03, b.25 and cautious q, K must be≥10105 annual attributable implementations for $1 million/10 or≥101054 for $100000/10. No observed denominator supports either target. Larger practices, more vaccines or durable effects could change this but require evidence.

Restoring $81792 recognized donated services increasesC and conditional price by 2.52%. Including an illustrative $50 external vaccine/administration cost peradditionaldose adds approximately $1.17 million per 10 USAQALYs at cautious q. That is a sensitivity, not an actual procurement price; patient/provider opportunity costs remain.

Without modeled mortality benefit, acute morbidity benefit nearly cancels the adopted transient adverse allowance. This exposes reliance on event-risk, mortality-effect and remaining-health assumptions, rather than proving poor clinical vaccination value.

For identical timely vaccination elsewhere, tau=0 and incremental h=0, so net health change is zero. Harm can remain when an ineffective or duplicate dose is genuinely additional, not merely obtained from a different provider.

One season only is credited. Multi-year workflow persistence would need continued use, vaccine updates, personnel continuity and protection against counting the same implementation again in later fundraising.
Do not treat FY 2025 foreign expense 26524/totalexpense as the USA health fraction, or apply older-adult influenza q to HPV, hepatitisB, meningococcal or childhood vaccines.

Honor rolls may improve practice incentives, but existing high-coverage institutions self-select. Prevented outbreaks or policy losses require causal probability and affected-population models, not a count of recognitions.

what: GHHI repairs housing hazards and helps public agencies, insurers and local organizations finance and deliver healthier homes.
Its services span lead remediation, asthma trigger reduction, injury prevention, energy upgrades, resident education and policy implementation.
The recipient also manages environmental-health grants, so its ordinary support cannot be treated as an asthma-only intervention.
strengths: Physical home repairs offer a concrete route from an identified hazard to lower exposure or injury risk.
Randomized evidence supports some asthma symptom and recurrent-fall benefits from related home interventions.
Recipient tax returns and a recent consolidated audit reveal spending, partners and the expanding grantmaking portfolio.
reservations: The incremental repairs, public-funding leverage and program mix caused by additional unrestricted support are not identified.
The prominent asthma hospitalization claim is uncontrolled, and lead remediation cannot simply be converted into IQ or lifetime QALYs.
The latest audit consolidates other entities, including a 501(c)(4); it is not the charitable recipient's standalone expense.

sections.what: GHHI's [Maryland services](https://www.greenandhealthyhomes.org/services/maryland-direct-services/) include assessments, hazard remediation, asthma education, energy upgrades, aging-in-place modifications and tenant advocacy. The [2024 recipient return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202543189349314709/IRS990) describes direct service and technical-assistance partnerships across US states, alongside policy, data and financing work. Health depends on actual repairs and sustained exposure reduction, not the number of assessments, grant applications or policy announcements.
sections.monitoring: In [2024](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202543189349314709/IRS990), Maryland recorded 875 asthma education/case-management home visits and 234 homes receiving healthy-housing/energy interventions; these are not 875 distinct treated children or 234 asthma-specific completions. Lancaster work included 220 lead-remediated homes and 77 healthy-homes interventions, financed with partners. The return also reports 303 cumulative Molina asthma members and a completed 461-member North Carolina fall-prevention pilot; the latter's payer ROI analysis was still prospective. Recipient-level tracking should identify unique residents, baseline hazards, completed repairs, health outcomes, alternatives, partner expenditure and what additional support changed.
sections.qualitative: The [Baltimore study](https://www.greenandhealthyhomes.org/wp-content/uploads/GHHI-Improving-Health-Economic-and-Social-Outcomes-through-Integrated-Housing-Intervention-Environmental-Justice.pdf) followed 139 of 201 children with paired caregiver surveys and reported approximately 66% fewer hospitalizations and 28% fewer emergency visits. It had no concurrent control; selection, regression to the mean, seasonality and reporting could explain part of the change. In contrast, [Morgan's randomized trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15356304/) of 937 urban children with atopic asthma found 0.81 fewer symptom days per fortnight in year one and 0.59 in year two. That is a clinical bridge, but generic utility per symptom day and transport to current GHHI clients remain judgments. [Lead-hazard randomization](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6233767/) reduced environmental lead but did not establish broad substantive neurobehavioral improvement. [Home-fall hazard removal](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8408671/) reduced the secondary fall rate, not the primary hazard of first falling or measured quality of life. Neither study licenses assigning every repair a large lifetime health gain. The lead trial enrolled a relatively low-exposure population; its null average neurobehavioral result does not establish zero benefit from targeting severe hazards. GHHI would need its own exposure distribution and sustained reduction before extrapolating larger effects.
sections.cost: Our best estimate: About $172 million per 10 USA QALYs through reduced asthma symptoms. At the modeled cost, portfolio allocation and funding response, $10,000 produces about 0.125 additional interventions. Each contributes roughly 0.0047 net QALY before geography, using trial symptom-day reductions, a cautious utility conversion and two years of benefit. We adopt the cautious asthma model: $8,000 per completed intervention, 20% portfolio allocation and 50% funding response. The cost allows a broader contemporary housing bundle than the older trial; allocation is a judgment informed by a mixed portfolio, not a reported asthma spending share. Lead, falls and policy effects remain unpriced, not worthless. Favorable, zero and adverse cases remain in the transparent model; positive scenarios are not confidence bounds or verified funding offers.
sections.funding: The [August 2026-issued audit](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/display_audit/2025-12-GSAFAC-0000426133) reports $7.89 m unrestricted consolidated net assets, $1.65 m operating cash inflow and $12.32 m financial assets available within a year. It reports $17.10 m federal expenditure, including $8.96 m passed to subrecipients. The [grantmaking page](https://www.greenandhealthyhomes.org/thrivingcommunities/) describes resumed EPA work and a closed application round; it does not establish an unrestricted funding gap. Private support may cover gaps in reimbursable work, but it may also substitute for government, hospital or insurance funding. Contractor capacity, referrals, landlord permission and participant retention matter. [Blue Cross NC's pilot](https://mediacenter.bcbsnc.com/news/blue-cross-nc-and-green-healthy-homes-initiative-team-up-to-reduce-home-injuries-for-leading-cause-of-er-visits-this-fall-season) illustrates why services already financed by an insurer must not all be attributed to philanthropy. No current itemized next-dollar expansion plan was found.

Conditional c includes allocated delivery/administration costs, f includes the ordinary-support portfolio share; partner repair costs must be added or explicitly attributed, not treated as free.

model.formula: Q_USA=(G*b*f/c)*[s*e*(d1+d2/1.03)*u/365-h]*g + G*theta_other; G=10000 computational normalization only. d1=.81*365/14; d2=.59*365/14. theta_other is net USA QALYs per unrestricted dollar from non-overlapping remaining pathways. Cost per 10=10G/Q_USA when positive.
model.counterfactual: b measures additional service spending rather than reserves or replacement funding; s is the fraction of asthma benefit absent without GHHI after landlord, public, insurer and other-provider alternatives. Both are currently judgmental rather than observed. h is incremental disruption or harm relative to the actual alternative. A different, less-disruptive option can deliver equivalent benefit while the extra repair adds harm; identical replacement repairs cancel shared burdens.
model.attribution: f isolates completed asthma remediation from lead, energy, grants, education and policy. e discounts trial transport, adherence and delivery differences. Do not credit public grant face value, partner-financed activity or coalition outcomes in full.
model.uncertainty: We adopt the cautious asthma model: $8,000 per completed intervention, 20% portfolio allocation and 50% funding response. The cost allows a broader contemporary housing bundle than the older trial; allocation is a judgment informed by a mixed portfolio, not a reported asthma spending share. Lead, falls and policy effects remain unpriced, not worthless. Zero and adverse outcomes remain possible; the quantified pathway is not a complete portfolio valuation.
model.nativeOutcomes: Completed and sustained hazard remediations; child symptom-free days; serious falls/injuries; measured exposure changes. Visits, homes, members, grants and dollars saved are not QALYs.

what: ANRF maintains tobacco-control policy data and supplies education, training and technical assistance for smoke-free environments.
It supports community and worker coalitions, including hospitality and casino workers, while addressing gaps in workplace and housing protection.
ANRF is the charitable recipient, distinct from the related Americans for Nonsmokers’ Rights; shared branding does not establish which entity caused an outcome.
strengths: Reducing secondhand smoke has a credible pathway to preventing serious cardiovascular harm.
ANRF supplies practical policy data and implementation assistance to communities and workers seeking smoke-free environments.
Original financial filings and a reproducible calculation make national support costs and the main health and household-resource assumptions inspectable.
reservations: The conditional estimate is about $67.6M per better life, versus $28.5M with no assumed worker-pay change and $18.1M with a small gain; USA wage effects are not measured.
Protected reach, policy additionality, ANRF contribution and next-dollar response are planning judgments, not a verified opportunity pipeline.
County-level health associations and German wage evidence may not transfer to the workers and patrons reached; the separate affiliate and remaining portfolio effects need further evidence.

sections.what: ANRF provides policy data, education and implementation assistance for smoke-free environments. Its [2024 return](https://no-smoke.org/wp-content/uploads/2024_ANRF_Form990.pdf) identifies the separate ANR affiliate. Schedule C Part I-A line 2 records $235,811 under political campaign activity, while Part IV describes legislative lobbying in NJ, PA and TN and CEASE coordination. The category/narrative mismatch is unresolved; we do not infer candidate campaigning, illegality or a filing error. It also makes a categorical assertion that only the affiliate lobbies too strong.
sections.monitoring:
ANRF’s [materials page](https://no-smoke.org/materials-services/) describes its law database and implementation training. Database records, users, papers and protected-population totals document reach, not incremental health. A valid marginal ledger would identify previously exposed nonsmokers, the change in protection relative to other actors, enforcement, years gained and the charitable recipient’s contribution. No such prospective ledger was located. We give no separate health credit for data use, publicity, training attendance or shareholder requests to study policies.

The October recheck found FY2024 reporting of 197,120 active website users and 708 newly analyzed laws. These are service outputs, not unique newly protected nonsmokers or causal successes. The model deliberately does not convert those counts into health gains. A useful next monitoring ledger would link named opportunities to prior exposure, likely outcomes without assistance, the charitable recipient’s role, implementation timing, resident beneficiaries and worker outcomes.
sections.qualitative:
The [Irish controlled before-after study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1283274/) followed bar workers for a year: among nonsmokers, cotinine fell more in the Republic than Northern Ireland, and respiratory symptoms improved. Attrition and nonrandom sampling limit transport; symptoms and biomarkers are not measured QALYs. The [Ho US study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5665160/) found no association with AMI or heart-failure hospitalizations after controls, tempering immediate cardiac claims. A [June 2026 study](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2850717) compared 38 adopting and 103 control counties using generalized synthetic controls. Its overall mortality association supports longer-term plausibility, but younger-adult estimates were imprecise and concurrent policies, ecological measurement and selected counties limit attribution. County population effects include mechanisms beyond exposed nonsmokers and cannot be inserted as worker-specific risk reductions or credited to ANRF. The [July 2026 Louisiana study](https://www.cdc.gov/pcd/issues/2026/25_0336.htm) examines ecological cancer incidence, not deaths; a Ouachita trend change preceded its law. We add no cancer, cessation, childhood or symptom QALYs to the cardiac model. Enforcement-related eviction, displacement and nicotine-substitution harms remain relevant; a small modeled harm allowance is not a verified upper bound.

The updated assessment distinguishes clinical protection from economic effects. The [US employment and sales study](https://www.cdc.gov/pcd/issues/2013/12_0327.htm) generally found no adverse restaurant/bar employment or sales association, but did not measure individual net wages and tips. An [AEA publisher summary of German research](https://www.aeaweb.org/research/charts/compensating-differentials-smoking-bans-germany) reports lower daily earnings after comprehensive bans, potentially reflecting lost hazard compensation. The full journal article was blocked in this recheck. That result is not a USA coefficient: we show zero, modest positive and adverse pay alternatives, rather than treating either employer revenue or a foreign percentage as local household income.
sections.cost:
**What does a donation support?** ANRF provides policy data, education and technical assistance that can help communities establish or preserve effective smoke-free protection. GiveBetter estimates about **$67.6 million per better life** in the central conditional comparison, combining health and net household resources. That figure is especially sensitive to the assumed worker-pay effect: **$28.5 million with no pay change**, or **$18.1 million with a small positive change**. These are transparent planning alternatives, not confidence limits or measured USA wage effects.

**From support to protection.** A $10,000 normalization funds 3.44 initially protected nonsmoker-equivalents and 13.62 discounted person-years of protection in this model: about $734 of national support per discounted protected year. It is not a service quote. All FY2024 charitable-recipient expenses, $3,927,527, remain in the cost denominator. The hypothetical opportunity collection contains 25,000 previously exposed nonsmokers per annual support equivalent, with 50% net coalition success, 20% ANRF contribution, 60% next-dollar response and 90% effective implementation. These are separate conditional judgments, not observed ANRF coefficients. The smaller reach prior is a scope/caution choice, not a newly measured pipeline; the prior 50,000 cohort is preserved in history and larger/smaller current reaches are tested. Database users, total statutory coverage and each new law are not additional cohorts.

**Health effects.** Protection begins after a judged one-year implementation lag and lasts at most five years, with 95% annual policy retention and 99% annual cohort survival. Clinical risk reversal ramps through 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% and 100% of its eventual level; the ecological study motivates a timing challenge but does not estimate this ramp. We use a worker/patron mixture with annual unexposed fatal and nonfatal coronary risks of 0.0006 and 0.0015, lower than the old 0.001 and 0.002 priors. CDC’s 25–30% coronary relative excess informs the 25% excess-risk judgment; half is removed and clinical transport is attenuated by half. These choices do not turn a county-level mortality association into an individual worker effect.

The calculation yields 9.03 ramp-weighted discounted exposure-years, 0.000335 fatal and 0.000838 nonfatal event-equivalents avoided for USA residents per $10,000. Avoided fatal events receive 10.50 subsequent discounted healthy years using a finite 20-year survivor horizon, 98% annual survival and 0.85 utility. This is a survivor-life surrogate, not a measured beneficiary life table. The 0.3-QALY nonfatal loss is pure clinical utility, not financial stress. Fatal and nonfatal branches are distinct; subsequent survival is not counted again as worker income. A separate 0.00002 clinical/downside allowance per protected year remains signed. Net health is **0.003504 healthy years**, or about **$28.54M per ten health years** alone. Younger-risk, older-risk/shorter-life, no-mortality and clinical-harm alternatives test the main assumptions.

**Household resources and income.** The [published reference framework](https://coefficientgiving.org/research/cost-effectiveness/) compares resource changes through one-half the logarithm of the resource ratio. This is welfare equivalence, not measured clinical QALYs. We assume $30,000 annual disposable household resources and one household-equivalent per modeled person; neither income distribution nor household overlap is measured locally, and no child or caregiver multiplier is added.

Thirty percent of protected person-years are assigned to workers. The central net wage/tip change is −0.1%, or −$30 per worker-year. This is a small skeptical transport judgment, **not a measured expected USA wage loss** and not the German −2.4% estimate imported wholesale. Its negative welfare receives the full debit. Zero and +0.1% pay cases are prominently shown because the outcome depends heavily on this prior. Wages occur only during the finite protection window among people alive in both worlds; ordinary earnings of people whose deaths are averted are excluded. Employer sales, payroll totals and revenue are not household income.

For avoided nonfatal events, separately judged household benefits are $300 of otherwise-paid medical expense and $500 of net recovery pay for workers. Insurance spending and hospital billed charges are not credited. Positive recovery welfare receives a 50% independence reservation; medical cash is distinct from the clinical utility loss. Worker/nonworker and avoided/nonavoided-event states are partitioned before logarithmic valuation: wage shifts occur first, medical cash is valued against post-wage resources, and recovery pay against post-medical resources. We do not take a logarithm of average lottery cash or count the same household baseline twice. Recurrent-event and household covariance are unmeasured.

A judged 1% of donor-supported potential people incur $5 of incremental travel or actual lost-pay advocacy expense at half a year. This is not all volunteer time priced as wages and is not suppressed merely because a policy fails. USA present-value medical cash is about **+$0.25**, net pay **−$121.22**, and attempted-access expense **−$0.37** per $10,000. Resource welfare is **−0.002024 equivalent years**, leaving **0.001480 combined equivalents** and **$67,579,293 per ten**. The money figures are not themselves the welfare score.

**What changed?** The preceding in-depth clinical-only estimate was **$8,194,355**; the initial alpha was approximately **$6.17M**. The revised model uses a smaller hypothetical reach, explicit implementation lag and risk-reversal ramp, lower worker/patron event risks and a longer finite survivor horizon. It then adds signed household medical, recovery-pay, wage and advocacy-cost effects. The old total is not preserved by reallocating a broad welfare envelope. Most of the gap between $28.5M and $67.6M comes from the weakly identified wage prior, not a new measured finding about ANRF. The full German-pay transport stress is adverse, not a favorable finite price.

**Scope and uncertainty.** Known absent protection zeroes its health and earnings routes; independent attempts can still impose known costs. Unavailable reach represented by a placeholder zero stays unknown. Unknown event risk cannot become numeric recovery cash just because its welfare weight is zero. The $25,000 software domain is a comparison limit, not verified available capacity or permission to scale linearly. The gross institutional companion adds a judged $25 of local implementation resources per protection-year, giving a $10,340 numerator and $69.9M comparison; this is neither donor cash nor complete net societal cost. Active-smoking cessation, lung cancer, housing displacement, smoking enjoyment and other portfolio effects remain outside this selected comparison, not demonstrated zero benefits or harms.

**Financial appendix.** Comparable national expenditures for FY2022–24 are **$3,455,347, $3,473,590 and $3,927,527**, averaging **$3,618,821** annually. FY2023 functional expense is $3,473,448 plus $142 of inventory direct cost. The latest year has revenue $3,789,343 and net assets $567,050; program fees total $592,548, including data $85,070, fee-for-service $169,096 and technical assistance $338,382. These are targeted original filing checks, not consolidated audited affiliate accounts. Current 2026 costs, unrestricted commitments and marginal capacity remain unverified; annual spending is an allocation proxy, not a gift price.
sections.funding:
The [ANRF donation form](https://no-smoke.salsalabs.org/anrf_donate/index.html), reached from its official site, solicits gifts for service continuity amid federal cuts. We verified a public giving route, not payment completion or a restricted restoration offer. The [July 2026 update](https://no-smoke.org/smokefree-lists-and-maps-july-1-2026/) reports fewer free lists/maps and paid quotes for specialized data. This supports a plausible use of flexible funds, but gives no marginal budget, hiring threshold or quantified protection effect. The [2024 return](https://no-smoke.org/wp-content/uploads/2024_ANRF_Form990.pdf) shows revenue $3,789,343, full expenses $3,927,527 and net assets $567,050. Program fees of $592,548 create a substitution question. Cumulative results and a deficit do not prove an additional gift is effective. Other funders, employers, unions, government staff and ANR may substitute or co-produce. We retain research-lead status; no verified marginal opportunity or qualified-pick claim.

The October recheck confirms current service-contraction and paid-data disclosures and separately verifies original FY2022–24 national IRS filings. Declining net assets and lost federal streams make a funding response plausible but do not identify its magnitude. Gifts might preserve services, replace fees or grants, or support new opportunities; a costed prospective ledger is needed to distinguish them. No current priced tranche, outreach, affiliate consolidation or donor-capacity claim is implied by this conditional model.

model.costScope: Full national charitable-recipient expense allocation for finite selected protection and household pathways. Donor cash remains numerator; local institutional resources are a separate partial gross diagnostic, household losses remain welfare debits. No verified whole-portfolio or marginal donor capacity.
model.geographicAttribution: g=.99 applies once to health and signed household resource flows, including attempts. USA includes50states/DC and tribal residents, excludes territories and foreign residents; residence is judged, not website/legal coverage.
model.formula: Initial=G/C*N*a*f*dp*e. Year t protection=initial*(retention*cohortSurvival)^(t-1), discounted at lag+t; clinical risk reversal ramps min(1,t/4). Health sums mutually exclusive fatal/nonfatal clinical event value minus independent harm. Explicit worker/event cash states receive separate signed logarithmic increments; attempts remain independent of policy success. Price=10*G/(health+resources) only when combined is known positive.
model.counterfactual: Only unique previously exposed nonsmokers whose protection changes relative to other actors, voluntary employer action, already scheduled policies and replacement funding. No additional cohorts per law/database user. Common-alive income only; actual paid household expense/net pay, not institutional billing or revenue.
model.attribution: Coalition probability, ANRF contribution, funding response, enforcement and retention are separate conditional judgments; their distinction does not establish identification. Separate affiliate costs/outcomes are not silently attributed. Worker/nonworker and event states are disjoint; positive recovery overlap never removes wage losses.
model.uncertainty: N25K and worker−.1% are scope/skeptical transport priors, not measured USA causal coefficients. Wage-null28.55M and small-positive18.10M should be read with67.58M center. Unknown reach zero placeholders remain unknown; known absent routes stay zero; independent attempts survive policy failure. Clinical uncertainty can leave known wages/attempts while event-dependent recovery cash stays unknown. Missing portfolio branches are not zero; software limits are not donor room.
model.nativeOutcomes: Per10K:3.4373 initial protected people,13.6187 discounted protection years,9.0342 clinical-ramp weighted exposure years,0.0003354 fatal and0.0008385 nonfatal USA event-equivalents avoided; health.0035041383 plus resources−.0020243951 yields.0014797432 combined equivalents.

annualExpenses.accountingBasis: Form 990 full recipient functional expenses plus identified netted direct costs

reports.priceScope: Smoke-free protection: health and household resources

historicalModel.costScope: Whole charitable recipient, including fundraising, administration, grants, data and education. One annual cost equivalent funds a prospective cohort with finite later benefits; P includes marginal funding response and portfolio allocation. Other ANR costs are not included or credited. The central ratio is donor support per health gain, not societal cost-effectiveness; a separate social-cost scenario adds implementation resources. No medical savings deducted.
historicalModel.geographicAttribution: N and P include all supported geography before applying g once. g=.99 is a judgment of resident health, not office location, statutory coverage, or measured allocation. Only 50 states/DC including tribal residents count in USA; territories and foreign residents do not.
historicalModel.formula: D=sum(t=1..T)[(retention*cohortSurvival)^(t-1)/(1+discount)^t]; L=sum(k=1..lifeYears)[utility*rescuedSurvival^k/(1+discount)^k]; P=N*dp*a*f*e*D; B=(rD*L+rM*qM)*excessRisk*exposureRemoval*transport-h; Pg=(G/(C*annualCostMultiplier))*P; Q_all=Pg*B; Q_USA=Q_all*g; costUSD=G+Pg*extraResourcePerPersonYear; costPer10=10*costUSD/Q_USA if Q_USA>0, otherwise null.
historicalModel.counterfactual: Count protection newly caused, preserved, or accelerated relative to public implementation, voluntary employer choices, other nonprofit work and replacement funding. dp is net coalition change, a allocates its ANRF share, and f is next-dollar capacity response; these are different uncertainties, not repeated discounts for the same fact. If the same prior already includes one factor, omit that factor. The hypothetical cohort must exclude overlapping laws and beneficiaries; no observed beneficiary ledger was available to verify deduplication. No repeated annual cohorts are assumed.
historicalModel.attribution: Neither database maintenance nor policy associations identify ANRF causal share. Health evidence is conditional on changed exposure. The 20% contribution and 50% funding response are explicitly judgmental. No credit to an affiliate’s work merely because branding is joint.
historicalModel.uncertainty: The central is a reasoned but highly speculative planning prior, not a fitted posterior or verified opportunity. Its reach and adoption inputs retain alpha continuity while finite protection and survival correct hidden durability assumptions. Research-lead only; zero and adverse scenarios remain. Most benefit comes from mortality extrapolation.
historicalModel.nativeOutcomes: Net additional, attributable, discounted years of smoke-free protection among previously exposed nonsmokers; conditional fatal and nonfatal coronary events avoided. No observed price per protected worker or successful law is available. Event values are discounted expected event equivalents because they inherit discounted protection years; they are not undiscounted event counts.

inputs.name: G
inputs.rationale: Disclosure normalization, not a package.

inputs.name: C
inputs.rationale: FY2024 functional expenses; Part VIII shows no additional netted direct costs.

inputs.name: N
inputs.unit: previously exposed nonsmokers across supported geography
inputs.rationale: Alpha planning cohort retained as a prior, not national coverage or a verified pipeline; ±10x tests.

inputs.name: dp
inputs.rationale: 50% judgment for a prospective collection of opportunities; subtract laws already scheduled, voluntary employer action and other actors.

inputs.name: a
inputs.unit: ANRF causal contribution conditional on coalition change
inputs.rationale: 20% allows for affiliate, public bodies, unions and other nonprofits; do not add ANR or coalition outcomes again.

inputs.name: f
inputs.rationale: 50% allows contract replacement, donor substitution and portfolio dilution; observed cuts motivate possible response, not this number.

inputs.name: e
inputs.rationale: 90% effective exposure-protection coverage; separate from degree of SHS risk removed.

inputs.name: T
inputs.rationale: Five-year finite horizon. Acceleration gets only years gained; one-year scenario.

inputs.name: retention
inputs.rationale: 95%; includes reversal and lost compliance; not an observed ANRF estimate.

inputs.name: cohortSurvival
inputs.unit: annual survival in protected risk set
inputs.rationale: 99%; no mortality benefit credited to members no longer alive.

inputs.name: discount
inputs.rationale: 3% year-end discounting on exposure years and event-conditional later health; distinct time intervals.

inputs.name: rD
inputs.unit: unexposed fatal coronary event risk per person-year
inputs.rationale: 0.001 retained from alpha; not observed among ANRF beneficiaries and may overstate younger-worker risk.

inputs.name: rM
inputs.unit: unexposed nonfatal coronary event risk per person-year
inputs.rationale: 0.002 retained; mutually exclusive fatal/nonfatal event branches.

inputs.name: excessRisk
inputs.unit: relative excess coronary risk from SHS
inputs.rationale: 0.25 informed by CDC coronary-disease association; transfer to fatal and nonfatal events is an assumption.

inputs.name: exposureRemoval
inputs.unit: fraction of excess SHS risk removed
inputs.rationale: 0.5 allows residual home and other exposures; cotinine reduction is not treated as linear health-risk reduction.

inputs.name: transport
inputs.rationale: 0.5; discounts immediate/full risk reversal and inconsistent US evidence. Not estimated by any cited study.

inputs.name: lifeYears
inputs.rationale: 15 finite years; no lifetime horizon. Vary jointly with baseline risk for younger/older cohorts.

inputs.name: rescuedSurvival
inputs.unit: annual subsequent survival after avoided fatal event
inputs.rationale: 0.97; allows competing mortality, distinct from survival to policy-year entry.

inputs.name: utility
inputs.rationale: 0.85; neither symptom study nor mortality study measured this utility.

inputs.name: qM
inputs.unit: discounted QALYs lost per nonfatal event
inputs.rationale: 0.3 retained alpha assumption, defined here as total discounted loss over at most three years, not a perpetual annual decrement; no overlap with fatal events.

inputs.name: h
inputs.rationale: 0.00002; illustrative displacement/enforcement penalty, not a measured bound.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: share of modeled health accruing to 50 states/DC residents
inputs.rationale: 0.99 retained alpha prior; apply once after all-population effects. Tribal residents included; territories and foreign residents excluded.

inputs.name: extraResourcePerPersonYear
inputs.unit: USD external implementation resources per net protected year
inputs.rationale: Zero in donor-only central; $100 sensitivity is explicitly social cost, not verified employer expense.

inputs.name: annualCostMultiplier
inputs.rationale: One central funds one opportunity cohort; five-year repeat-funding scenario if future support is required. No claim continued maintenance is free.

At central clinical yield, $1m per10 USA QALYs requires at most $52.20 per net protected person-year. This is a threshold, not a forecast.

Finite five-year protection and conditional fifteen-year rescued survival replace rounded exposure duration and the unexplained ten-QALY mortality value. No policy benefits extend beyond T, although an averted event within T can have subsequent finite health benefits.
No mortality credit, no clinical transport and high downside cases challenge the dominant health pathway. Nonpositive QALYs have null finite cost per10; do not display a fabricated positive price.
