model.costScope: Two years of full FY 2025 audited recipient resources, including all programs, administration, fundraising and donated services. Separate c4 excluded. Regulatory agency and corporate compliance spending disclosed but not included in recipient cost.
model.geographicAttribution: Only domestic resident health in the EPA PM pathway is quantified, so g=1 by model scope. No overseas, territorial, biodiversity or global climate health credit is included. This is not an organization-wide USA allocation.
model.formula: C=2*183685874. Y(L,start)=sum(i=0..L-1)1/1.03^(start+i). Q_USA=Q_all=D*m*q*Y*p*a*b-H. D=(2100+4500)/2=3300 central; the two EPA mortality studies are alternatives, not additive. q is discounted lifetime health per death including cessation lag to the exposure year; Y discounts exposure years to2026. Price=10*C/Q_USA when positive.
model.counterfactual: Current 9µg/m3 standard, June 2026 defense victory and July 2026 designation order remain in baseline. L is the extra full-equivalent exposure protection secured by future implementation work, not all protection under the rule. p is coalition incremental chance of achieving that addition, with existing statutory duties and state/local litigation continuing.
model.attribution: Earthjustice is one of several important legal contributors. a=.2 subjective share of incremental coalition contribution, not share of all rule benefits. b=.5 discounts reserves, existing support, fee recovery and replacement gifts. A successful future case does not establish these values retrospectively.
model.uncertainty: Very-low-confidence partial expected-value assessment. Clinical mechanism is stronger than marginal policy attribution. The midpoint of two regulatory forecasts is judgment, not a posterior estimate; broad scenarios are not confidence intervals. Remaining recipient pathways can add benefits or harms, precluding a whole-recipient ranking from this number.
model.nativeOutcomes: Legally effective implementation, additional emissions/exposure reductions, full-equivalent protected exposure years, adult deaths prevented and discounted lifetime QALYs. Court orders, case counts, acres and tonnes are not themselves QALYs.

inputs.name: C
inputs.unit: USD, two annual full recipient budgets
inputs.rationale: Judgment extrapolation to two years at the observed annual recipient expense: 2×FY 2025 audited expense. Two-year support horizon is judgment; donated services included.

inputs.name: D
inputs.unit: modeled adult deaths avoided per 2032-equivalent protected year
inputs.rationale: Midpoint of alternative EPA 2100 and 4500 estimates, not their sum or a pooled clinical estimate. Baseline assumes current 12/35 standard; identified controls for revised 9/35, not all possible attainment benefits.

inputs.name: m
inputs.rationale: Allows uncertain composition, adherence, changing emissions and residual confounding; .3–1 scenarios. Not an EPA parameter.

inputs.name: q
inputs.unit: QALYs per avoided adult death, discounted to exposure year
inputs.rationale: Composite of remaining survival, health quality, competing mortality and cessation lag. Broad 1–10 range; not EPA VSL divided by a QALY price. An older-adult dominated benefit cannot be valued as a young person's full lifespan.

inputs.name: L
inputs.unit: full-equivalent years of pollution protection conditional on incremental success
inputs.rationale: One year of avoided delay or equivalent retained exposure reduction; favorable 3. Does not count an indefinite standard or July 2026 victory again.

inputs.name: start
inputs.unit: years from 2026 to first modeled exposure year
inputs.rationale: 2032 reference-year controls; later timing tested. Native benefits are not observed 2026 outcomes.

inputs.name: r
inputs.rationale: Y discounts exposure timing. q already includes within-person lifetime and cessation-lag discounting.

inputs.name: p
inputs.unit: incremental coalition probability of securing protection beyond baseline
inputs.rationale: Subjective 10-percentage-point implementation contribution, not raw court win probability. Existing binding order and legal duties sharply constrain available additional credit.

inputs.name: a
inputs.unit: Earthjustice share of incremental coalition contribution
inputs.rationale: Counsel with important technical/client capacity, but state/local plaintiffs, CATF, SELC and other groups can substitute. .05–.5 scenarios; no equal division or sole credit.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: Growth plans support capacity use, but reserve funding and replacement gifts can preserve existing commitments. .1–.8 scenarios; no measured marginal staffing-to-outcome response.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: USA share of this quantified domestic branch
inputs.rationale: The model intentionally includes only US resident effects in EPA domestic analysis. This is not a claim that all Earthjustice work or all global benefits are domestic.

inputs.name: H
inputs.rationale: Provisional zero, with explicit net-harm case. Energy-cost/access effects, implementation displacement and litigation downside not measured.

inputs.name: otherPathways
inputs.unit: net QALYs from all other recipient work
inputs.rationale: MATS, chemicals, water, habitat, climate, other clean-air cases and nonfatal PM effects unpriced; avoid overlaps and policy-output conversions.

sensitivity: At $367,371,748 cost, $1 million/$100 thousand per 10 requires 3673.71748/36737.1748 net USA QALYs, versus 103.63868 centrally.

With q=5 and other central values, the $1 million threshold requires about 35.45 times the central product of protected years and incremental contribution. One favorable parameter alone need not achieve it.
Using only the 2100 or 4500 mortality alternatives changes central health by 2100/3300 or 4500/3300. These are not confidence bounds; uncertainty also includes model transport and exposure changes.

Using the three-year mean reduces cost about 7.8%. Excluding all donated services from latest expense reduces cost 9.15%, but omits real legal resources and public-service advertising; neither adjustment solves marginal attribution.
A delay from 2032 to 2036 reduces benefits by 1/1.03^4. q includes post-exposure cessation lag; do not count all modeled deaths as immediate.
All-population harm above 103.63868 QALYs erases the central partial benefit. Zero future implementation effect gives no finite positive price.
A portfolio sum must de-duplicate PM effects of MATS, power-plant, permitting and ambient-standard cases before adding them. Historic successes are not new-donation yield.

what: CBE combines community organizing, scientific research and litigation to reduce pollution in California communities.
Its work includes Exide cleanup and refinery disputes in Los Angeles, alongside substantial Bay Area and statewide activity.
A judgment-based partial-health central estimate is about $75.5 million per 10 LA/Orange QALYs; it is not an observed return or a donor-ready recommendation.
strengths: Current primary documents identify concrete cleanup barriers, including access to multi-family properties.
Legal, scientific and resident knowledge can complement government cleanup capacity.
Original financial returns identify the full recipient cost rather than only a selected campaign budget.
reservations: Policy probability, exposed population, dose reduction and marginal funding response are judgment inputs, with no verified next-dollar work plan; zero or harm remains possible.
The effect of remaining soil remediation on local blood lead and clinical outcomes is not measured here.
Statewide activity and coalition overlap prevent allocating all recipient benefits to Los Angeles.

sections.what:
CBE, EIN 94-2998086, operates in Southeast Los Angeles and Wilmington as well as East Oakland and Richmond. Ordinary support funds organizing, science, legal work, education and statewide initiatives. Its current support page reports more than 10,000 community members, 530 meetings annually and over 70 staff; these are scale claims, not health outcomes. The donation page explicitly identifies the recipient and EIN. [Recipient and operations](https://www.cbecal.org/donate/)

The current refinery portfolio includes Long Beach storage expansion, Paramount/Altair conversion, national hydrogen-fluoride regulation and statewide fuel-policy litigation. Several cases involve Earthjustice, East Yard or other counsel; activity and shared representation do not identify a sole causal owner. [Current cases](https://www.cbecal.org/initiative/refineries/)

In August 2026 CBE launched a two-year, ten-organization statewide climate-adaptation cohort supported by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation. That is current implementation capacity, but the announcement does not identify additional cooling/smoke protection, utilization or clinical effects. Existing foundation support belongs in the funding counterfactual. [CACHE launch](https://www.cbecal.org/news/post/10-community-led-orgs-launch-statewide-climate-adaptation-efforts/)
sections.monitoring:
CBE's March 2026 letter recognizes progress on Exide cleanup while requesting better owner participation, retrospective sampling and state/federal contingency planning. It also identifies delayed technical-assistance grants and problems at other contaminated sites. These are plausible actionable bottlenecks, but the letter does not count additional homes cleaned because of CBE or report residents' health changes. [Current intervention](https://www.cbecal.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/CBEs-Comment-Letter-on-the-Board-of-Environmental-Safety-Evaluation-of-DTSC.pdf)

The March legislative briefing says over 6,000 high-priority properties had been cleaned by end-2025 and describes remaining contaminated parcels and proposed new funding. It requests $70 million in each of two fiscal years, yet separately describes $70 million for about 1,000 parcels. That internal cost/scope ambiguity means neither $70,000 nor $140,000 is presented as a verified marginal cleanup price. The proposal is not treated as enacted funding. [Primary budget record, p. 36](https://sbud.senate.ca.gov/system/files/2026-03/agenda-mar19-calepa-3.16.pdf)

Useful monitoring would link otherwise-inaccessible households to actual access, completed remediation, sustained environmental and blood-lead changes, age-specific exposure duration and clinical outcomes. Measure what happens later without the additional advocacy, not only treatment versus no cleanup ever.
sections.qualitative:
The mechanism is biologically credible but heterogeneous. A Boston randomized trial of 152 young children with much higher baseline soil lead found roughly 1.5–1.9 micrograms/dL greater blood-lead declines from soil abatement than comparison interventions. Its median baseline soil concentration was 2,075 ppm; that is not directly portable to the lower-concentration Exide parcels now being considered. [Original trial](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/article-abstract/405094)

The later HOME randomized trial enrolled 355 pregnancies and followed children through age eight. It reduced dust lead but found no statistically significant overall blood-lead reduction and no substantive neurobehavioral improvement; a subgroup had greater exposure reduction. This is not evidence that all remediation fails, but it makes a universal QALY-per-house assumption unsafe. Neither soil ppm nor an IQ/earnings estimate is silently converted to QALYs. [Original HOME trial](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamapediatrics/fullarticle/2696978)

The refinery air pathway is more directly modelable clinically: AQMD's draft assessment reports PM-related deaths and morbidity, rather than only tonnes or monetized benefits. However, Rule 1109.1 was adopted in 2021, with implementation scheduled over subsequent years. The historical total is not a new donor's impact. No current CBE-specific change to remaining compliance, associated emissions or LA/Orange exposure was established. [Native table](https://www.aqmd.gov/docs/default-source/rule-book/Proposed-Rules/1109.1/1109-1-draft-socioeconomic-impact-assessment-090721-merged.pdf?sfvrsn=10) [Adoption](https://www.aqmd.gov/home/research/pubs-docs-reports/newsletters/jan-feb-2022/refinery-rule)

Community voice, accountability and environmental justice can matter independently of health. Cleanup can also create dust, displacement or exported waste burdens. These are not presumed zero merely because clinical quantification is absent.

A more geographically analogous smelter-cleanup study in Omaha found lower elevated blood-lead odds in several models, but no intervention association in its fully adjusted difference-in-differences model. The authors caution that remediation and measurement timing were highly correlated. This strengthens the case for local longitudinal measurement rather than selecting only a favorable before/after result. [Original researchers' summary](https://assessments.epa.gov/risk/document/&deid=354467)
sections.cost:
Original returns report full recipient expenses of $4,803,145 (2022), $6,001,139 (2023) and $7,882,417 (2024); the mean is $6,228,900.33. No reported separately netted event/inventory costs require restoration. [Original 2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/942998086/202523219349326347/full)

The central model charges five full budgets at the latest annual expense, not only a selected campaign cost. Technical/legal and organizing capacity changes the probability of additional enforceable refinery/fuel-related emissions controls beyond existing permits and Rule 1109.1. Current World Oil and Paramount disputes establish a live mechanism, not the assumed probability or PM reduction. HF accident prevention, soil lead, Bay Area activity and non-health justice value are not converted to PM mortality.

Conditional on an additional policy increment, 250,000 older residents experience 0.3 micrograms/m³ less annual ambient PM2.5. A 8% recipient-specific increase in that policy probability over the five-year effort and 35% marginal funding response are judgments, not measured attribution. The funding response allows for reserves and replacement gifts; coalition contribution is already inside the probability change and is not discounted twice. The assumed exposed cohort is alive at implementation, three years after model start.

Using the external HR 1.06 per 10 micrograms/m³, a 0.7 log-risk transport factor, annual baseline mortality hazard 0.035 and survivor utility 0.75, integrate competing all-cause survival curves for ten years and discount at 3%. Half the modeled effect is durable within that window; half is three-year acceleration of an otherwise identical policy. Acceleration retains only the finite survival difference versus delayed implementation. No lifetime QALYs are appended. All inputs beyond the external study estimate and financial accounts are judgments. [External clinical study](https://xiaowu.io/publication/wu2020evaluating/wu2020evaluating.pdf)

The $10,000 normalization yields 0.0013250 local QALYs and $75,471,532 per 10. Favorable and poor joint scenarios give $516,735 and $3,795,077,413,953 per 10; they are sensitivity cases, not confidence limits. Zero and net-harm cases have no finite beneficial price. This is a partial-health estimate: omitted pathways have zero net central contribution by judgment, not proven absence of benefit or harm. Public implementation, regulated-facility, volunteer and partner resources are additional unpriced social costs; this is not an all-resource societal cost-effectiveness estimate.
sections.funding:
The 2024 return reports revenue of $8,062,410, year-end cash of $5,989,690 and unrestricted net assets of $5,964,296. These balances do not prove that every asset is freely deployable today, but they weaken an assumption of immediate one-for-one expansion from an additional gift. Expense grew about 31% from 2023, while the return records 83 employees during the year; headcount is not full-time equivalents. [Original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/942998086/202523219349326347/full)

A useful next-dollar case would specify otherwise-unfunded organizers or technical/legal capacity, the affected cleanup queue or enforceable emissions change, and why reserves, agency outreach, other funders or partner groups would not replace it. Current broad fundraising claims do not provide that marginal work plan. [Support page](https://www.cbecal.org/donate/) The current jobs page lists no available positions; that is a website observation, not proof that the organization lacks useful work or cannot expand. [Current vacancies](https://www.cbecal.org/get-involved/jobs/)

model.costScope: Five full latest-year gross reported recipient budgets, across all programs and support, normalized linearly to a $10,000 ordinary gift. No policy-only cost carveout. External social resources unpriced.
model.geographicAttribution: Only health within Los Angeles and Orange counties (FIPS 06037, 06059) is counted. The 250,000 older adults are an analyst-selected conditional exposure cohort, not an office-count allocation or observed participant total. Riverside and San Bernardino outcomes are excluded. allPopulationQalys equals local quantified branch only, not an assumption that the whole portfolio is local.
model.formula: h1=h0*exp(-ln(HR)/10*transport*pm); rho=ln(1.03); F(a,t)=(1-exp(-a*t))/a. qD=u*(F(h1+rho,T)-F(h0+rho,T)). a=min(A,T). qT=u*(F(h1+rho,a)-F(h0+rho,a)+(1-exp(-(h0-h1)*a))*(exp(-(h1+rho)*a)-exp(-(h1+rho)*T))/(h1+rho)). q=(f*qD+(1-f)*qT)/1.03^L. Qgift=10000/(E*Y)*b*(p*N*q-harm). Price=100000/Qgift if positive. N is cohort alive at implementation; no extra survival-to-implementation multiplier. Costs are constant-real full budgets; no cost discount haircut.
model.counterfactual: Already-completed properties, adopted air rules, public cleanup appropriations and work by regulators, residents and partner organizations continue without the marginal support. Acceleration must count only the exposure interval gained, not lifetime no-cleanup benefit. Technical/legal and organizing capacity changes the probability of additional enforceable refinery/fuel-related emissions controls beyond existing permits and Rule 1109.1. Current World Oil and Paramount disputes establish a live mechanism, not the assumed probability or PM reduction. HF accident prevention, soil lead, Bay Area activity and non-health justice value are not converted to PM mortality.
model.attribution: p is the incremental recipient-specific probability effect of a five-year whole-organization effort versus partner/regulator action without it. b models donation-sensitive capacity after replacement funding, distinct from coalition p. Local linear extrapolation to a small gift is judgment and can fail at lumpy capacity thresholds.
model.uncertainty: Explicit judgment central, not identified causal charity effectiveness. Wide scenarios include clinical-null, no-policy-effect and harm. This is not a complete portfolio estimate or a reason to override donor diligence.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional annual ambient PM2.5 exposure reduction among an explicitly modeled older cohort; finite discounted all-cause survival differences, without adding overlapping mortality/morbidity or lead/IQ units.

what: East Yard organizes residents around pollution, transportation, housing stability, youth leadership and local food systems in eastern and southern Los Angeles County.
Its community-academic lead study helped change cleanup oversight; current work also addresses port emissions and a proposed resilience hub.

sections.what:
East Yard, EIN 46-5685097, is a community-based environmental justice organization. Its membership areas include East LA, Boyle Heights, Long Beach and Southeast LA cities, all within LA County. It also participates in statewide and regional coalitions, so its total health footprint is not automatically 100% within the LA+Orange boundary. [Membership geography](https://eycej.org/index.php/about/membership/)

The recipient includes tenant organizing, youth and leadership work, community research, composting, gardening and pollution advocacy. La Cosecha's garden builds and produce exchange may support well-being; its traditional-remedy workshops are cultural/educational activities, not assigned clinical efficacy or QALYs. [Programs](https://eycej.org/index.php/la-cosecha-colectiva/)

The official donation page links a Raisely campaign, but the fetched payment page did not expose a verifiable legal payee, so no donation button is asserted here. [Official route](https://eycej.org/index.php/donate/)
sections.monitoring:
The 2026 Get the Lead Out paper reports 1,128 soil samples from 373 properties, including 143 previously remediated homes. Sampling found 105 of those homes had at least one sample above 80 ppm. Recruitment used meetings, social media and outreach, with selected downwind neighborhoods prioritized; it was not a representative randomized audit. The study did not compare directly with original samples because methods differed, and cannot distinguish inadequate initial removal from recontamination on every property. [Original study and methods](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13085797/)

Importantly, the authors describe concrete subsequent changes: verification sampling in new contracts, a state-funded third-party monitor and expanded blood-lead testing access. Verification results were still forthcoming. These are credible intermediate outcomes, not proof of health effect or sole EYCEJ causation. Already-established oversight cannot be credited afresh to new support. [Study implementation discussion](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13085797/)

The older campaign page still describes waiting for an I-710 final EIR and other historic statuses; it is used to identify scope, not to date current milestones. Current agency documents show the ports agreement is already effective. [Campaign scope](https://eycej.org/index.php/campaigns/) [Current status](https://www.aqmd.gov/home/air-quality/air-quality-management-plans/air-quality-mgt-plan/facility-based-mobile-source-measures/comm-ports-wkng-grp/potential-cooperative-agreement-with-the-ports-of-long-beach-and-los-angeles)

A July 2026 suit names East Yard as a plaintiff in the Barstow International Gateway challenge. This is concrete current litigation, but the rail facility is in San Bernardino County, outside this edition. Potential effects along the LA–Barstow route require geographically resolved net traffic and emissions, not assigning all alleged project emissions to LA residents. [Counsel's case announcement](https://earthjustice.org/press/2026/lawsuit-challenges-approval-of-nations-largest-rail-facility-in-california)
sections.qualitative:
Lead remediation is a plausible health mechanism, but a reduction in soil concentration is not itself a QALY. The Boston randomized trial found blood-lead improvement at high baseline soil contamination; the later HOME trial found no significant overall blood-lead effect or substantive neurobehavioral improvement. These do not invalidate cleanup, but they require local exposure, age and persistence inputs before assigning a per-house clinical yield. The original trials were first reviewed in the CBE research interval and reused here, with EYCEJ-specific interpretation separately timed. [Boston trial](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/article-abstract/405094) [HOME trial](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamapediatrics/fullarticle/2696978)

Air pollution has a better-established mortality bridge: a large Medicare study found broadly consistent PM2.5 effects across several causal-inference approaches, subject to confounding and exposure-measurement assumptions. The missing link here is not whether polluted air can harm people, but the additional emissions and exposure changes that EYCEJ's marginal work would produce. [Original PM study](https://xiaowu.io/publication/wu2020evaluating/wu2020evaluating.pdf)

The September 10, 2026 port addendum adds ship and zero-emission truck incentives plus $40 million total off-port charging/fueling funding. Truck-program approval is due February 28, 2027, with possible extensions. Participation goals and quantified benefits remain to be developed; the agreement explicitly acknowledges uptake is beyond the ports' control. The off-port fund covers the South Coast basin, not just LA+Orange. [Actual addendum](https://www.aqmd.gov/docs/default-source/ports-ca/addendum-to-ports-ca_final-approved-sept-2026.pdf?sfvrsn=a4db637e_2)

East Yard was part of the coalition contesting the earlier port proposal and joined the May 2026 demand for refinery monitoring during decommissioning. These establish active roles; neither a letter nor a monitor establishes avoided exposure without an ensuing action. Coalition credit must not be duplicated across EYCEJ, CBE, CCA, Earthjustice and others. [Port coalition](https://www.aqmd.gov/docs/default-source/planning/fbmsm-docs/2025-10-01-final-scaqmd-gov-board-ltr-re-draft-cooperative-agreement.pdf?sfvrsn=eaaa6c7e_2) [Monitoring coalition](https://www.aqmd.gov/docs/default-source/rule-book/proposed-rules/rule-1180-and-1180.1/2026/comment-letters/2026-05-11-coalition.pdf?sfvrsn=cc32677e_2)

The new central scenario assumes a three-year organizing effort has a 20% chance of improving implementation beyond adopted commitments enough to reduce PM2.5 by 0.1 microgram per cubic meter for 100,000 older adults for five years. Neither that exposure footprint nor the success probability is measured or source-calibrated. EYCEJ receives 10% of coalition contribution and a 25% marginal funding response. This is a transparent judgment scenario, not an agency forecast. A closed-cohort survival integral follows the cohort for ten years, with mortality hazard returning to baseline after year five and no benefit after year ten. This avoids repeated lifetime credits for the same people. Lead cleanup, housing, gardens and the proposed hub remain unpriced.
sections.cost:
Full 2024 recipient cost is $1,562,510: reported functional expense of $1,539,414 plus $23,096 of event costs netted against revenue. The functional split is $1,256,380 program, $195,000 administration and $88,034 fundraising. Comparable 2023 and amended 2022 totals are $1,118,780 and $1,030,737, with no reported netted event/inventory adjustments; the three-year mean is $1,237,342. These are original accrual returns; an independent audit is indicated in the latest return but was not recovered. [2024](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/465685097/202512769349301586/full) [2023](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/465685097/202433179349305163/full) [2022](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/465685097/202421919349301957/full)

At the latest annual cost, $100,000 per 10 LA QALYs requires 156.251 net additional QALYs; $1 million per 10 requires 15.6251. For an air-mortality pathway, an illustrative 5 discounted QALYs per death would require 31.25 or 3.13 expected additional LA deaths avoided, after all coalition and funding adjustments. This is a decision threshold, not a claim that East Yard achieves those totals.

The conditional air component uses three annual full recipient budgets, $4,687,530. It yields 0.254947 LA QALY, about $183.86 million per 10. A favorable joint case is about $451,475 per 10; a weak case exceeds $13 trillion per 10. These are judgment stress cases, not confidence limits.

The scenario assumes better use of already-committed implementation resources. Any additional vehicles, chargers, monitoring or operating resources must be added for a social-cost price; the $40 million already committed is not created by a new gift. Hub capital and benefits are excluded.
sections.funding:
The 2024 return reports $4,238,201 cash, $3,651,369 other investments and $7,318,249 unrestricted net assets, compared with about $1.56 million annual full cost. These assets may be designated or intended for long-term commitments; unrestricted accounting is not evidence of immediate availability. Nevertheless, assuming every additional dollar expands current operations would be weak. [Original balance sheet](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/465685097/202512769349301586/full)

The June 2026 transition announcement specifically seeks capital-campaign support to replace a freight-focused warehouse with a community resilience hub. It provides no acquisition price, funding gap, operating plan or number of protected heat/smoke-exposure hours. The July update identifies Laura Cortez as current executive director as Taylor Thomas transitions out; old co-director listings are not used as current governance evidence. [Current transition and capital plan](https://eycej.org/index.php/blog/blog/)

East Yard has concrete local accountability evidence, but this highly assumption-sensitive component does not establish a whole-portfolio health-cost-effectiveness recommendation. The decisive diligence is a marginal operating/capital plan tied to verified extra exposure protection, with public funding and partner substitution explicitly separated. Clean Energy Group's historical 2021 award supported microgrid/community-solar capacity and advocacy; it does not establish that the proposed 2026 hub is operating or that its capital gap is known. [Original funder record](https://www.cleanegroup.org/initiatives/resilient-power-leadership-initiative/awards/)

what: Vital Access Care Foundation offers Vietnamese-language cancer and hepatitis screening, navigation and patient support in Orange County, inside the LA metro area.
It also connects residents to food, insurance and public-benefit services; its 2024 return reports 2,499 mixed screening/vaccination activities and 282 cancer patients assisted.
It helps residents navigate medical care in their own language, including hepatitis B services where timely follow-up can prevent serious liver disease.
strengths: Bilingual screening and navigation can turn an otherwise missed infection into monitoring, treatment or vaccination.
An established local service network reaches residents facing language and access barriers; completed care has a credible clinical mechanism.
Original returns establish a real operating recipient, and the historical community study supports a relevant hepatitis burden.
reservations: Current unique hepatitis tests, completed treatment and incremental cancer-stage outcomes are not reported.
The clinical transfer and resource ledger are explicit judgments; partner, public-payer and other portfolio effects remain unpriced.
Large unrestricted reserves and recent surpluses leave the next ordinary gift's service expansion uncertain.

sections.what: The [current programs](https://www.vacf.org/programs) include cancer and hepatitis screening, care navigation, medication assistance, peer support, food distribution and public-benefit enrollment. The [current organization page](https://www.vacf.org/about) locates services in Fountain Valley, Orange County, within the current LA–Long Beach–Anaheim metro boundary. The legal recipient is Vital Access Care Foundation dba Vietnamese American Cancer Foundation, EIN 91-2170415; the official site links its donation route.
sections.monitoring: The 2024 return reports 2,499 combined screenings/vaccinations and 282 cancer patients assisted; these are outputs, not lives saved. The current website's 2025 impact heading links an image whose filename still says 2024; the image shows 3,750 screening/prevention activities. We use the dated return cohort, not that ambiguously labeled image, for numerical scale. VACF's [2019 HBV study](https://www.vacf.org/_files/ugd/dd68d6_5174bf64856744a4af4985d3f0c2c316.pdf) found 225 current infections among 2,508 participants but explicitly lacked information on completed necessary care. Improved monitoring would publish unique tests by disease, prior diagnosis, confirmatory results, referral completion and treatment/vaccination outcomes. No current controlled cancer-stage, completed HBV-treatment or additional-income outcome was verified. Screening, infectious testing and vaccination totals cannot be treated as unique completed treatment. For the conditional reference, 25% of mixed activities are judged HBV opportunities and 80% unique service participants; their appropriateness is separately stress-tested. No raw screen is valued as a life saved.
sections.qualitative: Bilingual outreach and navigation can reduce missed diagnoses and improve linkage. The [Chahal clinical model](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6346293/) gives 23.861 discounted lifetime QALYs for the inclusive Asian/Pacific-Islander offer versus 23.780 without intervention: 0.081, not the table's sequential 0.007. This is modeled clinical evidence, not a VACF evaluation. Its disease progression, treatment response and finite lifetime are included once; no recurring lifetime copies or survivor earnings are added. The retained 0.25 transfer prior covers age/cascade mismatch and is not an observed treatment-completion probability. [CDC screening guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/72/rr/rr7201a1.htm) supports screening linked to appropriate care, but ordinary medical access is an alternative. [Every Woman Counts](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/every-woman-counts/) supplies free eligible breast/cervical screening and treatment referrals, including Vietnamese-language assistance; VACF cannot claim all partner-paid care as its additional effect. Broader cancer support, food security, research and training remain unknown rather than assigned arbitrary health or wage values.
sections.cost:
Original 2024 full-recipient expenses are $2,205,208: $2,153,424 program, $49,846 management and $1,938 fundraising. Separately netted event costs are zero; no rental, gaming or inventory expense addback was found. The 2022–24 expense mean is $1,531,013.33, used only as a cost sensitivity, not matched historical outputs. The annual-funded-work equivalent assigns 25% capacity expansion to an ordinary gift, giving 124.95 incremental service people; all incur modeled costs even if care or clinical benefit fails. Health remains 1.2018628125 LA QALYs. Signed household resources subtract 0.1312803504 welfare equivalents, yielding 1.0705824621 combined equivalents and $20.60 million per ten, versus the initial diagnostic's $18.35 million health-only estimate. A $10,000 gift corresponds to about 0.5666 incremental service people, 0.00545 clinical QALYs and −0.0005953 income equivalents, conditional on linear capacity. This is a partial recipient-funded component, not complete social EV or a marginal-gift queue observation.

Resource branches are mutually exclusive household outcomes, not separately added gains for the same family. The central reference assumes one unique service participant per distinct household and weights one welfare person per household. Other family-member welfare is unpriced; no conversion of unique participants into households by dividing by family size is used. Household baseline disposable resources are judged $30,000, compatible with—not estimated by—the historical low-income population. Every incremental screening household incurs $50 net time/travel cost. A 12.5% resource-care branch has $300 net resource relief or baseline-alive work preservation, discounted for 50% positive health overlap, minus $200 treatment/work disruption and the full $50 common cost: −$100. A disjoint 5% false-alarm branch loses $250; the remaining 82.5% loses $50. Taxes, benefit withdrawal, avoided bills, work disruption and replacement care must be netted inside these amounts; they are not measured separate gains. One household-year is counted, never survivor wages. Partner-payer stress separately assigns $1,459 or $5,000 per reference-equivalent clinical offer across 100 disjoint payer persons at $50,000 baseline, as one-year fiscal opportunity-cost losses. The $1,459 is the external model's inclusive-versus-no-intervention medical-cost difference, not current VACF costs or observed taxpayer incidence; fiscal opportunity cost and incidence are unknown in central. Three-year stress means recurrent care costs and resources each year, not repeated one-time screening cost asserted as fact. Private-provider margin and insurer/public-payer incidence are unknown, not factual zero; ±$25 per service counterparty stresses use ten disjoint one-person owner households at $60,000 baseline. Other local/nonlocal patient and partner burdens are unpriced. Thus the headline is explicitly partial, not total household resources or complete world benefit.
sections.funding: The [2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/912170415/202523219349307047/full) reports revenue of $3,252,848, a $1,047,640 surplus, $4,035,365 cash and $4,049,616 net assets without donor restrictions. Government grants are blank in Part VIII, which does not prove absence of publicly supported partner care. The [program page](https://www.vacf.org/programs) explicitly connects patients to Every Woman Counts and other assistance. An ordinary gift may support the entire expanded portfolio or reserves; no verified cash-only service queue was found. Funding responsiveness is therefore a judgment, not an observed grant-to-treatment conversion. The 25% capacity response is a donor-response prior, not observed additional patients per dollar. Zero expansion has no new benefits or service costs; clinical null retains all new service burdens.

historicalAlphaModel.costScope: Full recipient annual 2024 Part IX expense, all programs/overhead; no selected-program denominator. Output denominator prices only HBV screening/care contribution. External clinical costs excluded and discussed separately.
historicalAlphaModel.geographicAttribution: LA MSA comprises Los Angeles and Orange counties. Historical study events were in both and current service focus is Orange County. g=.95 is judgment allowing nonresident beneficiaries, range .9–1, not measured residence share. National research spillovers are unpriced.
historicalAlphaModel.formula: Q_all=N*s*d*a*b*t*q_ref; Q_LA=g*Q_all; price=10*C/Q_LA. N=2499 mixed screening/vaccination activities; s=.25 HBV-related screening opportunities; d=.8 unique appropriate people; a=.5 incremental versus other care; b=.25 ordinary-funding responsiveness; t=.25 age/cascade transfer; q_ref=23.861−23.780=.081 discounted lifetime QALY per API screening-program offer from Chahal et al. Central Q_all=1.26511875 and Q_LA=1.2018628125. One annual-budget cohort only; never repeat lifetime benefit each year.
historicalAlphaModel.counterfactual: Without additional ordinary funding, existing grants/reserves and public/clinical providers continue. a removes HBV care that would occur anyway; b removes non-marginal funding or displacement. The reference model's no-intervention comparator is more favorable than contemporary care, so it is not copied directly.
historicalAlphaModel.attribution: s and d translate mixed reported outputs to candidate clinical opportunities; no multiplying 9% prevalence into a reference model that already includes infection prevalence. t is a joint transfer discount for older case mix and less complete care than reference; not an empirically calibrated completion probability. No independent cancer/food/navigation additions that could double-count the same people.
historicalAlphaModel.uncertainty: All organization-specific conversion factors are explicit subjective scenarios, not measured rates or confidence intervals. Partial component only. Low/high combine assumptions rather than statistical bounds; zero and small adverse effects remain possible.
historicalAlphaModel.nativeOutcomes: Central 624.75 candidate HBV activities, 499.8 unique appropriate opportunities, 249.9 incremental opportunities before funding, 62.475 funding-responsive opportunities and 15.61875 reference-program-equivalent offers. These fractional expected quantities are model constructs, not observed diagnoses, cures or beneficiaries.

inputs.name: C
inputs.rationale: Original full recipient expense.

inputs.name: N
inputs.rationale: Return does not split diseases or vaccines.

inputs.name: s
inputs.rationale: Hepatitis is established but current share unknown; .1–.5 scenarios.

inputs.name: d
inputs.rationale: Historical study had to remove duplicate participants; current dedup unknown.

inputs.name: a
inputs.rationale: Other medical care, prior diagnoses and contemporary screening reduce additionality.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: Substantial surplus/reserves; no verified immediate cash bottleneck.

inputs.name: t
inputs.rationale: Reference starts age 30; VACF serves many older residents and lacks completion follow-up.

inputs.name: q_ref
inputs.rationale: Published modeled (not empirical) API inclusive 23.861 minus no intervention 23.780; includes imperfect uptake, avoids inflating per actual test.

inputs.name: g
inputs.rationale: Local service focus with nonresident allowance; not office-location allocation.

reports.program: Perinatal mental-health training, access and peer support

acceptance.scope: Conditional finite training/peer component with signed household resources and explicit transfer/counterparty alternatives; not complete portfolio or verified marginal-gift EV.

what: Maternal Mental Health NOW trains health and social-service providers and offers culturally responsive perinatal peer support in LA County.
Its Sana Sana service provides weekly follow-up, resource navigation and free support groups; the organization became independent from Community Partners on July 1, 2025.
Through provider education and ongoing peer contact, it helps parents recognize distress and find appropriate support.
strengths: Better-equipped providers can identify distress and connect parents to appropriate clinical care.
Sana Sana offers ongoing, bilingual, affirming support rather than only a referral directory.
External randomized evidence supports plausible short-term clinical mechanisms, with uncertainty and differences in program intensity made explicit.
reservations: Training attendance and confidence do not establish completed care, patient caseload or causal health effects.
Current successor actual expenses and ordinary-gift expansion remain unverified; the transition return is not a full operating-cost measure.
Resource incidence, family spillovers and direct birthworker-transfer welfare are unmeasured; the combined price is a conditional partial reference.

sections.what: The [current mission and model](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/about-us/) combine provider training, stigma reduction and access to care. [Sana Sana](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/sana/) offers ongoing peer contact and resource navigation for LA County parents. The [FY25 impact report](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/MMHN-Impact-Report-FY25.pdf) dates independence from Community Partners to July 1, 2025; today’s gift is not a gift to all of the former sponsor’s projects.
sections.monitoring: The [donation page](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/donate/) reports 800+ trainees and 150 warmline callers during 2024–25. We do not add 300 support-group participants to callers because overlap and attendance definitions are unresolved. The [December 2025 Sana Sana white paper](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/MMHN-whitepaper-Dec2025-1.pdf) distinguishes repeated interactions from unique clients, reports low survey response, and describes weekly 30–60-minute support. Its billing projections are not actual reimbursement. Provider confidence and non-random differences between home-visitor and clinic screening are not causal health outcomes. Current fresh reporting confirms the counts but not deduplicated uptake or causal patient outcomes. The impact report additionally lists 500 warmline calls, which are not 500 unique parents, and $15,000 distributed to birthworkers, which is not earned income.
sections.qualitative: The [PoNDER economic analysis](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6518383/) found a small adjusted six-month QALY gain from intensive UK health-visitor training in lower-risk postpartum women; uncertainty included no health gain. Our training model retains only 10% of that reference effect before further additionality and funding reductions. A [Canadian peer-support trial](https://www.bmj.com/content/338/bmj.a3064) found less probable depression at 12 weeks in high-risk women, but no significant difference at 24 weeks after referral of severe cases. It supports short-term benefit, not permanent remission. [LAMMHA’s funder report](https://www.chcf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/CollaborativeCareModelImprovesMaternalMentalHealth.pdf) identifies MMHN as training coordinator within a larger clinical coalition; all clinical outcomes cannot be assigned to MMHN. Only positive clinical contributions receive the cross-route overlap factor; negative clinical outcomes remain full. Peer 12-week endpoint improvement is translated with a finite, judged benefit-area assumption, not counted as lifetime remission. Clinical-null and adverse cases retain participant burdens. Existing LAMMHA grants and services are baseline.
sections.cost:
The [FY25 impact report](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/MMHN-Impact-Report-FY25.pdf), page 18, reports a $1.17 million operating budget. This is a full-program continuation-year planning cost, not audited actual spending or a verified marginal service queue. The original successor 990-EZ reports $1,513 pre-operating expenses while the operating program remained with Community Partners through June 30, 2025; no sponsor-wide budget or tiny transition cost is substituted. Actual sponsor transfers, all transition overhead and current reserves are unknown. Cost sensitivities use $1.0 million and $1.5 million; no comparable three-year full-recipient mean is available.

Central clinical benefit remains 0.4402119119 LA QALYs. Signed net resources subtract 0.2023741876 healthy-year welfare equivalents, giving 0.2378377243 combined equivalents and about $49.19 million per ten, versus the initial $26.58 million health-only reference. A $10,000 gift's modeled share gives 0.00376249 clinical QALYs and -0.00172969 income equivalents. These are linear capacity priors, not observed delivered outcomes per gift.

The resource ledger distinguishes 800 training records from a judged 80% unique course-user share and a separate 50% clinically effective frontline share. At 50% capacity response and 80% local residence, 256 local course users incur four hours at $25/hour, with 25% uncompensated: a net $25 own-household burden each at $60,000 baseline. Employer-paid training time and clinical backfill are separate unknown institutional costs, not counted again as participant lost wages. All course-user costs survive clinical failure.

The judged clinical-workflow resource exposure is 10% of the 12,000 annual care opportunities times funding response and geography: 480 local parent households incur $10 net time, travel or childcare cost. This exposure prior is distinct from the 10% clinical-effect transfer. The 75 incremental peer households incur $60 each. One participant per distinct household and one welfare person are modeled; family income and welfare are unpriced. Half of peer households are judged also exposed to clinical workflow: 37.5 joint households lose $70, 442.5 workflow-only lose $10 and 37.5 peer-only lose $60. Each household nets resources before the log; no separate same-household benefit logs. Course users and parent households are assumed disjoint, not observed disjoint; overlap across professional and parent roles remains an uncertainty.

All amounts are net after taxes, benefits, replacement care and foregone-work offsets by assumption, not measured expenditures. There is no central income gain. Resource-relief stresses add $100 net baseline-alive work or bill relief once per household, discount only that positive portion for 50% health overlap, and retain all negative costs. No survivor earnings, gross salary or gross billing is treated as welfare. One annual cohort and one household-resource year are counted after a one-year delay at 3%. A two-year stress explicitly assumes recurrent resource exposure, not measured persistence.

Private provider margin and insurer/public-payer net resources remain unknown, not factual zero; the central neutral anchor is partial-boundary bookkeeping. Separate stresses apply $500 net partner fiscal cost per reference-equivalent offer across 100 disjoint payer persons at $50,000 baseline, and ±$100 private margin across ten one-person owner households at $60,000 baseline. These are illustrative, not source-observed incidence. The external NHS £82 saving is not patient cash and is not converted into QALYs or subtracted from donor cost. The reported $15,000 Black Birthworker Enrichment Fund distributions establish a transfer, but unknown recipients, additionality, offsets and funding counterparties prevent a complete net-welfare estimate; it remains unpriced alongside other family and policy outcomes.

Direct-transfer stress explicitly uses the observed $15,000 Enrichment Fund aggregate, but not observed recipient net income. At 50% capacity response, 50% further causal transfer additionality and 10% taxes/benefit/opportunity offsets, twenty distinct one-person recipient households receive $168.75 net each before 50% positive health-overlap discount ($84.375). These shares, household count and $30,000 baseline are judgments. The matched hypothetical funding counterparty loses the full $3,750 incremental amount across 100 disjoint one-person households at $100,000 baseline; an adverse incidence case lowers that baseline to $20,000. These are alternative institutional funding/incidence hypotheses, not donor utility losses or proven public funding for this fund. Central transfer incidence stays unknown/unpriced, not zero evidence. The disjoint-recipient hypothesis is explicit; a half-overlap case instead assigns ten recipients to the modeled course cohort, removes their course-only pathways and jointly nets fund receipt with their full $25 course burden at the same $60,000 household baseline. No gross fund cash is counted on top of an overlapping household log. The reported three of eight peer participants training as birthworkers is not a causal placement or earnings result. Negative resource changes receive no positive overlap discount; sign-guard cases preserve full losses.
sections.funding: The FY25 operating-budget graphic attributes 55% to foundations/corporate, 25% government, 15% earned income and 5% individuals. Public and philanthropic support already finances delivery. The [current LAMMHA page](https://ccalac.org/los-angeles-maternal-mental-health-access-lammha/) describes the 2022–26 coalition program, closed enrollment and clinic implementation grants; these belong in the baseline. The [Sana Sana paper](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/MMHN-whitepaper-Dec2025-1.pdf) examines prospective billing, not guaranteed revenue, and [DHCS](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal-peer-support-services/) confirms specialty-system peer support is a defined benefit rather than universal reimbursement for every peer interaction. Ordinary gifts may preserve uncovered capacity, replace other funding or fund administration; 50% marginal responsiveness is an explicit judgment. A post-transition budget, sponsor transfer reconciliation and cash runway would materially improve the estimate.

model.costScope: Full recipient program annual planning budget of $1.17m, not the $1,513 standalone pre-operation return and not former sponsor total. Modeled continuation year with current successor delivery assumed; actual full recipient expenses unverified. External clinical labor, insurer spending and participant time excluded from donor cost.
model.geographicAttribution: LA MSA is Los Angeles plus Orange counties. Sana Sana eligibility is LA County, so peer g=1. Training is available beyond LA and online; training beneficiary share .8 central (.5–.95) is judgment, not trainee/HQ location evidence. No global or state-policy spillovers added.
model.formula: QT=T*d*L*r*a*b*q; QP=P*peerUnique*e*rP*aP*b*u*w/52. Positive-only overlap H(x)=k*max(x,0)+min(x,0); QLA=[H(gT*QT)+H(QP)]/(1+discount)^delay. Course/resource exposure counts are independent of q/r clinical efficacy. Joint household signed net resources BEFORE log; income=.5*persons*discounted years*log(1+net/baseline). Price10=10*C/(QLA+income).
model.counterfactual: Current grants, commissioned training, other educators, clinical providers and referral services persist without the next ordinary gift. a and aP remove substitution by alternative training/support; b discounts donation-to-expanded/preserved service responsiveness. The 2022–26 LAMMHA grants and enacted screening laws are baseline, not fresh gift outcomes.
model.attribution: T is an output floor, d removes duplicate/non-frontline training records, L is a subjective annual unique lower-risk postpartum caseload per effective trainee, and r scales the intensive UK training reference to heterogeneous MMHN courses. Peer rP allows lower intensity and different risk profile than the high-risk RCT. k removes cross-route overlap. No additional LAMMHA, screening, group-attendance or awareness QALYs are layered onto these pathways.
model.uncertainty: Conditional partial estimate, not calibrated posterior or complete portfolio EV. External clinical uncertainty and all resource-incidence assumptions remain material. Complete unknown remains null; financial-only/clinical-null retains full household costs.
model.nativeOutcomes: Central annual modeled pipeline: 400 effective unique frontline trainees; 12,000 lower-risk care opportunities; 300 reference-equivalent training offers. Resource cohorts separately include 256 local course users, 480 workflow-exposed parents and 75 peer households, with 37.5 joint parent households. None is measured completed treatment. Clinical .4402119119 QALYs and signed income −.2023741876 equivalents.

historicalAlphaModel.costScope: Full recipient program annual planning budget of $1.17m, not the $1,513 standalone pre-operation return and not former sponsor total. Modeled continuation year with current successor delivery assumed; actual full recipient expenses unverified. External clinical labor, insurer spending and participant time excluded from donor cost.
historicalAlphaModel.geographicAttribution: LA MSA is Los Angeles plus Orange counties. Sana Sana eligibility is LA County, so peer g=1. Training is available beyond LA and online; training beneficiary share .8 central (.5–.95) is judgment, not trainee/HQ location evidence. No global or state-policy spillovers added.
historicalAlphaModel.formula: Q_training_all=T*d*L*r*a*b*q; Q_peer_all=P*e*rP*aP*b*u*(w/52). Q_LA=k*(gT*Q_training_all+Q_peer_all)/(1.03^delay); Q_all=k*(Q_training_all+Q_peer_all)/(1.03^delay); price=10*C/Q_LA. Central T800,d.5,L30,r.1,a.5,b.5,q.002; P150,e.11,rP.25,aP.5,u.1,w12;k.9,gT.8,delay1,C1170000. Training .6 all-pop QALYs and peer .02379808 before overlap/delay; final .54506628 all-pop and .4402119119 LA.
historicalAlphaModel.counterfactual: Current grants, commissioned training, other educators, clinical providers and referral services persist without the next ordinary gift. a and aP remove substitution by alternative training/support; b discounts donation-to-expanded/preserved service responsiveness. The 2022–26 LAMMHA grants and enacted screening laws are baseline, not fresh gift outcomes.
historicalAlphaModel.attribution: T is an output floor, d removes duplicate/non-frontline training records, L is a subjective annual unique lower-risk postpartum caseload per effective trainee, and r scales the intensive UK training reference to heterogeneous MMHN courses. Peer rP allows lower intensity and different risk profile than the high-risk RCT. k removes cross-route overlap. No additional LAMMHA, screening, group-attendance or awareness QALYs are layered onto these pathways.
historicalAlphaModel.uncertainty: Best-effort partial-health scenario, heavily judgment-driven; no empirically measured MMHN causal conversion. Positive scenarios are not confidence bounds. Reference training QALY CI includes zero; negative case retained. Full policy, anti-stigma, workforce and infant/family outcomes are unpriced, not known to be absent.
historicalAlphaModel.nativeOutcomes: Central training pipeline: 800 records→400 effective unique frontline trainees→12,000 unique lower-risk postpartum care opportunities→300 reference-equivalent opportunities after transfer/additionality/funding. Peer pipeline: 150 callers→9.375 high-risk RCT-equivalent participants after transfer/additionality/funding→1.03125 fewer probable-depression cases at 12 weeks, translated with .1 utility×12/52 year. These are expected model quantities, not observed treated cases. No infant mortality or lifetime recurrence multiplier.

sensitivity: The positive low/high scenarios are stress tests, not calibrated probability quantiles; training caseload and clinical implementation dominate. Zero additional funding response yields zero benefit.

The original training Table 5 QALY difference is .002 with 95% CI−.001 to .004. Cost-saving probability is not a 99% probability of improved health; NHS cost savings are not subtracted from this donor numerator.

Training benefit ends at six-month follow-up for each modeled parent, with only one annual cohort. Peer benefit is .1 utility for 12 weeks per incremental probable-depression case; no persistence beyond 24 weeks assumed. The peer benefit area is a subjective scenario, not the trial's measured duration of improvement.

At the central $1.17m budget, $1m/10 requires 11.7 LA QALYs; $100k/10 requires 117. Central modeled component=.44021. With other factors fixed, training caseload would need about 835 lower-risk parents per effective trainee to approach $1m/10; do not treat that threshold as observed capacity.

Cost should be updated from reconciled current recipient accounts; $1,513 is not a cheaper valid scenario. Paid clinical follow-through is a necessary complementary resource and could materially raise societal costs.

what: Urban Peace Institute supports community violence prevention and intervention in Los Angeles through the LA Peacemakers coalition.
Its partners use trusted outreach, crisis response and conflict mediation to help people facing serious violence.
UPI also trains intervention workers and works on public policy; this comparison focuses on a specified Los Angeles participant pathway.
strengths: Preventing shootings can protect life, reduce lasting pain and disability, and preserve work among survivors.
Community partners can reach people who face concentrated risks and may not be well served by conventional systems.
Three consecutive original returns disclose expenses and regrants, making the financial support boundary inspectable.
reservations: Reported crisis interventions and neighborhood homicide trends do not identify the additional causal effect of UPI funding.
Prospective engagement, survival, household savings and recovery earnings remain explicit assumptions rather than measured local outcomes.
Public programs, existing grants and partner resources complicate the counterfactual; no additional unfunded service tranche is verified.

sections.what:
UPI is the independent nonprofit Connie Rice Institute for Urban Peace, EIN 36-4816075. Its ordinary support funds training, technical assistance, regranting, community safety and justice reform, including work beyond Los Angeles. The official donation page identifies this recipient and EIN. No restricted Peacemakers-only gift is assumed. [Recipient](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/donate/)

LA Peacemakers braids $9.6 million of public and private support across 18 independent organizations during 2024–2026. Its first-year report covers February 2024–January 2025 and reports 1,027 new participants. These are observed operational counts, not 1,027 people whose lives were saved. [Year-one report](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/LA-Peacemakers-Y1-Report.pdf)

FY2025 Schedule I lists 17 legal grant recipients totaling $3,625,415, including fiscal-sponsor routes. The 18-member initiative and a single fiscal-year grant table are different denominators. The largest listed recipient, Chapter Two, received $1,035,767. These transfers are already included in UPI expense and are never added a second time. [Actual regrants](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202630969349301208/IRS990ScheduleI)
sections.monitoring:
The year-one report describes 13% fewer fatal injuries and 24% fewer nonfatal injuries between its two half-years. Its graph does not clearly tabulate the exact totals used in alpha, so those totals are removed. Injury definitions are not sufficiently specified to equate every reported event with a shooting. This before–after comparison has no controlled counterfactual, consistent person-time denominator or independent outcome linkage. It is not used to estimate e or r. [Year-one report, p15](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/LA-Peacemakers-Y1-Report.pdf)

The year-one 1,027 new enrollments inform a prospective annual scale, not measured engaged person-years. The newer progress report separates 47 frontline positions from 53 operational positions; neither is a verified full-time equivalent. Cumulative enrollment subsequently approached 2,000. Reported prevented incidents are staff judgments, not observed counterfactual injuries. The model neither annualizes cumulative counts nor adds citywide homicide declines. [Progress, p4](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/LA-Peacemakers-Initiative-Progress-Report.pdf) [February 2026 statement](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/homicides-drop-by-nearly-27-in-neighborhoods-most-impacted-by-violence-in-2025/)

Remaining evidence priorities are unique engaged person-years by risk and service intensity, incident definitions, independent linkage to fatal/nonfatal outcomes, matched comparison trajectories and the exact staffing/service loss after already-committed grants and reserves. Prospective reporting must protect participants from identification, coercive information sharing and retaliatory exposure.

October 2 review: original FY2023–25 returns and FY2025 Schedules D/I were freshly checked. Schedule D reports a zero adjustment between audited and return expenses; this is a return reconciliation, not a newly read matching audit or opinion. Current cumulative enrollments and crisis interventions remain process measures, not current unique participant-years or causal prevented shootings. READI was read in selected original full-text passages, and the survivor study as its indexed abstract only. Earlier public-contract and cohort-dedup evidence is inherited rather than freshly reviewed.
sections.qualitative:
READI randomly offered intensive employment, cognitive-behavioral programming and support. Only 55% began programming. Its 12% lower victimization estimate is treatment-on-the-treated relative to control compliers, not a significant intent-to-treat reduction or a UPI coefficient. The primary violence index was not significantly improved; outreach-referred participants had a stronger 43% victimization estimate. The 11 events per 100 controls over 20 months is a rate benchmark, not the same estimation denominator. The historical model used risk .04 and effect .10 as transport judgments, not study-derived effects. The current model instead uses .035 and .07, with the same evidence limitations. [Original trial](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10898100/)

A closer local study models nonrandomized GRYD incident response in 2014–17, using spatial-temporally sampled controls. It estimates roughly 14–18% lower retaliatory triggering, with meaningful model and inferential uncertainty. This is neither all violence nor the incremental effect of UPI, training, or Peacemakers. Existing GRYD is part of the baseline; the study supports mechanism plausibility without supporting direct transplantation of a headline reduction. [Original local study](https://www.pjeffreybrantingham.com/_files/ugd/50eba0_8b88fa1624d442979bbff5c880935271.pdf)

Historical clinical model: mortality value used an explicit finite survival calculation: .8 health utility, a 47-year cap, 1% annual all-cause mortality and 3% discounting produce 16.7227 QALYs per initially avoided death. The annual death probability and cap are judgments, not a recipient life table; future victimization risk has not disappeared. Nonfatal value is .1 acute QALY plus .05 annual utility loss for at most ten years, with the same survival/discounting, totaling .5047 QALY. The current model instead uses a 35-year cap, 1.5% annual mortality and a nonfatal course of .08 acute plus .04 annually for five years, as explained in the current cost section. The small Boston cohort supports ongoing morbidity but does not identify either set of parameters. Fatal and nonfatal branches are mutually exclusive. [Survivor study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32530586/)

Only one service year is central. Extra downstream health is not another program year. Continued exposure to violence, displacement to other people or neighborhoods, worker injury/burnout and privacy harms can erode or reverse benefit. No arrest, crime-cost dollar or reported mediation is directly converted to QALYs. The Richmond evidence previously reviewed remains contextual, not an additional credited channel.

The current model separately reconsiders finite health, signed medical obligations, access costs and recovery earnings. It replaces the old clinical transport assumptions rather than allocating money inside an unchanged clinical total. The earlier numerical health values are explicitly historical; the current cost section and parameters govern the revised comparison.
sections.cost:
GiveBetter estimates about $61.2 million per better life for the specified LA community-violence pathway, including health and signed household-resource effects. Preventing a shooting can avert death or lasting injury; among nonfatal survivors it can also avoid otherwise-paid medical bills and preserve recovery-period earnings. The estimate credits those tangible pathways without equating every reported intervention with a prevented shooting.

A hypothetical $10,000 donation supports 0.404 participant-year equivalents under a proportional annual-support model. At the current assumptions it averts 0.000589 serious victimizations, split into 0.000118 fatal and 0.000472 nonfatal events. These fractional model expectations are not observed additional people served or rescued. The model fixes a prospective cohort of 1,027 engaged participant-years independently of its accounting denominator; it does not treat cumulative enrollments as current annual person-time.

Risk is assumed at 3.5% per participant-year, causal risk reduction 7%, UPI attribution 60%, and funding response 35%. None is empirically identified for an ordinary UPI gift. READI supplies relevant experimental evidence from Chicago but paired cognitive-behavioral programming with supported paid employment; its pooled violence index and victimization effect were not significant, while an outreach subgroup showed stronger effects. Neither that subgroup nor the uncontrolled LA neighborhood homicide decline is imported as UPI effectiveness. Public providers and existing committed support remain in the counterfactual.

Fatal and nonfatal outcomes are exclusive. An avoided fatality receives a finite 35-year health course at utility 0.8, annual competing mortality 1.5% and discount 3%. A nonfatal injury receives 0.08 acute healthy-year loss plus 0.04 annual loss for five years, with the same finite survival and discount. These are planning judgments, not measured LA utilities or a local life table. Survival and discount through the half-year event delay apply once. Independent process harm of 0.0001 healthy years per financed participant-year remains even if the intervention has no clinical benefit. Current local health is 0.00168618 years per $10,000.

Income and household resources are considered separately. Twenty-five percent of financed participants are assumed to incur $30 of additional access costs or actual lost disposable pay. Thirty percent of otherwise-injured nonfatal households are assumed to avoid an $800 medical obligation they would actually bear; hospital bills paid by Medicaid, charity care or government are not household savings. Sixty percent of those nonfatal households are assumed to preserve $3,000 of net recovery-period earnings for one year. No ordinary lifetime wages are credited to lives saved, and READI program payroll, UPI staff salaries, regrants and broad social crime-cost valuations are not added as income. These amounts and incidences are judgments motivated by plausible mechanisms, not measured effects.

Payer states are evaluated before the signed log-resource conversion, using a $25,000 annual household baseline. Positive medical savings and recovery pay receive 50% retention for potential overlap with health valuation; negative effects remain fully debited. Acquisition is an immediate early budget loss. Medical outlay occurs at the half-year event delay, and recovery pay starts one year later with common-alive survival. The first pay-year baseline carries forward the medical saving or cost; later years reset. This is an explicit household-budget approximation rather than observed consumption timing.

Per $10,000, discounted acquisition costs are −$3.03, medical savings +$0.11 and recovery earnings +$0.80. Their welfare equivalents sum to −0.00005205 years. Adding them to health gives 0.00163413 equivalent years and $61,194,667 per ten; the health-only comparison is $59.3M. Income equivalents support a welfare comparison, not a claim that income is measured clinical QALYs. Unknown monetary magnitudes stay unknown, not zero; the shared cash-knowledge flag conservatively couples acquisition and medical amounts when either is unavailable.

The financial denominator is $8,897,684 of FY2025 full recipient accrual expense, including $3,625,415 of regrants once. Gross institutional and donor-support proxies are equal centrally; external partner resources are unmeasured. Full recipient spending includes other activities, so proportional gift-to-LA-support response is a hypothesis, not measured marginal productivity. Both local shares are 100% only for the specified LA-resident cohort, not all UPI activity. The $25,000 comparison ceiling is not verified capacity. Scenarios test lower and higher causal effects, funding, survival, costs, economic harms, zero and unknown routes without assigning empirical probabilities.

Historical comparison and financial appendix. The prior clinical-only central was $15,409,129.75 per better life. Its complete 22-case model remains frozen. The revised estimate is less favorable mainly because transport and funding assumptions are lower and health duration is shorter, not because income was deducted from an inherited welfare total. The following analysis is historical; original financial evidence remains useful.

Three original accrual returns cover consecutive July–June fiscal years ending 2023, 2024 and 2025. Full operating expenses are $3,185,128, $5,293,277 and $8,897,684 (mean $5,792,030). The FY2024 return includes an additional $100,000 nonoperating leasehold-disposal loss; Schedule D reconciles its $5,393,277 total to audited operating expenses. Both series are disclosed rather than silently mixed. No reported event, gaming, inventory or donated-service adjustment requires an extra latest-year addback. FY2025 Schedule D independently repeats $8,897,684 as reported audited expense, but does not substitute for the missing correctly matched audit package. [FY2023](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202441309349303054/IRS990) [FY2024 reconciliation](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202501079349300100/IRS990ScheduleD) [FY2025 reconciliation](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202630969349301208/IRS990ScheduleD)

The latest full cost includes $7,075,093 program, $1,264,399 administration and $558,192 fundraising. Regrants are included once. The revised model generates 5.7743 modeled additional LA QALYs from the selected participant branch, giving approximately $15.4 million per 10. This change from alpha is mainly the explicit residual mortality assumption, not new measured clinical effectiveness. Positive joint stress cases and a zero/harm case are not confidence limits. [Original FY2025 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202630969349301208/IRS990)

Full recipient annual cost is a ratio normalization, not an observed marginal gift or guaranteed purchase of 1,027 engaged person-years. National work and unpriced justice reform stay in the denominator. Partner/public resources outside UPI are not included in this donor-cost scope; a separate sensitivity adds $3 million of hypothetical external delivery resources. Attribution a does not make external resources costless, and no social-cost-effectiveness claim is inferred.
sections.funding:
FY2025 revenue was $12,539,904, government grants $5,292,475, cash $6,898,638, unrestricted net assets $6,213,733 and total liabilities $2,716,158. Cash equals about 9.3 months of FY2025 expense before commitments; that is not a current runway. The balance includes restrictions and obligations, and the correct FY2025 audit is still needed. FY2024 audited notes document concentrated funding and accrued external grants, illustrating why gross cash is not a spendable gap. [Latest accounts](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202630969349301208/IRS990)

UPI announced an $8 million Ballmer commitment over two years in July 2024 and says Peacemakers funding ends in 2026. This is historical committed support, not a fresh 2026 renewal or an extra amount to add to annual revenue. No verified remaining Peacemakers gap, renewal probability or marginal hiring budget was found. [Ballmer announcement](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/2024-7-17-upi-receives-8m-grant-from-ballmer-group/) [Dated cliff claim](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/homicides-drop-by-nearly-27-in-neighborhoods-most-impacted-by-violence-in-2025/)

The cliff is not all-recipient shutdown: BSCC identifies a separate UPI frontline-training contract from August 2025 through June 2029. Los Angeles also approved a $5.087 million Safe Passage award, with $3,438,380 in provider contracts including Community Partners and Alliance for Community Empowerment, recipient routes also appearing in UPI grants. Council authorization and appropriation do not by themselves prove every contract has been executed or replaces identical services. They do establish a material funded baseline to investigate, not zero public support. [BSCC](https://www.bscc.ca.gov/s_cpgpcalvipgrant/) [Named allocation](https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2026/26-0542_rpt_cao_05-27-26.pdf) [Adopted recommendations](https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2026/26-0542_rpt_ps_bf_06-16-26.pdf) [Final appropriation](https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2026/26-0542_CAF_8-13-26.pdf)

The historical central used b=.5 as an explicitly subjective effective capacity response to ordinary private support after reserves, replacement donors, secured grants and current commitments; historical a=.75 separately represented the UPI-enabled share of service benefit. These discounts must not be estimated from the same loss twice. The historical short-bridge case credited only a quarter-year gap and then assumes other funding resumes. Complete funding replacement removes clinical benefit; signed induced burdens, if any, are assessed separately in the current model. UPI itself describes trust and information-sharing concerns with federal funding; the report treats these as documented organizational constraints, not an independent legal finding. [UPI statement](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/concerns-regarding-recent-changes-to-doj-cvipi-funding/)

The filing labeled FY2025 contains FY2024 statements plus a February 2026 corrective-action attachment about recurring contribution-recognition controls. The period mismatch remains unresolved; obtain the correctly matched audit, implementation evidence and a current unrestricted cash/commitments schedule before treating this as donor-ready.

Separately, GreenLight Fund announced a $1 million multi-year Oakland Peace Academy investment in October 2025, with cohorts expected in 2027–2029. This supports the existence of funded non-LA activity, not an extra LA benefit or proof that Peacemakers is fully renewed. It should not be added again to historical revenue without a recognition and payment schedule. [Funder announcement](https://greenlightfund.org/greenlight-invests-1m-to-launch-peace-academy/)

The current 35% funding response is a conditional planning judgment, not verified additional slots. Existing public support, committed grants and spendable reserves must be considered before interpreting an ordinary gift as additional activity. Grants to partners are already included in recipient expenses and are not added a second time.

model.geographicAttribution: Specified LA-resident participant cohort: independently configurable health and household-resource local shares, both1 centrally.
model.formula: Financed participant-years=gift/cashSupport*participants*funding; events=participant-years*attribution*risk*effect*survival through event delay. Exclusive fatal/nonfatal outcomes use finite survival and discount, less independent process harm. Signed medical/access cash and common-alive recovery pay pass through the shared log-resource bridge. Price=10*gift/(local health+signed resources) if known and positive.
model.counterfactual: Public providers, committed support and reserves continue. No automatic causal credit for ecological homicide declines, reported mediations or ordinary program payroll.
model.attribution: Specified participant pathway, one locality allocation and exclusive fatal/nonfatal events; no regrant/partner/household/member multiplication.
model.uncertainty: Transparent finite planning judgments, not identified empirical expected donation return, full portfolio value or verified capacity.
model.nativeOutcomes: Financed participant-years, expected net avoided victimizations, exclusive fatal/nonfatal events, finite health and signed household dollar/welfare flows.
