acceptance.scope: Independently challenged conditional health and signed recipient consumption reference; unresolved counterparty welfare, clinical utility and marginal funding remain explicit.

what: God's Love We Deliver prepares meals tailored to people living with serious illnesses and delivers them to their homes.
Registered dietitians provide nutrition care and education alongside the meals.
The organization also serves eligible children and caregivers and supports some clients transitioning to tailored groceries.
strengths: Home delivery and individualized nutrition support address difficulty shopping and cooking during serious illness.
Caregiver and child meals support the household around the ill client.
Nutrition counseling and grocery transitions offer support as clients regain the ability to prepare food.
reservations: Delivered meals and food security do not establish clinical utility gains; controlled studies give mixed results.
Contract-funded services and existing food support make the effect of another unrestricted dollar uncertain.
Clinical recipients, consumed dose and net household resources are not separately measured for the published service totals.

sections.what: God's Love We Deliver, EIN 13-3366846, provides free medically tailored meals and dietitian support. Eligibility depends on serious illness and difficulty with daily activities; income is not a universal eligibility limit. Caregivers and children are part of the delivery portfolio. [Services](https://www.glwd.org/get-meals/faqs/) New insurance pathways and grocery transitions change the service mix. [2025 operations](https://www.glwd.org/about-us/2025-impact-summary-report/)
sections.monitoring:
Controlled evidence supports nutritional and food-security outcomes more clearly than QALYs. The 2019 randomized crossover improved diet, food insecurity, reported hypoglycemia and a secondary mental-health-days measure; it did not establish persistent utility. [Original crossover](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6420590/) Maryland's pilot randomized 74 people; clinical and diabetes-quality-of-life contrasts were null, while food insecurity improved. Consumption was much lower than delivered volume. English-language, diabetes and storage requirements and disease exclusions limit transport to NYC's illness mix. [Original pilot](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11606-024-09248-x)

The 2019 instrumental-variable claims analysis and 2026 Massachusetts Medicaid matched cohort are observational. The latter's randomized comparator dates do not randomize meal receipt; its main sample requires >90 days enrollment. Neither establishes GLWD donor-level QALYs. [2019 cohort](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6547148/) [2026 cohort](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04407-5) FAME-D's newer randomized conference abstract was found, but original full-text retrieval was blocked; no quantitative coefficient is imported. [Publisher](https://diabetesjournals.org/diabetes/article/75/Supplement_1/1249-OR/167139/1249-OR-Medically-Tailored-Meals-Lower-Hemoglobin)

Request distinct linked patients/households, consumption, service dates, controlled utility and signed household budgets. Satisfaction and payer savings are neither utility nor household income. The organization's 2025 PDF describes preliminary research and peer-reviewed work in progress; no controlled utility coefficient from those projects was established here. [Research update](https://e1.nmcdn.io/assets/glwd/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/GLWD-ImpactReport-R17-051926-1.pdf)
sections.qualitative:
Existing cash, SNAP/in-kind food, insurer meals, nonprofits and family cooking remain the baseline. Added food and freed spending form one household ledger: replaced purchases are removed, and retained consumption elsewhere is credited once. Caregiver time receives no automatic dollar value. The conditional annual ledger is $500 food consumption minus $250 substituted food plus $50 other retained consumption. Half that positive subtotal is removed for possible clinical overlap, and the full $25 burden is subtracted, giving $125 independently valued net resources. Baseline $18,000 includes existing cash and in-kind food. These are judgments, not measured GLWD effects.

A householdShare of .8 converts consumed clinical dose-years to household-year equivalents; these are not observed unique households. Insurer reimbursements fund expenses already in the denominator. Extra external/admin resources and adverse displacement are separately varied; missing fiscal costs or counterparty effects are not established zeros. Hospital savings are never deducted or converted into household resources. The central reference conditionally includes no quantified other-household displacement; this is unresolved, not a measured zero. A disjoint-household sensitivity subtracts support lost by other households at full weight. Disjoint nonconsuming delivered-dose household equivalents receive no positive consumption credit but retain full $25 receipt/storage/scheduling burdens. Thus c=0 does not imply zero household costs.
sections.cost:
Conditional full annual resources: $59,921,600.2. NYC-MSA health is 9.69 QALYs, with 4.90 signed consumption-equivalent healthy years, totaling 14.59. Main price is $41,079,886.48 per better life (ten combined equivalent healthy years); health-only is $61,865,622.21 per ten QALYs. Income equivalents are welfare comparisons, not clinical QALYs/DALYs.

A $1,000 full-resource portfolio share corresponds to 61.58 delivered meal units, 0.09 clinical delivered dose-years and 0.03 additional consumed dose-years after use and gift response. These are portfolio ratios, not a promised unrestricted-gift purchase. 520 meals is a reference service-year intensity, not a count of completed treatment or unique yearlong patients. No mortality or post-service persistence is credited.

One-year resource benefits occur at service onset. A delayed sensitivity is a new service-onset cohort and discounts both pathways at 3%; current delivered volume already reflects living recipients. Clinical-null retains $122.3 million per better life under the same resource judgment. Zero, negative and unresolved cases retain full costs and no finite positive price. Complete overlap leaves full household burdens.
sections.funding:
The current financial index links FY2024 audit and return. [Index](https://www.glwd.org/about-us/financials/) Tax functional $49,631,474 plus $10,034 COGS and $121,838 donated legal services equals audited $49,763,346. Add $2,377,336 direct event costs netted in revenue and $2,134,000 volunteer plus $199,500 advisor resources explicitly excluded from the audit: $54,474,182. An assumed 1.1 forward projection gives $59,921,600.20. Recognized donated materials/legal services are retained once. [Audit, statements and Note7](https://e1.nmcdn.io/assets/glwd/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/FY2024-Gods-Love-We-Deliver-Audited-Financial-Statements.pdf) [Return PartsVIII–IX and ScheduleD](https://e1.nmcdn.io/assets/glwd/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Gods-Love-We-Deliver-Public-Disclosure-Copy-5-15-25.pdf)

This forward resource perimeter and 2025 output are different dates, not a matched FY2025 result. FY2024 managed-care revenue is $11,583,319; donors, government and insurers continue. [Current partnerships](https://www.glwd.org/healthcare-partnerships/) No costed unrestricted incremental offer or contract substitution split was established. b=.5 is judgment. Capital/systems expansion may consume gifts before output; financing replacement makes b=0 plausible. [Donate](https://www.glwd.org/donate/) The FY2025 operating summary reports $51,256,141 expense excluding depreciation and $9,003,996 healthcare/partnership revenue. Its cost perimeter is incomplete for full resources. A separate scenario adds historical event, volunteer/advisor and depreciation proxies, without presenting them as observed FY2025 amounts. The PDF also describes a $40 million Brooklyn campaign funding infrastructure and ten years of rent, with $16 million still sought; this is concrete capital demand, not an incremental-meal offer. [2025 PDF, pages10–11](https://e1.nmcdn.io/assets/glwd/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/GLWD-ImpactReport-R17-051926-1.pdf)

model.costScope: Gross FY2024 audited expenses incl netted direct event resources and excluded volunteer/advisor replacement estimates, projected1.1. Whole recipient including festival. Outside clinical/admin resources unknown and separately varied. No payer savings netting. FY2025 operating summary is separately disclosed; proxy scenario substitutes summary expense and explicitly retains unrecovered event/volunteer/depreciation resources.
model.geographicAttribution: 2025 95% five boroughs; pooled5% Hudson/Nassau/Suffolk/Westchester/Monroe. g=.975 judgment, .95–1 bounds; Monroe state unclear and MonroeNY outsideMSA.
model.formula: C=(F+E+I+L+V)*f+X; P=min(M/D,N)*r*t; E=P*c*b; Qall=E*a*u/(1+d)^delay-h; Qmsa=Qall*g. H=E*householdShare. Joint annual resource gain=(positive food net of substitution+other consumption)*distinctShare-all burdens/benefits/taxes; shared log crosswalk; W=Qmsa+I; price10=10*C/W only for W>0. Nonconsuming cohort H0=P*b*(1-c)*householdShare incurs full burden via its own disjoint log ledger; no clinical overlap haircut.
model.counterfactual: Existing insurers, public/in-kind benefits, purchased groceries, family cooking and other providers remain. a clinical nutrition substitution, b donor capacity and c consumed exposure are different steps; net financial ledger is not multiplied by a again.
model.attribution: Annual whole-recipient work with explicit donor capacity response. Meal-dose years capped at one per reported person, mixed beneficiary share adjusted; household conversion is judgment. Counseling included in utility and never stacked.
model.uncertainty: Conditional model, not empirically calibrated expectation. Consumption, household overlap, alternative food, donor response and fiscal/resource incidence unmeasured for GLWD. Missing effects are unknown, not measured causal zeros.
model.nativeOutcomes: Delivered/consumed dose-equivalent years and joint household consumption-year equivalents; no mortality/post-service credits. Clinical QALYs and signed income equivalents separate.

historicalAlphaModel.costScope: FY2024 recipient functional expenses plus direct fundraising-event and inventory costs netted against revenue; all programs retained including festival; multiplied1.1 for forward cost. Volunteer time and outside clinical costs excluded.
historicalAlphaModel.geographicAttribution: 2025 distribution reports95% across NYC five boroughs,5% Hudson/Nassau/Suffolk/Westchester/Monroe combined. First four are MSA counties; MonroeNY is outside (MonroePA is inside). Without split/state detail set g=.975, sensitivity .95–1. Transfer of2025 geography to2024-volume projection explicit.
historicalAlphaModel.formula: C=F+E+I; exposure=min(M/D,N)*r; Q_all=exposure*a*u*b; Q_MSA=Q_all*g; cost=C*f; price10=10*cost/Q_MSA. D=12*52meal units per supported-year; N caps at one-year per reported recipient; clinical share r; additional nutrition a; utility u; funding b.
historicalAlphaModel.counterfactual: Ordinary public/private contracts, other donors, other meal providers and family food continue. a=.5 discounts alternative nutrition; b=.5 separately discounts financing substitution. No healthcare savings are converted into additional QALYs.
historicalAlphaModel.attribution: Model follows unrestricted recipient portfolio. r=.8 removes caregiver/child meal units from the illness-utility calculation rather than valuing all recipients as ill adults. Nutrition counseling assumed included in utility, not added.
historicalAlphaModel.uncertainty: Very weak causal and marginal estimate. Randomized pilot's null quality-of-life contrast makes zero material. Gift allocation, meal intensity and source-year transfer may dominate observed food volume.
historicalAlphaModel.nativeOutcomes: Dose-equivalent patient-years of incremental nutrition while services occur; finite utility only, mortality zero.

what: God's Love We Deliver cooks and delivers meals tailored to serious illness and provides nutrition support.
Its reported reach includes ill clients, children and caregivers, so our health model adjusts meal volume before estimating patient health.
The central model implies about $43.6 million per 10 NYC-MSA QALYs.
strengths: Concrete cooking and delivery operations reach people unable to meet nutrition needs.
Original tax reporting supports a cost denominator with direct event costs restored.
Current geographic reporting distinguishes the five boroughs from additional counties.
reservations: A recent randomized diabetes pilot improved food security but found no differential quality-of-life or clinical improvement.
Service volume includes caregivers and children and is not a count of additional clinical benefits.
Medicaid contracts and capital expansion complicate marginal unrestricted-gift allocation.

sections.what: The recipient delivers tailored meals and dietitian support to people affected by illness. A new grocery transition program and Medicaid pathways expand the service mix. This analysis prices the whole recipient against one meal-supported health pathway, with other net health provisionally zero. [Current impact](https://www.glwd.org/about-us/2025-impact-summary-report/) [Healthcare partnerships](https://www.glwd.org/healthcare-partnerships/)
sections.monitoring:
A 74-person randomized Maryland diabetes pilot used 12 meals weekly for 3 months plus dietitian calls. It reduced food insecurity, but clinical and diabetes-quality-of-life changes did not differ between arms at 6 months. This challenges translating meals into large health gains. Our 0.01 utility coefficient is a small subjective positive scenario, not a measured effect from that study; zero health remains plausible. [Original trial](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11606-024-09248-x)

Request residence, distinct clinical recipients, meals actually consumed, days exposed and controlled utility outcomes. Do not add hospitalization savings, reported satisfaction or meal counts as separate QALYs.
sections.qualitative: Home delivery may reduce physical burden and nutritional instability for people with complex illness. Alternative family support, other meal programs and insurance-funded nutrition remain available to varying degrees. Grocery transition and Medicaid expansion change the marginal service mix; it is not established that an unrestricted gift buys the historical average bundle. [Partner pathways](https://www.glwd.org/healthcare-partnerships/)
sections.cost: The model starts with FY2024 tax functional expense $49,631,474 and restores $2,377,336 direct fundraising-event costs plus $10,034 inventory cost netted outside that total, giving $52,018,844 recipient resources. A 1.1 forward multiplier gives $57,220,728.40. Benefit uses 4.2 million meals/624 meals per patient-year, 0.8 clinical-patient meal share, 0.5 incremental nutrition over alternatives, 0.01 utility gain, 0.5 gift additionality and 0.975 MSA share: 13.125 MSA QALYs. Price is $43,596,745 per 10. Exposure is volume-limited and capped at one year per client; no survival benefit or post-service continuation is credited. Volunteer time and external medical spending are excluded, so this is not full social cost effectiveness.
sections.funding:
The operating recipient's FY2024 return spans July 1, 2023–June 30, 2024. It reports $42,055,419 program, $2,084,720 management and $5,491,335 fundraising functional costs. Programs include a food festival, so food/delivery direct costs alone would understate the recipient. The same return records 4.2 million meals and 15,839 clients/caregivers/children. [Original Form 990, pages 1–2, 9–10](https://e1.nmcdn.io/assets/glwd/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Gods-Love-We-Deliver-Public-Disclosure-Copy-5-15-25.pdf)

For a $1,000 gift, scaling the whole recipient's forward cost corresponds to about 73 historical meal units before marginal-capacity and clinical adjustments; this is a portfolio equivalent, not a promised meal purchase. Public/insurance contracts and other fundraising continue; b=.5 discounts substitution. Current giving accepts ordinary gifts, with no verified restricted incremental offer. [Donation route](https://www.glwd.org/donate/)

The current 2025 impact page instead reports 3,689,816 meals and 15,115 people including children and caregivers. This model deliberately pairs FY2024 output with FY2024 expense before its assumed forward-cost multiplier; it is not a measured 2025 cost-effectiveness result. Substituting 2025 volume while retaining projected cost gives 11.530675 MSA QALYs and about $49.6 million per 10; this sensitivity does not repair the missing current expense.

model.attribution: Model follows unrestricted recipient portfolio. r=.8 removes caregiver/child meal units from the illness-utility calculation rather than valuing all recipients as ill adults. Nutrition counseling assumed included in utility, not added.
model.uncertainty: Very weak causal and marginal estimate. Randomized pilot's null quality-of-life contrast makes zero material. Gift allocation, meal intensity and source-year transfer may dominate observed food volume.
model.nativeOutcomes: Dose-equivalent patient-years of incremental nutrition while services occur; finite utility only, mortality zero.

reports.program: Civil legal aid, housing and mental-health rights

acceptance.scope: Independently challenged conditional recipient health-plus-net-household-resource scenario; counterparty welfare and marginal donation capacity remain unmeasured. Held until combined publication.

what: Mobilization for Justice provides free civil legal advice and representation to low-income New Yorkers.
Its lawyers address eviction, disability benefits, debt collection and workplace barriers, often alongside health and social-service partners.
The organization also uses community education and litigation to address barriers that individual advice cannot resolve.
strengths: Housing, benefit and debt assistance can protect practical necessities for people with mental-health disabilities.
A randomized NYC legal-counsel study supports better court outcomes, although it does not measure MFJ health gains.
Benefit and debt assistance can help families preserve the resources needed for ordinary daily life.
reservations: No controlled MFJ cohort establishes net household resources, sustained health gains or additional outcomes from a new donation.
Government funding, other counsel and a $3.5 million disability-rights grant complicate donor additionality.
Case totals and benefit awards are not unique households or causal welfare gains; household costs and counterparty losses can outweigh benefits.

sections.what: MFJ is one civil legal-aid recipient, EIN 13-2622748, formerly MFY Legal Services. Its services include housing, disability/aging, children and economic justice. [Recipient](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/) The adult mental-health project is the bounded modeled cohort; other portfolio effects remain unknown. [Mental-health services](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/projects/mental-health-law-project/)
sections.monitoring: Ask for a matched-year unique-household ledger recording housing retained, benefits actually received, collectible debt payments avoided, wages collected and job access sustained, with alternative help and all household costs. A randomized NYC study found better court outcomes with counsel; it measured neither modern MFJ marginal capacity nor QALYs. [Original 2001 study](https://doi.org/10.2307/3185408) The 2023 medical-legal trial reported mixed mental-health and utilization effects, so no trial-derived positive utility coefficient is inserted. [Trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37028914/)
sections.qualitative: Legal representation can retain housing, secure SSI/SSD or public assistance, prevent collectible debt payments and recover wages or remove licensing barriers. [Benefits](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/projects/government-benefits-project/) [Consumer rights](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/projects/consumer-rights-project/) [Workplace justice](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/projects/workplace-justice-project/) Count actual additional disposable resources after taxes, benefit withdrawal, rent, fees, travel and lost earnings. Debt face values, salary levels and legal victories are intermediate outcomes. Same-household pathways are netted before the logarithmic conversion, and gain/burden cohorts are disjoint. Public benefits are transfers with taxpayer costs; wage settlements and forgiven debt may transfer resources from employers or creditors. This recipient-welfare comparison does not establish net social resource creation; the counterparty and fiscal scenarios test this limitation. Housing scarcity can displace another household and all such unmeasured effects remain unknown. [Public counsel baseline](https://comptroller.nyc.gov/reports/evictions-up-representation-down/)
sections.cost: The reference retains the historical conditional health calculation: 6.14297 NYC-MSA QALYs per annual recipient expense of $25,609,806, or $41.69 million per ten health QALYs. A separate signed household ledger contributes -0.33641 equivalent healthy years, giving 5.80656 combined years and $44.10 million per better life. These are judgment-led conditional scenarios, not measured expected returns. A $1,000 gift scales to 0.0390 additional mental-health service exposures and 0.00215 incremental legal-stability outcomes under the retained capacity assumptions; neither is a promised client or legal win. Resource priors imply 0.00108 gain-household exposures and 0.0372 burden-only exposures per $1,000. Gain households receive a net $1,200 for one year at a $12,000 annual resource baseline; remaining households lose $25, including time/opportunity-cost consumption equivalents. Gains are already net of winner costs. A 50% positive overlap adjustment prevents adding all economic-security welfare to the same psychiatric stability endpoint; negative costs receive full weight. [Welfare comparison](https://coefficientgiving.org/research/cost-effectiveness/)
sections.funding: FY ended June 2025 gross expense remains the September29 original-return reconciliation: Part IX $25,194,864 plus separately netted event direct cost $414,942 = $25,609,806. Fresh original-return and Schedule D endpoints were inaccessible in this review; this is inherited verified provenance, not a new check. [Return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202620619349301467/IRS990) The freshly accessed FY2025 annual report states $25,118,398 expense, a distinct unreconciled perimeter. Its 9,848 cases are not unique households. [Annual report](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/wp-content/uploads/MFJ-2025-Annual-Report.pdf) MFJ announced a $3.5 million disability/aging grant in July2025, a relevant competing funding source rather than proof of extra ordinary-gift capacity. [Grant](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/news-and-press/patterson-grant-settlement/) No costed current unfunded plan was established. Ask which additional attorney/paralegal capacity a gift buys, the staffing timeline and restrictions; current annual ratios cannot establish a marginal price. Unrecognized pro-bono/clinical resources, public service use and additional fiscal transfers are unknown and separately stressed; no public savings are credited.

model.costScope: One year full recipient gross recognized expense including separately netted event direct costs. Current mental-health exposure retained; other portfolio net health provisionally zero, not a whole-portfolio lower bound. Headline is conditional recipient-household welfare: signed counterparty/fiscal welfare remains unknown, not an established zero. Signed household resource welfare is separate from health; donor-recipient expense is not full social cost.
model.geographicAttribution: 22-county OMB23-01 MSA. g=.98 is a judgment from NYC-focused service, not measured patient residence; test actual addresses before beta.
model.formula: A=sum(t=1..T) exp(-m*t)/(1+d)^t; Qall=N*z*l*e*r*a*b*u*A-h; Qlocal=g*Qall; price10=10*C/Qlocal when Qlocal>0. Separate income I=.5*sum(disjoint households*discounted finite years*ln((baseline+signed net resources)/baseline)*MSA share*positive overlap share). W=health-only editionQalys+I; headline=10*C/W if W>0, else null. Burden overlap share is always1.
model.counterfactual: Existing public representation, other legal aid, psychiatric care and benefits administration persist. e is incremental outcome versus no MFJ among otherwise-addressable clients; r discounts alternative help; a divides legal/clinical partner credit; b captures net extra capacity from gift. Household resources are compared against publicly funded counsel, alternative legal aid, hospital assistance and ordinary benefits administration, not no government support.
model.attribution: l=1 preserves the historical mental-health exposure per whole-recipient dollar; it does not earmark all dollars to the project. z deduplicates/intensity-adjusts reported clients; no separate general housing or Medicaid benefit is added. Financial exposure scales once with b and l; positive gain cohort shares e/r/a with incremental stability and is halved by resourceShare. Burden-only exposure is every remaining additional service household, independent of clinical success. No separate earnings, housing subsidy, debt and benefit additions are stacked.
model.uncertainty: Very weak, judgment-led health conversion and marginal allocation; scenarios are not confidence intervals. Neither the mixed clinical trial nor court-outcome experiment calibrates .06 annual utility or .15 incremental stability. Overlap remains a weak judgment. Delay uses forecast survivors/new intake at service onset, not fixed current persons; no survival through lag is claimed. Financial cohort size, net amounts, baseline and overlap are explicit uncalibrated conditional priors. The reference is not a probability-weighted expected estimate. Clinical-null, financial-only, unknown and negative scenarios are distinct.
model.nativeOutcomes: Legal service -> additional stable housing/income/care -> finite psychiatric utility improvement. Household collectible cash/consumption change and service burdens; gross legal claims are not resources.
model.nativeCosts: Retained whole-recipient annual ratios: 2,500 reported mental-health service exposures per $25,609,806; judged2,000 distinct/intensity equivalents; after50%capacity,1,000 extra exposures and55.125 local incremental stability outcomes. Not a marginal service-unit quote.

what: Mobilization for Justice provides free civil legal help to low-income New Yorkers.
Its mental-health legal work addresses housing, income and access to benefits alongside a much wider legal portfolio.
The highly uncertain conditional estimate is $41.7 million per 10 NYC-MSA QALYs from mental-health stability, charging gross whole-recipient cost.
strengths: The service reaches people whose psychiatric health may deteriorate when housing or income is disrupted.
Original tax-return reconciliation supports a full-recipient cost denominator.
Hospital and outpatient partnerships offer a concrete route from legal help to continued community living.
reservations: No MFJ-controlled study identifies sustained health gains or the response to another unrestricted dollar.
Legal wins, dollars recovered and avoided judgments cannot be treated as QALYs.
Public legal services and clinical partners already help many clients, reducing incremental donor credit.

sections.what: MFJ, formerly MFY Legal Services, is one recipient, EIN 13-2622748. It provides housing, disability, aging, consumer, employment, immigration and family-related civil legal help. The Mental Health Law Project is not a separately priced charity. [Official recipient](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/) Its current program page reports over 2,500 people with mental-health disabilities served annually and describes collaboration with outpatient providers and psychiatric units. [Mental-health services](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/projects/mental-health-law-project/)
sections.monitoring: Track distinct clients, legal need, case intensity, alternative representation, durable housing/benefit outcomes and patient-reported health at 6–24 months. A legal outcome is an intermediate endpoint. The historical NYC randomized representation study improved court outcomes, but supplies no MFJ QALY estimate. [Original study](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/F1782DCB947F50D13325322DDD0A88CC/S0023921600032977a.pdf/the-impact-of-legal-counsel-on-outcomes-for-poor-tenants-in-new-york-citys-housing-court-results-of-a-randomized-experiment.pdf) A 2023 medical-legal trial found mixed health results—less stress and fewer emergency visits but more anxiety and hospital visits—so reduced utilization is not automatically a health improvement. [Trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37028914/)
sections.qualitative: The higher-value plausible chain is legal action preserving psychiatric patients' housing, income or effective benefits, thereby reducing distress and relapse. The model combines these into one stability endpoint to prevent overlapping credit. It does not add deaths averted, rent transfers or citywide policy gains. NYC right-to-counsel is an important publicly funded alternative, although the Comptroller documents large representation gaps; an 89% housing-retention statistic is an uncontrolled outcome, not an 89% treatment effect. [Public baseline](https://comptroller.nyc.gov/reports/evictions-up-representation-down/)
sections.cost: Central: $25,609,806 in gross whole-recipient expense divided by 6.14297 MSA QALYs gives $41.69 million per 10 QALYs. At 2,500 reported mental-health clients, gross exposure is one service per $10,244; after a judged 20% repeat/intensity adjustment, one client-equivalent per $12,805, or 0.0781 per $1,000. These are whole-recipient ratios, not project prices. Incremental legal outcome, alternative-help, partner and funding factors imply 0.00220 stability outcomes per $1,000. Each receives a judged 0.06 annual utility for two years, 2% mortality and 3% discount. Current reach and FY ended June 2025 expense are a forecasting proxy, not a matched-year causal efficiency estimate. Prior-year and management-summary expense sensitivities are separately labeled; neither replaces the reconciled gross denominator.
sections.funding: The latest original return covers July 1, 2024–June 30, 2025 (tax-year form 2024). Part IX expense is $25,194,864; Part VIII line 8b separately nets $414,942 direct event expense, making gross recipient expense $25,609,806. Schedule D lines1/3/5 repeat $25,194,864, but Part IX explicitly excludes VIII8b; that reconciliation does not eliminate event resources. Revenue is $24,245,240 and ending net assets $7,687,646, not all spendable cash. [Original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202620619349301467/IRS990) [Schedule D](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202620619349301467/IRS990ScheduleD) FY2024 original expense is $22,033,456 and event line 8b zero. The annual report gives $25,118,398 expense, $76,466 below the latest Part IX total; this discrepancy is unresolved and the annual report is retained only as a distinct sensitivity. [Annual report](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/wp-content/uploads/MFJ-2025-Annual-Report.pdf) No current costed unfunded plan was established. The 0.5 gift response and continuation of historical mental-health allocation are judgments; unrestricted gifts may replenish reserves or replace support.

what: KAVI supports young people affected by violence in Brooklyn hospitals, schools and communities.
Its hospital team helps patients and families recover, de-escalate conflict and connect with continuing support.
A conditional reinjury model estimates $127.5 million per 10 local QALYs using the whole recipient's expense.
strengths: Hospital contact can identify people at elevated risk soon after violent injury.
Follow-up and conflict mediation provide a specific pathway to reduced harm.
Original 990 and audited reconciliation establish the full recipient cost and government-funding baseline.
reservations: No KAVI-specific controlled reinjury effect or annual engaged-patient count was located.
External HVIP studies are mixed and suggest sustained engagement is crucial.
An unrestricted gift supports the broader portfolio and may substitute for public or philanthropic funding.

sections.what: Kings Against Violence Initiative Inc., EIN 81-1626947, is a separate nonprofit with school, hospital and community programs in Central Brooklyn. [Scope](https://www.kavibrooklyn.org/) The hospital program works at bedsides and with families, provides conflict de-escalation and trauma recovery, and refers patients to continuing support. It partners with Kings County Hospital and violence-prevention organizations; KAVI does not provide the hospital's emergency surgery. [Hospital pathway](https://www.kavibrooklyn.org/hospital)
sections.monitoring: Measure eligible patients, distinct enrolled patients, sustained engagement, completed services and violent reinjury/mortality using multi-hospital follow-up, including people who disengage. A 2025 St Louis observational evaluation found 7.6% one-year reinjury among participants versus 7.4% among matched controls, with wide uncertainty. [Original study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12379808/) A 2026 Boston target-trial emulation found no benefit for any engagement but favorable, imprecise results among the small sustained-engagement subgroup; residual selection remains possible. Its combined reinjury/perpetration endpoint cannot be transferred directly into injuries averted. [Original study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41587478/)
sections.qualitative: The promising health mechanism is preventing a subsequent violent injury through trusted ongoing contact, mediation and care linkage. Merely counting bedside contacts misses engagement; converting every mediation into a life saved would be wrong. Schools and community healing may add health value, but no separate QALY credit is assigned here. NYC Health lists KAVI, Man Up! and Save Our Streets at Kings County and funds a wider intervention network. That public baseline remains, and overlapping patients/events cannot receive full credit in each charity's report. [City network](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/neighborhood-health/anti-violence.page)
sections.cost: Full annual recognized cost is $4,360,879. Because a measured KAVI patient count was unavailable, the model explicitly assumes 35% of marginal unrestricted expenditure reaches the hospital pathway and $5,000 in allocated cost per supported patient. This implies 305.3 annual patient-equivalents, or 0.07 per $1,000 of recipient spending, not an observed output. Only 25% sustain engagement; a transferred 7.4% one-year reinjury baseline and judged 25% causal reduction are then reduced for alternative help, partner credit and gift response. The resulting 0.3706 donor-attributable events produce 0.341964 local QALYs. Five percent of prevented events are assumed fatal; survival benefit stops after 30 years with 0.85 utility, 1% annual mortality and 3% discount. Nonfatal injury prevention receives 0.15 utility for two years only. Both severity assumptions are unmeasured. No repeated cohort or lifelong crime reduction is added. Because N=C*l/k, changing C alone scales both modeled capacity and cost; inflation is correctly tested by changing k.
sections.funding: FY2024 original Form 990 shows $4,360,879 expense ($3,522,226 program, $647,538 management and $191,115 fundraising) and $4,168,812 revenue. Government grants supply $2,689,257; $108,000 of contributions are noncash and are not added again. Net assets are $1,919,879, including $1,566,596 without donor restrictions. FY2023 expense comparator is $3,389,059. Schedule D reconciles audited expense to the same FY2024 total. [Original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202523219349301002/IRS990) [Schedule D](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202523219349301002/IRS990ScheduleD) A deficit does not establish which next position is unfunded. No current costed expansion plan was found; 0.5 net donation response is a judgment. Hospital resources and public benefits induced by referral are outside recipient costs; this is not full social cost-effectiveness.

what: Samaritans of New York offers free, anonymous, confidential, round-the-clock emotional support and suicide prevention.
The recipient also offers bereavement support and public education, whose separate effects are not monetized here.
We examine incremental crisis episodes supported by an ordinary gift against existing free NYC988 and other support, with signed household-resource effects.
strengths: Current operator pages identify a specific active hotline and its consent and privacy policies.
Original fiscal returns reconcile annual recipient costs, including separately netted event expense in FY2022.
The model distinguishes calls from episodes and values common-alive distress and net cash effects without adding survivor earnings.
reservations: Unique callers, causal death prevention, persistent utility change and extra gift-funded capacity are not observed.
Free NYC988 is a substantive alternative; hotline studies do not measure this recipient’s next-dollar effect.
The conditional central is about $30.7M per better life, with slightly negative net resources; null, adverse and funding-replacement cases are explicit.

sections.what: The recipient is Samaritans of New York Inc., EIN 13-3164464. Its [current crisis page](https://samaritansnyc.org/crisis/) describes free 24/7 anonymous confidential listening, no caller tracing unless location is shared and no police/EMS action without caller consent. Ordinary telephone-provider charges may still apply. Its [overview](https://samaritansnyc.org/get-support/) also offers bereavement and education. An unrestricted gift does not create a verified restricted hotline slot. The model conservatively charges the whole recipient’s cost while counting only conditional crisis effects; other portfolio effects remain unknown rather than zero.
sections.monitoring: The latest original return reports FY 2024-labeled 37,734 contacts, including 29,129 crisis calls. They are not unique callers or resolved independent episodes. The overview’s 50,000 contacts/30,000 volunteerhours and older 2023 education/bereavement totals have different reporting scope and dates and are not a matched current denominator. Anonymous service limits residence and unique-person measurement. Needed data include privacy-preserving repeat-episode counts, wait/abandon rates, unmet demand, follow-up retention, actual clinical outcomes, local residence, covered staffing and a dated next-dollar capacity plan. No source supplies these measurements.
sections.qualitative:
[Gould 2007](https://doi.org/10.1521/suli.2007.37.3.338) followed 1,085 suicidal callers at eight US centers; 380 (35%) completed follow-up. Distress and suicidality fell, but there was no untreated control, substantial follow-up attrition and no generic utility or causal mortality estimate. The [original randomized ASIST training study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3838495/) compares trained versus existing counselors, not a hotline versus no help; its primary indexed abstract supports immediate distress outcomes, not deaths averted. Full text was inaccessible in this pass, so no numerical effect is imported. The [2026 national 988 study](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/article-abstract/2848066) compares observed 15–34-year-old mortality with a forecast after the national launch, not an isolated Samaritans donation. Its 11% national association cannot identify this program’s effect. [Current NYC 988](https://nyc988.cityofnewyork.us/en/) offers free 24/7 calls/text/chat, languages, referrals and follow-up. Noncoercive anonymous listening may reach people avoiding other routes; it may also delay escalation for some crises. Consent policy is not proof that net harms are absent. Independent delay/safety harm is modeled, with adverse/null cases.

The primary Gould full text also excludes 654 callers considered too acutely suicidal to administer the assessment, adding selection bias to follow-up attrition. The assumed episode multiplier is an approximate repeat-contact adjustment, not a verified distinct-person registry; repeated crises within one person remain a source of uncertainty. Mortality probabilities are deliberately small, but this does not establish real unique lives saved.
sections.cost:
Our conditional combined estimate is **$30.7 million per better life**: ten health-and-household-resource-equivalent years in the NYC metro area. The initial health-only estimate was $13.9 million. The change reflects revised crisis-episode, clinical and household-resource assumptions, not an observed deterioration in the hotline.

**What additional funding could provide.** The latest annual expense is $1.29 million. Historical crisis-call volume, a judged current-scale transfer and a 40% funding response imply about 72 additional call equivalents per $10,000 mathematical normalization, or roughly $138 per additional call equivalent. Assuming five contacts per independent crisis gives about 14.5 crisis episodes, or $691 per episode. These are conditional average-support calculations, not verified additional staffing prices or unique callers. The full recipient's administration, fundraising, education and support costs are charged once; donated volunteer hours are not automatically monetized or added twice.

**Health.** Existing free NYC988 and other help remain in the counterfactual. The model assumes a modest acute mortality-risk difference among a judged high-risk subgroup, one-day response delay and a finite twenty-year survival tail. Short-lived distress improvement applies only to people alive in both worlds. A separate safety/delay burden remains in clinical-null cases. Hotline studies support the plausibility of immediate relief, not these numerical mortality or generic-utility assumptions. Repeat contacts and unique crisis episodes are uncertain.

**Net household resources.** Small one-off phone charges and uncovered care or transport costs are subtracted after free calling, insurance and other support. A small response group avoids actual lost disposable pay, net of taxes, benefits, paid leave and work costs. Caller time, gross wages, ordinary earnings of newly surviving participants and retail value of free services receive no cash credit. Nested care/no-care groups use a shared resource ledger rather than duplicate receipts.

The [Coefficient Giving-inspired logarithmic comparison](https://coefficientgiving.org/research/cost-effectiveness/) uses a judged $25,000 annual household-resource baseline. Common-alive survival, dated receipt, local attribution and discounting apply once. Half of positive income-equivalent welfare is retained to reduce overlap with distress relief; negative resource costs are charged fully. These are unmeasured resource priors, not caller financial outcomes.

At the $10,000 mathematical normalization—not a gift recommendation—the central case yields about 0.00331 health years and −0.000057 income-equivalent years, or 0.00325 combined years. Scaling funding and activity together does not change the price. The twenty scenarios include weaker and stronger clinical responses, repeated contacts, delay, low acute risk, shorter survival, signed pay losses, overlap, zero expansion, full clinical substitution and adverse outcomes. An external-resource companion adds $100 per episode for selected unrecognized volunteer or public resources, not a complete societal-cost inventory. Other portfolio benefits, unique-person outcomes and actual gift-sensitive capacity remain unmeasured.
sections.funding:
Original FY 2025, FY 2024 and FY 2022 returns were freshly retrieved; FY 2023 was not available in the inspected original index, so these are not a consecutive three-year series. FY 2025 audited expense $1,288,400 differs by $1 from Part IX $1,288,399 (program 926,923/management 183,353/fundraising 178,123); direct event expense is blank and is not added. FY 2024 Part IX/audit $1,194,820; FY 2022 Part IX $902,572 plus separately netted direct event $77,785 reconciles to audited gross $980,357. FY 2025 prior-year expense comparator $1,115,933 differs from the FY 2024 original $1,194,820; no comparable mean is forced.

Latest government grants $375,396, revenue $1,002,201, deficit $286,198 and prior-period adjustment−$5,081 accompany ending net assets without restriction $439,448. Cash $283,011, grants receivable $107,596 and accounts receivable $79,916 mean net assets are not cash runway. FY 2024 government grants $370,000 and FY 2022$439,297 are not evidence of uncovered current capacity. Grant renewals, fund restrictions, staffing vacancies, unmet calls and donation replacement remain unknown. No audit opinion/control report was inspected and no donation/contact was made.

model.costScope: Donor marginal capacity scenario from full annual average expense; unknown external volunteer/public resources not known zero.
model.geographicAttribution: g=.8 anonymous-caller MSA residence judgment; applied once to health and each income path.
model.formula: k=ln(1+r); F(q,t)=(1-exp(-q*t))/q; E=G*b*N*f*episode/C; B=E*a; survival gain=B*s*R*e*exp(-(m+k)*L)*u*F(m+k,T); common-alive morbidity=B*(1-sR)*p*v*exp(-(m+k)*L)*F(m+k,days/365); harm=E*h*exp(-(m+k)*L); H=mortality+morbidity-harm. Income=.5*people*ln(1+gain/sequentialBaseline)*commonAlive(receipt)*g*independence/(1+r)^receipt; price10=10*(G+E*external)/(g*H+income), null if denominator<=0.
model.counterfactual: Free NYC988, other support, grants, covered care and paid leave continue. b controls incremental scale; a clinical advantage; resource incidence is separately net causal differential.
model.attribution: Calls are not unique people. Independent episode/household judgments prevent literal contact multiplication. Common-alive utility/resources exclude acute baseline deaths and additional-survivor earnings. Negatives full credit; sequential bases avoid log ledger inconsistency.
model.uncertainty: Unweighted scenarios, not credible intervals or measured causal next-dollar effects. Outcome/funding/economic priors are judgments; missing other-program effects remain unknown.
model.nativeCosts: Latest whole-recipient audited expense1288400; mathematical gift10000, no arbitrary donor-specific framing; selected external-cost companion only.

sections.what: Citizens Housing and Planning Council of New York Inc., EIN 13-1782468, researches housing, land use and neighborhood policy. It is distinct from the Massachusetts Citizens' Housing and Planning Association and from NYC housing agencies. The January 2026 agenda includes basement implementation, affordable-housing pipelines, costs and land-use administration; an ordinary gift supports this entire agenda. [Current recommendations](https://chpcny.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Housing-Recommendations-for-a-New-Administration-1.pdf)
sections.monitoring: Track CHPC recommendations adopted beyond existing plans, the implementation change attributable to its work, actual safe occupied units and the timing difference versus baseline. Record displaced tenants, return rates, rents, remediated moisture, functioning egress/fire protection and injuries. CHPC's2016 Hidden Housing study estimated10,000–38,000 potential apartments under then-existing zoning; it is a technical opportunity estimate, not a current approved pipeline or measured output. [Original research summary](https://chpcny.org/publication/hidden-housing/)
sections.qualitative: The scalable mechanism is making already-occupied unsafe homes safer sooner. Existing residents already have some shelter, so legal status and property appreciation receive no automatic QALYs. Current DOB rules describe a 10-year legalization route and exclude high-risk flood locations; it would be wrong to assign protection from every future Ida-like death to eligible conversions. [Current program](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/codes/adu.page) The2025 proposed rules specify egress, alarms and later sprinklers/flood sensors, plus tenant return procedures. [Safety mechanism](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/dob/pr-legalizing-basement.page) A small randomized housing-moisture remediation trial supports a respiratory-health mechanism for symptomatic asthmatic children receiving combined home and clinical intervention; the model's population prevalence and QALY conversion are separate judgments. [Trial](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1626393/)
sections.cost: Two years of full gross recipient cost total $3,705,810. The conditional model considers1,000 safely implemented units influenced by a possible administrative improvement, then applies 0.25 incremental implementation probability, 0.2 CHPC share and 0.5 financing response: 25 attributable unit-equivalents, or 0.00675 per $1,000. These are expected-value modeling units, not homes sold by CHPC. With 80% occupancy and 2 residents each, 40 attributable resident-equivalents receive at most five years of safer conditions beginning year2. Annual injury risk 0.0002, 50% risk reduction, 10% fatal severity and 0.3 nonfatal QALYs are judgments. Fatal gains have20-year survival cap, 0.8 utility, 2% mortality and 3% discount. Separately10% of residents receive 0.02 annual utility through respiratory improvement; no lifetime cure is assumed. A 20% offset allows displacement/other housing harms. Central benefit is 0.285329 local QALYs. The1-year acceleration scenario is relevant if baseline implementation catches up quickly.
sections.funding: FY2024 Form 990 expense is $1,571,694, but Part VIII also nets $281,211 event costs from revenue; full gross recipient cost is $1,852,905. FY2023 analogously adds $259,755 to $1,617,518 for $1,877,273. Schedule D repeats the net presentation; it does not eliminate the real event resources. FY2024 net assets total $2,501,602, of which $2,364,762 are unrestricted. [2024 original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202503219349311945/IRS990) [2023 original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202443209349311019/IRS990) No costed unfunded implementation position was located; reserves and broad advocacy scope make 0.5 gift responsiveness uncertain. The mayor reported more than $1 million invested in the city legalization effort by August 2026; this continues in the counterfactual and is not assigned to CHPC. [Current public baseline](https://www.nyc.gov/bn/mayors-office/news/2026/08/transcript--mayor-mamdani-holds-ethnic-and-community-media-round) Recipient expense excludes owners' retrofit and public administration costs; an illustrative25 attributed units*$50,000=$1.25 million addition shows one resource sensitivity, not measured construction cost.

what: Chicago Recovery Alliance provides low-barrier harm-reduction services in Chicago, Cicero and Harvey.
Its outreach supplies naloxone and practical training so people can respond promptly to an opioid overdose.
It also offers sterile equipment, drug checking, testing and referrals; this estimate focuses on its overdose-response pathway.
strengths: Timely overdose response can prevent death and preserve years of health for people facing substantial risks.
Peer-based, low-barrier outreach can reach people who may not receive timely help through pharmacies or clinical services.
Original annual returns and audited accounts make its institutional spending inspectable, including a material settlement expense.
reservations: Current unique at-risk reach, additional timely rescues and the response to another donation are not directly measured.
The survival course, household spending and recovery earnings depend on explicit assumptions rather than a local causal study.
The 2024 return and later audit disagree, while public alternatives and existing grants complicate additional funding capacity.

sections.what:
CRA provides naloxone access and overdose-response education alongside sterile supplies, drug checking, counseling, HIV/HCV testing and referrals. Its current website lists Chicago, Cicero and Harvey sites and reports weekend closures after August 2025 funding cuts. A separate claim of seven-day service remains on the website; it is not treated as a verified current schedule. [Schedule](https://anypositivechange.org/) [Services](https://anypositivechange.org/cra-services/)

The model follows a prospective first-overdose encounter among people without otherwise-equivalent timely naloxone protection. It does not count every distributed dose or repeated reversal as a new person with a fresh lifetime of benefit. A 4,500 annual risk-person-year scale is a planning judgment, approximately 30% of an inherited statement that over 15,000 people relied on CRA annually after accounting jointly for current cuts, repeat contacts, nonopioid services and indirect recipients. It is not an observed current count; 2,250 and 9,000 are independent sensitivities.

Other services may confer substantial benefits or harms, but their net effects are not identified in this comparison. The current finite health and signed household-resource pathways should not be mistaken for measured impact of the entire organization.
sections.monitoring:
CRA's 2006 evaluation reported peer reversals, not counterfactual deaths averted. It predates today's fentanyl supply and alternative access. The Massachusetts naloxone study was observational; the 2024 HEALing Communities randomized trial of a broader package found a mortality rate ratio of 0.91 (95% CI 0.76–1.09), not a statistically clear reduction. Neither estimates CRA's current effect, and the latter does not show that naloxone itself is ineffective. [CRA evaluation](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16956873/) [Massachusetts](https://www.bmj.com/content/346/bmj.f174) [Trial](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2401177)

Request distinct people, repeated contacts, doses, witnessed events, administrations, verified survival, subsequent mortality, MSA residence and alternative access. A reversal need not equal a death prevented. Recent county/city data describe declining mortality alongside multiple interventions; no fraction of that decline is assigned to CRA. [Local context](https://cookcountypublichealth.org/2026/06/24/cook-county-chicago-joint-opioid-report-shows-third-year-decline-in-opioid-overdose-deaths/)

October 2 reassessment: current homepage and original 2022–24 IRS-derived returns were freshly accessed. Root independently confirmed the same entity and EIN in all three returns and matched source hashes. The detailed service/cut pages were blocked; matching signed audits, opinions, public-contract details and prior deduplication research are inherited earlier evidence, not newly reread PDFs. Historical peer reversals and the broader HEALing Communities trial do not identify current CRA marginal mortality effects. Fresh primary abstracts were read for those studies and the Massachusetts prognosis cohort, not their complete papers.
sections.qualitative:
CRA was selected for research value, not a validated donation ranking: direct overdose prevention and documented service cuts make additional diligence potentially useful. Accepted clinic alphas have uncertain utility transfers; DHC has major external-provider cost ambiguity; legal/housing models require further causal steps. These comparisons do not establish expected-value superiority.

Peer trust and low-barrier outreach may complement libraries, clinical care and vending machines; alternatives also reduce exclusivity. Illinois' free Access supply channel does not establish CRA's participation or mortality effect. Volunteers provide real resources, not economically free labor. [Illinois evaluation](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13126739/) [Volunteers](https://anypositivechange.org/volunteering-at-cra/)

Other portfolio net health remains unknown, tested in both directions rather than declared absent. No separate infection, counseling or referral credit is added. Beneficiaries may overlap Night Ministry, clinics and other outreach, so edition estimates cannot be summed as independent impact.

The current estimate reconstructs finite survival, signed access costs, actual purchase avoidance and conditional common-alive economic effects independently. It does not allocate income inside an inherited health total. The explicit clinical-null, adverse, unknown, alternative-access and survival cases are unweighted diagnostics rather than a calibrated probability distribution.
sections.cost:
GiveBetter estimates about $2.64 million per better life for CRA's specified Chicago-area overdose-response pathway, including health and signed household-resource effects. We think this pathway can be valuable because timely naloxone response can prevent an overdose death, preserving a finite course of health. The cost-effectiveness estimate depends on how much additional timely protection a donation actually creates, not simply the number of doses distributed or reversals reported.

Under the current assumptions, an illustrative $10,000 donation supports 4.03 risk-person-year equivalents, of which 3.22 receive usable supplied or trained coverage. After excluding people who would otherwise receive equivalent free protection or buy it, 1.45 equivalents have unmet timely access. The model predicts 0.0345 additional timely administrations and 0.00517 deaths averted. These are fractional model expectations, not observed additional people served or a verified donation offer.

The chain assumes 35% gift-sensitive funding response, 80% usable coverage, 50% otherwise-free access, 5% otherwise-purchasers, an 8% annual first-overdose encounter chance, a 30% increase in timely administration among remaining unmet encounters, and a 15-percentage-point mortality reduction conditional on an additional timely administration. Every coefficient is an explicit planning judgment. Free or otherwise-purchased equivalent protection receives no additional clinical credit. The timely-response coefficient is not another discount for the same public alternative, and funding response concerns usable financed coverage rather than clinical effectiveness. Illinois pharmacy coverage and Cook County free vending support the existence of alternatives but do not establish actual timely use.

Health is calculated independently of the old five-year estimate. The current model integrates survival and discount over a finite 40-year analytical course at utility 0.65. Annual conditional mortality is 7.5% in the first year, 4% in years 2–10, 5% in years 11–25 and 8% thereafter. The resulting discounted health area is 7.87 years per initially averted death before event-delay adjustment. A Massachusetts EMS cohort provides first-year prognosis context; later hazards and recipient utility are judgments, not a fitted Chicago life table. Forty years is a cap, not a claim of 40 years of remaining life. One-year, prior five-year, 55-year and alternative mortality cases expose this important uncertainty. Independent attempt harm persists even if rescue has no clinical benefit.

Income and household resources are evaluated separately. Twenty percent of financed person-equivalents are assumed to incur $5 of additional travel expense and $5 of actual lost disposable pay. Completed recipients who would otherwise purchase equivalent protection are assumed to avoid one $15 payment, with no extra clinical-access credit. Those who would otherwise obtain free supplies or forego purchase do not receive fictional retail savings. Publicly supplied medicine and volunteer labor are institutional resources, not recipient income.

Medical obligations and recovery earnings are considered only for people alive in both counterfactuals. Their central net amounts are zero as provisional, unidentified-sign judgments—not findings of no economic effect. Positive and negative sensitivities test $500 of actual household medical obligations and $300 of one-year recovery pay, with a 30% worker share. Lives saved do not receive ordinary baseline lifetime wages as an additional income benefit. The modeled common-alive and mortality-changed groups cannot exceed the same event cohort.

The resource ledger uses a $25,000 annual household baseline and the Coefficient Giving log-resource crosswalk. Actual access losses and purchase savings are evaluated in separate states before conversion, rather than logging their pooled mean. Lost pay uses the cash-adjusted budget. Delayed event obligations are stratified by earlier access burden; recovery pay starts one year after the event and includes first-year survival. Positive event-related gains receive 50% retention for possible overlap with health valuation; negative effects are fully debited. Access states and later event households are an additive low-incidence approximation, not observed joint lifetime consumption trajectories. Peer rescuer and victim household identity may differ.

Per $10,000, discounted local cash is −$1.53 and actual disposable pay is −$3.83. Resource equivalents are −0.0001072 years, added to 0.038029 health years for 0.037922 combined equivalent years. The health-only comparison is $2.63 million per ten years; the combined comparison is $2,637,009. Income equivalents support welfare comparison and are not measured clinical QALYs. Knowledge flags distinguish missing magnitudes from genuinely absent routes; an unknown clinical zero placeholder does not establish zero benefit.

Financial normalization uses $3,908,692 of later audited 2024 full recipient expense, including the $1,811,958 settlement loss once. Fresh original 2022 and 2023 amended returns report $1,642,030 and $2,385,530 of expenses. The earlier 2024 return reports $1,988,340 and does not reconcile to the later audit; the blank Schedule D bridge does not resolve the gap. All three original returns identify the same organization and EIN 36-3809778. The three-year audited average remains $2,645,417. These are historical accrual accounts, not cash flow or a priced expansion tranche.

Captured gross support equals the audited normalization centrally. External donated supplies, volunteer opportunity cost and induced care costs remain unknown, so the comprehensive resource comparison is not established. A 25% gross-cost allowance changes only the numerator. A settlement-exclusion diagnostic rescales funding with the denominator so it does not create extra people or health merely by changing accounting treatment. The $25,000 gift ceiling is a computational comparison boundary, not verified room for funding.

Historical comparison and financial appendix. The original clinical-only central was $4,080,401.52. The new estimate is more favorable mainly because it replaces an arbitrary five-year cutoff with a finite mortality-adjusted course, while using a different and lower effective reach/rescue chain. It is not improved by assigning saved-life wages. All 16 original scenarios remain frozen below; the following discussion is historical and does not govern the current comparison.

The cost boundary is one full recipient: $3,908,692 of 2024 audited expense including all support functions and the $1,811,958 settlement loss. Missing volunteer and externally provided inputs are K, additional resource cost net of anything already recorded. The displayed finite scenario conditionally sets K=0; it is not a complete economic-cost estimate. An illustrative 25% resource add-on raises the price to $5.10 million. Retail medicine prices are not substituted for opportunity cost. [Audit](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/display_audit/2024-12-GSAFAC-0000415493) [Volunteers](https://anypositivechange.org/volunteering-at-cra/)

The retained chain gives 4.05 conditional deaths prevented, 2.4897 discounted QALYs per death over five capped years, and 9.5792 MSA QALYs. Reach, risk, causality and financing factors are unmeasured. Ontario post-poisoning mortality is context only, not a CRA calibration. Survival 90%, utility 0.65 and the horizon are judgments. No lifetime extrapolation, recurring cohorts or extra reversal credit is added. [Mortality context](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31561997/)

One survival year gives $15.86 million per 10 QALYs; half distinct reach gives $8.16 million. Zero effect, no exclusive rescue access or complete financing substitution yields no incremental QALYs and no finite price. A negative net other-portfolio scenario is included. These are sensitivity cases, not confidence intervals.

The annual average is not an incremental gift price: a $1,000 gift cannot be promised 0.00245 QALYs or staff hours. At the central survival/geography assumptions, ten QALYs require about 4.228 additional deaths prevented, not four reported rescues. A priced expansion tranche and verified funding response are missing.
sections.funding:
Original full-recipient audited expenses are $1,642,030 (2022), $2,385,530 (2023) and $3,908,692 (2024). Earlier amended returns match their audits. The 2024 return predates the April 2026 audit, reports $1,988,340 and has blank Schedule D audit reconciliations. Its $1,920,352 expense difference exceeds the settlement loss by $108,394; that residual is unexplained. The later audit remains central. Settlement-excluded expense $2,096,734 and descriptive three-year mean $2,645,417 are sensitivities, not forecasts. [2022 audit](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/display_audit/2022-12-GSAFAC-0000378548) [2023 audit](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/display_audit/2023-12-GSAFAC-0000391384) [2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202523219349306217/IRS990)

The 2024 audit records $2,261,995 revenue, $1,298,180 cash and $487,099 settlement payable. These are historical balances, not current liquidity; expected 2025 payment is not verified. Government grants were about 85.6% of revenue. An unmodified financial opinion coexists with a repeated receivables-control weakness. An older personnel-compliance finding was marked resolved; no diversion or fraud is inferred.

The 2025 funding appeal is not proof of today's gap. City contract 259502 was extended through December 2026 with a $540,000 amendment amount but a requirements-dependent master ceiling; ledger payments during calendar 2026 total $323,090.73 through retrieved entries. Contract 259501 was extended through August 2026 and shows $62,497.69 paid during calendar 2026. Payment dates are not service periods, unrestricted revenue or new donor room. Neither payments nor contract modification amounts are added to historic revenue or subtracted from costs. [259502](https://webapps1.chicago.gov/vcsearch/city/contracts/259502) [Payments](https://webapps1.chicago.gov/vcsearch/city/vendors/92846178A/contracts/259502/payments) [259501](https://webapps1.chicago.gov/vcsearch/city/contracts/259501) [Payments](https://webapps1.chicago.gov/vcsearch/city/vendors/92846178A/contracts/259501/payments)

Donor readiness: HOLD. Request current management accounts/cash forecast, audit-to-return reconciliation, settlement status, grants and reimbursement timing, a priced unfunded restoration tranche, resource valuations and deduplicated local outcomes. The current 35% funding-response factor is a planning judgment, not evidence that 35% of a gift creates services. No contact or donation was made.

The assumed 35% funding response does not verify a new unfunded tranche. Current grants, restrictions, reserves, staffing capacity, settlement payment status and the 2024 audit/return disagreement still need reconciliation. This planning comparison should not be treated as verified productivity for an ordinary unrestricted donation.

model.costScope: Full recipient audited accrual support including settlement once; captured gross proxy equal centrally, external resources unknown. Not verified gift capacity.
model.geographicAttribution: Specified Chicago-area risk cohort: separate health and household-resource residency shares .95 centrally, each applied once.
model.formula: Financed risk-person-years=gift/supportCost*riskUnits*peoplePerUnit*funding. Additional first timely responses exclude completed otherwise-free/buyer coverage, then use encounter and timely-response judgments. Signed mortality benefit integrates finite discounted survival less attempt harm. Signed household cash/pay use state-level log-resource conversion. Price=10*gift/(local health+signed resources) when known and positive.
model.counterfactual: Public supplies, equivalent free/bought protection and other rescuers continue; gifts may replace existing finance. No reported reversal or ecological decline receives automatic causal credit.
model.attribution: First-event risk-person-year units, disjoint mortality/common-alive cohorts, actual purchaser savings without extra clinical credit; no repeat lifetime, household or portfolio multiplication.
model.uncertainty: Finite unweighted planning judgments, not identified expected donation return, comprehensive economic cost, whole-portfolio benefit or verified capacity.
model.nativeOutcomes: Financed risk-person-year equivalents, completed/unmet coverage, additional timely administrations, deaths averted, finite health, signed cash and actual disposable pay.

historicalModel.costScope: Single full-recipient boundary C*f+K. C includes all recorded support functions and settlement. K is unknown unrecognized donated/volunteer inputs needed by the same portfolio, net of recorded overlap. Displayed finite illustration conditionally K=0. Not complete economic cost or marginal gift price; induced external healthcare cost remains unpriced.
historicalModel.geographicAttribution: Chicago/Cicero/Harvey sites establish MSA eligibility, not 95% residency. Staff describe statewide activity. g=.95 is judgment, tested at .75; national training receives no benefit credit.
historicalModel.formula: deaths=N*c*r*h*e*a*b; L=sum(t=0..T-1)(s^t*u/(1+d)^(t+.5)); Q_all=deaths*L+H; Q_MSA=g*Q_all; cost=C*f+K; price10=10*cost/Q_MSA only when Q_MSA>0.
historicalModel.counterfactual: EMS, peers, libraries, other outreach and donors continue. a selects reach lacking equivalent timely rescue without CRA; h is counterfactual fatal risk in that selected group, not population mortality. e is conditional prevention in that group. b is additional usable capacity beyond replacement finance. These unmeasured factors may be correlated and are not trial-calibrated.
historicalModel.attribution: Whole recipient only; no credit for city decline or all reversals. Other portfolio health H is signed and unknown. Cross-recipient benefits overlap and cannot be added.
historicalModel.uncertainty: Very low confidence. Central retains alpha assumptions for continuity, not calibrated expected value. K=0 and H=0 are conditional omissions, not established absence or lower bounds. Marginal donor price is unknown. Scenario ranges are not confidence intervals.
historicalModel.nativeOutcomes: Conditional deaths prevented over one operating year, at most five subsequent survival years centrally, ten in favorable sensitivity; no perpetual cohort or separate infection/reversal credit.

inputs.name: h
inputs.rationale: Uncalibrated 2% fatal risk in people without equivalent timely rescue; external Ontario post-poisoning cohort is context, not CRA calibration.

inputs.name: e

inputs.name: b

inputs.name: T

inputs.name: s

inputs.name: u

inputs.rationale: Current service anchors inMSA; unknown resident/training leakage.

inputs.name: K

acceptance.evidence: Independent GPT-6 Astra Medium acceptance audit, 2026-09-29: original financial statements, service geography, clinical-source interpretation and model arithmetic checked. Accepted only as an explicitly judgment-driven alpha scenario, not measured marginal effectiveness.

what: Above and Beyond offers free outpatient addiction counseling on Chicago's West Side.
The model credits only a short health-utility improvement from additional treatment.
The central model uses $4,296,413 of whole-recipient audited expense.
strengths: Annual participation and recovery claim are published.
Audit includes recognized donated resources.
Free walk-in access can remove affordability barriers.
reservations: Recovery has no clear denominator or follow-up.
2023 counts proxy current treatment scale.
Gifts may replace fees, trustees or other donors.

sections.what: Free Level I/II outpatient counseling and referral operate at 2942 W Lake Street, Chicago (Cook County, current MSA). Medical linkage is not evidence of universal medication treatment. Pantry is a sister organization. [Protocol](https://aboveandbeyondfrc.org/how-we-do-it/clinical-protocol/)
sections.monitoring: 2023 snapshot reports 1,058 group participants and 42.9% recovered, without definition or denominator. Applying that rate to group participants is judgment; validity factor 0.5 reduces it but cannot validate the unknown denominator. Project MATCH compared active alcohol therapies, not treatment versus none; it does not supply this recipient's causal effect. Request validated utility, retention and counterfactual recovery. [Snapshot](https://aboveandbeyondfrc.org/donate/annual-report/) [Original trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8979210/)
sections.qualitative: Walk-in trauma-informed counseling provides plausible access. Housing, employment and medical linkage receive no separate health credit to avoid overlap. No mortality benefit or lifelong remission is assumed. [Programs](https://aboveandbeyondfrc.org/donate/annual-report/)
sections.cost: Use all $4,296,413 audited 2024 expenses, not the $3,526,474 tax summary. Includes $572,432 recognized donated resources and gross event costs. A $1,000 whole-portfolio equivalent corresponds to 0.246 group participants before response/additionality/geography, not actual marginal admission cost. Six-month utility gain is judged, no survival effect. [Original audit](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/display_audit/2024-12-GSAFAC-0000386319) The audit separately nets a $50,786 loss on transfer of assets against revenue. It is outside the operating-expense numerator; including it as a broader accounting-cost sensitivity gives $4,347,199. This is not an omitted recurring treatment cost.
sections.funding: 2024 original audit: support/revenue $5,078,619; program expense $3,231,072, management $756,564, fundraising $308,777; net assets $2,355,942; cash $1,892,947. Program fees $2,390,278, deferred grant $585,104 and note payable $850,000 complicate liquidity. Gift is unrestricted portfolio support; 30% financing additionality discounts fee/trustee/donor replacement. Marketing that operating costs are covered does not establish zero overhead or entirely additional health. [Audit](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/display_audit/2024-12-GSAFAC-0000386319) [Giving](https://aboveandbeyondfrc.org/donate/)

model.costScope: All audited expenses including recognized in-kind, support and events; no sister pantry benefit. A $50,786 loss on transfer of assets appears separately in revenue and is excluded from operating expense; broader accounting-cost sensitivity disclosed.
model.geographicAttribution: Chicago Cook County site; g=.95 judged, not observed residence.

model.counterfactual: Other care/spontaneous recovery removed by a; replacement financing separately removed by b.
model.attribution: Only short incremental morbidity; no all-recovery, employment, housing or mortality credit.
model.uncertainty: Very weak clinical attribution; current volume and response definition unknown. The central estimate is an illustrative scenario, not a calibrated expected value; favorable/poor scenarios are not statistical confidence bounds. Service location establishes eligibility, while modeled MSA residency shares remain unmeasured.
model.nativeOutcomes: Incremental response equivalents, .10 utility for .5 years central.

what: VOCAL-NY combines harm-reduction services with organizing and advocacy.

Conditional central estimate: $80.4 million per10 NYC-MSA QALYs; additionality is highly uncertain.
