model.costScope: Full September-ending FY2025 recipient expense plus netted direct event cost; partial prevention benefits only.
model.geographicAttribution: Judged .6 Denver ten-county CBSA19740 share of combined HeyDenver/Hey719 navigation. Clinic location and statewide headquarters do not establish client residence.
model.formula: Clinical patients N × navigation additionality × eligibility × adherence × biological efficacy × annual infection risk times finite HIV utility burden; subtract full participant harm. Household resources require prevented infection and jointly log net illness-related gains minus full navigation costs. Price =10C/(health + signed resource equivalents).
model.counterfactual: Public PrEP clinics, insurance and medication assistance, and other providers without CHN navigation.
model.attribution: Judged .2 navigation additionality, .8 eligibility, .6 adherence; .86 biological efficacy borrowed conditionally from high-risk on-demand trial, not measured navigation efficacy.
model.uncertainty: Risk, utility burden, adherence, residence, unique people, household costs, actual public alternatives and next-gift capacity unknown. Other recipient channels unknown, not zero.
model.nativeOutcomes: Official February 2026 statement reports FY2025 557 PrEP navigations and separate test counts; neither completed medication nor causal clinical outcomes.

reports.program: Community mental health, substance-use treatment, crisis care and recovery support
reports.priceScope: Matched FY2025 full recipient cost against partial depression-compatible care benefits; unknown crisis/substance/other effects, not whole-portfolio or marginal-gift EV.

what: Jefferson Center provides community mental health, substance-use, crisis and recovery services.
Its matched FY2025 reference uses a broad envelope of over 24,681 individuals, not prescriptions or completed therapies.
A partial depression-compatible care mechanism assesses health and signed household resources; other effects remain unknown.
strengths: Matched original fiscal 2025 full expense and native client envelope.
An original randomized collaborative-care trial provides an explicit utility anchor and null/adverse uncertainty.
Clinical patients are separate from resource households, with public alternatives and full burdens retained.
reservations: Broad client reach does not identify the eligible completed depression-care subgroup.
External UK primary-care trial results are not recipient clinical outcomes.
Full annual expense covers crisis, substance use, pharmacy and other unquantified channels.

sections.what: Current care includes collaborative-care clinic, adult and child programs, substance-use treatment, crisis services, mobile medication-assisted treatment and recovery supports. Reported 59,933 prescriptions are not additional unique beneficiaries. Jefferson, Gilpin and Clear Creek service counties are inside the Denver CBSA, but county operations do not establish all client residences.
sections.monitoring: Request deduplicated clients, diagnoses and completed dose by program; measured residence; comparable outcomes against active public services; patient/caregiver after-tax resources and access costs; and restricted marginal capacity. Match outcomes to the fiscal cost boundary rather than summing programs and prescriptions.
sections.qualitative: Original CADET randomized 581 adults in 51 UK primary-care practices to collaborative care versus usual care, finding .02 incremental QALYs over twelve months with CI−.02 to .06 and no difference at 36 months. It excluded acute suicidality, psychosis/bipolar and primary alcohol/drug conditions. Thus only a judged depression-compatible subgroup is transferred conditionally, not the whole community-care portfolio. Local fidelity and alternative services can erase or alter gains.
sections.cost: FYJune2025 full annual expense is $91,195,341, including $117,464 netted direct event costs. N=24,681 is an observed lower-envelope broad individual count, not treatment success. Eligibility .3, adequate delivery .7, incremental enhanced-care share .25 and Denver share .9 are judgments. q=.02 is already the average trial incremental annual QALY; response=1 avoids another clinical responder multiplication. Delivery .7 represents transfer/fidelity uncertainty, not a claimed empirical adjustment to trial intention-to-treat. Clinical patients retain full .0001 judged process harm; household uniqueness .85 affects resources only. Completed eligible incremental households have a .5 resource-success hypothesis and $400 net caregiver/adult work resources after taxes, benefits and work costs, with .5 positive overlap. Every client household retains $5 judged access/time burden regardless of benefit; intensity and high-cost scenarios acknowledge brief versus intensive services. Central actual copay avoidance and external payer loss are zero judgments, not measured absence. A recognized $76,489,720 all-program expense sensitivity excludes overhead but is not allocated depression cost. Other crisis, substance, housing and pharmacy benefits are unknown rather than zero.
sections.funding: Current own giving page links a ColoradoGives recipient identifying EIN84-0474717; the destination returned HTTP200 without a transaction. Insurance, Medicaid and public mental-health provision shape alternatives and funding incidence. Donations may support unmet needs, but program revenue or financial deficits do not prove the next unrestricted gift creates incremental care. Related entities are not added to this recipient-only IRS boundary.

model.costScope: FYJune2025 named recipient full functional expense plus netted event expense; no automatic related-entity aggregation. Partial depression channel benefits only.
model.geographicAttribution: Judged .9 ten-county Denver CBSA share. Jefferson/Gilpin/Clear Creek service geography supports local presence, not measured resident share.
model.formula: Health = (N clinical patients × judged eligible subgroup × delivered dose × incremental mode share × average annual trial-reference QALY − full patient process harm) × local share. Patient health is not reduced by household grouping. Household resources jointly log net gains and full access costs; distinct payer loss localized once. Price =10C/(health+signed income).
model.counterfactual: Medicaid/public mental-health provision, other clinicians and active usual care without additional enhanced service.
model.attribution: Judged .3 depression-compatible subgroup, .7 delivered transfer dose and .25 incremental enhanced-care share; native reach is not causal clinical gain.
model.uncertainty: Eligibility, completion, active alternatives, clinical transfer, client residence, household grouping/resources and marginal gift capacity unmeasured. Other clinical channels unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: FY2025 original IRS reports OVER24,681 individuals and59,933 prescriptions. Lower count24,681 used as broad envelope only.

reports.priceScope: Matched FY2024 full annual recipient cost against partial integrated depression-care mechanism; other primary/dental/pharmacy benefits unknown, not portfolio or marginal-gift EV.

what: Tepeyac provides bilingual primary care, mental health support, dentistry and pharmacy services in Denver.
Patients can receive short-term therapy, preventive and chronic-disease care in one clinic.
It accepts insurance and offers sliding fees without refusing care solely for inability to pay.
strengths: Matched2024 unique patient count and full original annual expense.
Integrated bilingual screening and6–12therapy sessions provide a concrete access mechanism.
Clinical patients and household resources remain separate, with active safety-net alternatives.
reservations: Unique patients do not identify completed depression treatment.
The trial utility reference comes from UK primary care, not local controlled outcomes.
Full clinic cost covers important primary, dental and pharmacy effects not quantified here.

sections.what: Tepeyac integrates bilingual primary care, behavioral health, dental care and pharmacy. Current behavioral health provides6–12sessions and case management plus referral to longer-term care. In2024 it served7,901unique patients across73zipcodes with35,438visits; service-line visits are not separate unique people.
sections.monitoring: Request unique behavioral patients, diagnoses and completed dose; clinical utility against active alternatives; patient after-tax resources, fees and access costs; actual residence and unrestricted marginal capacity. Keep primary, dental and pharmacy channels separate from overlapping behavioral patients.
sections.qualitative: The2024annual reports62%uninsured,22%public-insured and16%private-insured patients. Sliding fees and insurance enrollment can improve access but neither retail care value nor coverage approval is automatically net income. CADET randomized581 adults in UK primary care and found .02 incremental annual QALYs versus usual care, CI−.02,.06; Tepeyac's bilingual integrated model differs and recipient outcomes are unmeasured.
sections.cost: FYDec2024 full cost $18,893,488 includes $133,641 netted event expense. The7,901unique patient envelope is observed; .15depression-compatible share, .7transfer/delivery and .3incremental enhanced-care share are judgments. q=.02 uses the trial's average annual incremental utility; response1 avoids a second responder factor. The .15eligible envelope1185clients times .7delivery830roughly fits5427behavioral visits at6–12sessions but is not an observed completion count. Clinical health retains all patients; .85household grouping applies only to resources. Judged adult/caregiver $300net work resources require eligible completed successful additional care and biological response, after taxes, benefit withdrawal and work costs; no child wages. Positive gains receive .5overlap discount; all households retain $5access/time loss and all patients .0001process harm. Actual avoided copays are centralzero judgments, with payer-incidence sensitivity rather than retail medical charity income. Denver share .95isjudged;73zipcodes are not a residence audit. Whole clinic costs versus partial BHbenefits do not estimate portfolio EV. Three-year mean and functional-only expense sensitivities quantify cost-boundary and expansion-scale uncertainty.
sections.funding: Own donation page embeds an actual Blackbaud donor form, with no transaction. Legal LaClinicaTepeyacInc DBA Tepeyac EIN84-1285505. Current payment page accepts Medicaid/Medicare/private insurance and family-income-based sliding fees. HHS support and other safety-net clinics are public-provider alternatives, not all donation-funded capacity. New clinic expansion and financial scale do not establish a next-gift effect.

model.costScope: Full calendar2024 IRS recipient functional plus netted direct event expenses; new clinic scale and capital/recognized resource boundaries uncertain. Partial integrated BHbenefits only.
model.geographicAttribution: Judged .95share of unique patients resident in ten-county Denver CBSA19740;73zipcodes and MetroDenver description support presence, not measured share.
model.formula: Health = (N clinical patients × judged eligible subgroup × delivered dose × incremental mode share × average annual trial-reference QALY − full patient process harm) × local share. Patient health is not reduced by household grouping. Household resources jointly log net gains and full access costs; distinct payer loss localized once. Price =10C/(health+signed income).
model.counterfactual: Other safety-net primary care and covered providers, usual depression treatment, sliding fees and HHS-funded services without Tepeyac integration.
model.attribution: Judged .15depression-compatible subgroup,.7delivery-transfer and .3incremental enhanced-care share; .02trial-average utility is not recipient efficacy.
model.uncertainty: Eligibility, completion, active alternatives, clinical transfer, client residence, household grouping/resources and marginal gift capacity unmeasured. Other clinical channels unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: 2024annual7,901unique patients/35,438visits;5427behavioral/6248dental/18179primary visits not summed as people.

reports.priceScope: Reused accepted national hypothetical gift model with judged Denver benefit share; not a verified Colorado-restricted funding offer.

what: Dental Lifeline Network matches eligible adults with volunteer dentists and laboratories for comprehensive care.
Colorado has separate Denver-metro and rest-of-state coordinators; treatment is non-emergency and noncosmetic.
Applicants may qualify through age, disability, medical necessity or recurrent infection when unable to afford care.
strengths: A concrete volunteer treatment mechanism operates in Denver.
Accepted national health and signed-resource evidence is reused transparently.
Paid care, free alternatives and genuinely additional care are separate cohorts.
reservations: Current unique Denver completions and restricted capacity are unknown.
National general donations do not guarantee Denver allocation.
The currently linked state report is2021–22, not current annual treatment.

sections.what: Current Colorado eligibility includes over60, temporary/permanent disability, medical need or recurrent infections. National65+criteria are not substituted for local rules. Separate Denver-metro and rest-of-state coordinators demonstrate local operations, not all national benefits belonging to headquarters.
sections.monitoring: Request current unique completed Denver patients, residence, case mix, waits, state/national coordinated budget and volunteer capacity. Obtain a confirmed Colorado-restricted funding offer before making any local marginal-gift claim.
sections.qualitative: The currently linked Colorado report is printedMay2023 and reports fiscal2021–22 409served/144waitlist; it is not a current completed cohort. The accepted USA model's original denture trial supports selected oral function, not generic utility conversion; observational employment associations are not causal wage gains. Existing evidence and original session identities are reused, not counted as new national research.
sections.cost: Exact accepted national hypothetical$10,000gift framework reused: support1500/candidate, funding response.5, capacity8, completion.65, purchaser share.05, nonpurchaser additionality.75, annual utility.025for3finite years and reliefdelay1year are judgments. New Denver g=.04is explicitly an unmeasured share of the national incremental cohort and its full resource burdens, tested at.01/.08/0/1. Not derived from headquarters or historical state count. Outside-Denver effects remain unpriced, not zero whole-gift EV. Same-time paid/free alternatives cancel equivalent clinical gain/harm; full application cash, travel, missed net pay and maintenance remain. Eligible responsive workers.1 receive300net aftertax/benefit pay for2finiteyears with25%positive welfare independence; negative pay stays full. Generic utility-null can coexist with oral-function earnings, but no additional oral care removes dependent workers. Volunteer actual net cash loss is separately stressed. No retail donated value, saved-life medical clearance or survivor ordinary wages are credited.
sections.funding: Own current Colorado page links actual national DonorPerfect general intake; no transaction. National payee84-6129064 differs from affiliate group84-1043478. Latest full national expenses2,090,255/2,172,269/1,758,119, mean2,006,881, are context only—not central donor10kcost or matched Colorado budget. Do not gross-add affiliate transfers or donated retail care. Current public dental benefits and free clinics remain alternatives. A Colorado-restricted model requires confirmed state allocation and additional volunteers.

model.costScope: Exact reused national donor10kframework; partial judged Denver attribution, not annual operating-cost ratio or local funding offer.
model.geographicAttribution: Judged .04national incremental cohort/resource share inside ten-county DenverCBSA; .01/.08/0/1sensitivities; no residence/capacity measurement.
model.formula: N=min(G*b/c,capacity), C=N*r; buyers=C*p, free=C*(1-p)*(1-s), A=C*(1-p)*s. Clinical=g*[A*(u*exp(-ln(1+d)*L)*integral_0^T exp(-(ln(1+d)+m+loss+catchup)*t)dt-h*exp(-ln(1+d)*L))-N*ha]. Resources sum signed per-household logarithmic receipt flows. Positive wages use independence; negative wages and direct cash burdens are charged fully. Combined=clinical+resources; donor price=10*G/combined only if positive and known. Denver g=.04 applied once to health and signed resources.
model.counterfactual: No-new-gift includes committed public/private support, existing volunteer slots, insurance exhaustion, medically linked Medicare, other free providers and delayed private care. Otherwise purchasers and equivalent same-time free care have no incremental clinical benefit or matched treatment harm. Additional application burdens remain.
model.attribution: Funding response, completion, otherwise purchasing, same-time alternatives and later catchup are separate judged pathways. Common-alive earnings are not survival-created pay. One candidate-equivalent is one representative household; no hidden household-size or patient-repeat multiplier. Denver share is new judgment, not re-estimated national efficacy.
model.uncertainty: Local completed cohort, restricted capacity, matched state budget and residence unknown. Underlying national clinical/resource judgments reused, not empirical local effects.
model.nativeOutcomes: Fresh local page links2021–22state report409served/144waitlist. Neither historical statecount nor current nationalDDS4367served is Denvercompleted patients.

reports.priceScope: Full annual recipient cost against conditional injury-response, completed-therapy and youth-workforce channels; not whole-portfolio or marginal-gift EV.

what: Struggle of Love provides violence interruption, trauma support and school-based mentorship in Northeast Denver and North Aurora.
It also operates food distribution and youth employment opportunities.
Its teams connect families to counseling, crisis support and other community providers.
strengths: Local BIPOC-led organization with direct crisis and neighborhood access.
The 2024 report distinguishes shooting incidents, therapy completions and paid youth placements.
Food, employment and mental-health support address more than one pathway to household welfare.
reservations: Incident responses and paid placements do not establish incremental health or earnings gains.
Controlled violence-intervention evidence is uncertain and differs from SOL’s model.
Full annual costs cover several unquantified channels, so the displayed partial-channel reference is not a portfolio ranking.

sections.what: Struggle of Love provides violence interruption, trauma support and school-based mentorship in Northeast Denver and North Aurora. It also operates food distribution and youth employment opportunities. Its teams connect families to counseling, crisis support and other community providers.
sections.monitoring: The 2024 report describes 105 shooting incidents responded to, 30 therapy completions or successful discharges, 25 concession-employed youth and ten additional public youth-employment placements. Food pounds, STAR referrals and center visits are not unique causal outcomes. The 30 completed therapy clients form a separate conditional clinical channel; potential shared benefits with incident response are overlap-discounted rather than presumed independent. The next useful monitoring asks for unique completed clients, local residence, actual additional gains and costs; contacts and satisfaction are not causal outcomes.
sections.qualitative: The numerical reference hypothesizes one exposed person per shooting incident, 20% recipient contribution, a 5% additional injury-risk reduction and 0.1 QALY per avoided nonfatal injury. These are judgments, not measured SOL effects. A 130-person hospital-based pilot RCT found a 10.4 percentage-point repeat-injury difference with p=.15; a null or harmful result remains plausible. The distinct 25-person concession-workforce envelope uses 30% additional employment and $500 net annual household gain after taxes, benefit withdrawals and ordinary work costs, with $50 additional participation cost on every household and conservative positive overlap. Public placements, alternative jobs, employers and other support organizations matter. There is no child lifetime-wage or retail food-income claim. Separately, 30 completed/discharged therapy clients receive a conditional 0.03 QALY one-year improvement (10.95 healthy-day equivalents), 20% additionality and 50% positive clinical overlap reduction. The original Resick randomized trauma-therapy trial establishes symptom improvement against minimal attention, not a utility conversion, SOL fidelity or superiority to active local care. The utility hypothesis remains unmeasured and tested at zero. Therapy access costs $20 on all completed-client households, jointly netted with job costs in an explicit overlap sensitivity; no additional therapy earnings are assumed.
sections.cost: The full FY2024 recipient expense is $3,006,875. Unmeasured therapy causal magnitude, pantry and broader coalition contributions remain unknown, not zero, and the model does not estimate whole-portfolio or next-gift expected value. A $30/hour sensitivity for 3,720 volunteer hours adds shadow resources without asserting a household payer loss. Giving goes through the recipient’s own ColoradoGives link; no donation was executed.
sections.funding: The three full-year original expense figures are disclosed below. Current marginal donor capacity, public-provider substitution and restricted program allocations are not established by these filings.

model.costScope: Full FY2024 organizational expenses, not allocated injury-response or job-placement costs.
model.geographicAttribution: Northeast Denver and North Aurora service area is within pinned ten-county Denver CBSA19740; .98 recipient-benefit share is a judgment allowing outside residents.
model.formula: Health = incident envelope × patient-per-incident hypothesis × additionality × injury-risk response × finite QALY burden, less full incident-exposure harms. Separate workforce household joint logs include full costs and positive-only overlap; price = 10 × annual cost / (health + signed resource equivalent). A separate 30-person therapy clinical hypothesis adds finite benefit with positive clinical overlap reduction and full client harms; therapy/job household costs jointly logged if overlapping.
model.counterfactual: Other community, hospital and public violence response; publicly supported youth placements, ordinary jobs and other family resources.
model.attribution: Recipient contribution .2 for injury prevention and job additionality .3 are separate hypotheses; they are not inferred from partner STAR totals.
model.uncertainty: Primary pilot trial does not establish injury reduction; recipient injury severity, unique people, net wages, donor capacity and portfolio cost allocation remain unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: 105 incident responses; 25 concession-employed youth; ten public placements; 30 therapy completions/discharges; 3,720 volunteer hours in the 2024 report.

reports.priceScope: Full regional annual cost against a conditional Denver-resident abortion-access subset; not whole-portfolio or marginal-gift expected value.

what: PPRM provides sexual and reproductive health services, including contraception, abortion, screening and testing.
Its current region includes Colorado, New Mexico and Wyoming.
It also provides education, outreach and advocacy for access to care.
strengths: A substantial regional provider with patient-centered access and established giving routes.
Original recipient filings distinguish clients and service mix rather than national affiliate totals.
Original comparative studies support considering existing patients’ health and economic consequences together.
reservations: Denver residency, alternative-provider access and additional donation capacity are unmeasured.
Turnaway studies do not directly calibrate PPRM QALYs or after-tax household income.
The historical regional full-cost numerator covers many services omitted from this partial numerical reference.

sections.what: PPRM provides sexual and reproductive health services, including contraception, abortion, screening and testing. Its current region includes Colorado, New Mexico and Wyoming. It also provides education, outreach and advocacy for access to care.
sections.monitoring: The original FY2024 return reports over 56,000 clients across 21 Colorado, Nevada and New Mexico centers; 24% received abortion services. The model uses the lower-rounded 56,000 envelope, not a measured exact count or appointments. Current own giving information identifies Colorado, New Mexico and Wyoming. Clinic presence is not Denver residency: the 15% Denver-beneficiary share is a judgment with wide sensitivities, allowing other states and traveling patients. Monitor unique completed clients, local residence and actual additional gains and costs; contacts are not causal outcomes.
sections.qualitative: Original Turnaway studies followed patients receiving or being denied wanted abortions, with adjusted observational economic differences persisting four years and some physical-health differences after childbirth. They did not measure PPRM-specific provider additionality, a direct QALY gain or a precise after-tax dollar effect. Conditional hypotheses are 10% additional access, 0.02 maternal QALY over one year and $1,000 annual net household resources for four years after taxes, benefit withdrawals, childcare and ordinary work costs. Positive resource gains are halved for overlap; negative changes remain full. A $20 incremental time, travel and copay burden applies to all patient-household equivalents even when benefits fail. First-year benefits and costs share one log; later years are separate periods. No intrinsic welfare is assigned to unborn life or additional births, and no gross wage is substituted for net resources.
sections.cost: Full FY2024 expenses are $67,062,349 including netted direct fundraising costs; the three-full-year mean is $62,457,070. The whole regional numerator against abortion-only local benefits is a conditional partial-channel reference, not portfolio cost-effectiveness or a next-gift price. Contraception, STI care, screening, education and policy effects remain unquantified, not zero. Other providers, insurance, Medicaid, self-pay alternatives and public budgets constrain additionality. Provider and public-payer resource losses are tested separately; central zero is unmeasured, not proof of no cost. The official giving page identifies EIN 84-0404253 and routes to one-time or recurring support; no transaction was executed.
sections.funding: Three full-year original expenses are disclosed below. Current marginal donor capacity and restricted cost allocations remain unmeasured.

model.costScope: Full FY2024 regional organizational functional expenses plus netted direct event expenses. No verified abortion-channel allocation or marginal gift cost.
model.geographicAttribution: Judged .15 Denver ten-county CBSA19740 resident share applied once to historical regional clients; no headquarters or clinic-site shortcut.
model.formula: Patient health = N × abortion share × completed access × provider additionality × finite utility, minus full all-patient harms. Resource households = N × unique-household judgment; changed households use same access gates. Net same-year gains/costs jointly logged; later gains separately discounted. Price = 10C/(health + signed household resource equivalent).
model.counterfactual: Other accessible reproductive providers, covered/self-pay care and patient-chosen fertility paths; not all patients otherwise denied abortion.
model.attribution: Provider additionality .1 is a judgment, separate from the clinical/economic effect of obtaining wanted care. Current donations do not automatically create equivalent new capacity.
model.uncertainty: Denver residence, access alternatives, marginal capacity, utility, net resources and omitted services remain uncertain.
model.nativeOutcomes: Over 56,000 clients and 24% abortion-service share in the original FY2024 regional return; not exact unique households.

reports.program: Therapeutic school, day treatment and family mental-health support
reports.priceScope: Matched FY2025 full annual recipient cost against conditional school/day-treatment clinical and caregiver resources; not whole-portfolio or marginal-gift EV.

what: Tennyson provides a therapeutic K–12 school and day treatment for children with complex behavioral and emotional needs.
It also offers child and family therapy, parenting support and community-based services across Colorado.
Its TREE program supports young adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities preparing for more independent lives.
strengths: Intensive school-based clinical, family and educational support addresses children with high needs.
A current report provides a dated 63-student school-served envelope and 17 community-school transitions.
Original child-trauma trials provide a plausible clinical mechanism without assuming measured local utility.
reservations: School-served students are not documented completed clinical doses or causal successes.
Utility, eligible case mix, caregiver net resources and provider contribution remain judgments.
The whole annual recipient cost covers several important unquantified channels beyond the modeled school subset.

sections.what: Tennyson’s therapeutic school and day treatment combine special education, individual/group/family therapy, occupational and speech supports. School placement requires a district-approved IEP separate-school setting. Its statewide community services include outpatient family therapy and PCIT; current PCIT ages 2–7 usually involves approximately 20 sessions, a dose not automatically supplied to every school student. TREE adds independent living and employment preparation but does not establish net wage gains.
sections.monitoring: FY 2025 annual report page 2 says school/day treatment served 63 children, compared with 46 in FY 2024, and 17 returned to community schools. Nearly 1000 children and families is a mixed-unit statement, not a unique patient denominator. Reported reading/math improvements are pre/post educational outcomes, not controlled health utility. Next useful evidence is unique completed clinical dose, clinical case mix, local residence, caregiver work/time and active-provider comparison.
sections.qualitative: The original Cohen randomized trial assigned 229 sexually abused children 8–14 with PTSD symptoms to TF-CBT or child-centered therapy and found better child symptoms and caregiver outcomes. It did not measure a QALY conversion, and Tennyson’s broader trauma-informed/ARC/neurodevelopmental programs and autism/IDD case mix differ. The .5 compatible clinical subgroup and .03 one-year utility (10.95 healthy-day equivalents) are explicitly conditional hypotheses, not imported empirical effectiveness. Public school placements and covered therapists form an active alternative. PCIT abuse-recurrence evidence is not extrapolated to all school children.
sections.cost: Full FY 2025 IRS recipient expense is $ 11,829,871 including $ 171,197 netted direct fundraising cost. A separate $ 5,825,981 recognized school/day-treatment program-cost sensitivity is source-aligned but excludes allocated administration, fundraising and unrecognized resource costs; it is not a marginal-gift price. Clinical patient health is not reduced by household grouping. Caregiver households use .9 household factor, .2 incremental provider share, .5 clinical-compatible subgroup and .5 net-resource response, with $ 500 after-tax/benefit/work/childcare resource gain as a judgment—not child wages. Positive gains alone receive 50% overlap adjustment; all households retain $ 10 incremental access/time cost and all students retain process harms. Resource gains and costs share one household log. Residential, community, PCIT, TREE and educational welfare remain unknown, not zero.
sections.funding: The legal recipient is Tennyson Center for Children at Colorado Christian Home, DBA Tennyson Center for Children, EIN 61-1458290. Original full FY 2025/FY 2024/FY 2023 IRS expenses are $ 11,829,871/$ 13,581,906/$ 11,112,242; mean$ 12,174,673. Annual report financial totals differ from the IRS totals; no reconciliation is claimed. Current giving links to the recipient’s ColoradoGives profile; no donation executed. Public education payments, Medicaid and private-pay alternatives matter; restricted additional donor capacity remains unmeasured. Distinct public-provider loss and unrecognized external resource costs are tested, not presumed absent.

model.costScope: Full latest FY2025 recipient expenses plus netted fundraising costs; partial school benefit reference and observed school-only recognized-cost sensitivity.
model.geographicAttribution: Denver school benefits use judged .9resident share within ten-county CBSA19740, not headquarters or all statewide community clients.
model.formula: Health=(Npatients × compatible clinical subgroup × dose × provider contribution × finite expected clinical utility − full patient harms) × local share. Household resources use N × household grouping with gated caregiver gains; same-year full costs and gains jointly logged, distinct payer costs localized once. Price=10C/(health+signed resource equivalent).
model.counterfactual: Publicly funded special-education placements, other trauma/family therapists and covered services without Tennyson integration.
model.attribution: Judged .2incremental recipient contribution versus active alternatives, independent of clinical-compatible subgroup and dose; no automatic next-gift expansion.
model.uncertainty: Local utility, fidelity, completed dose, parent net earnings, household duplication, geographic share and omitted portfolio channels remain unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: FY2025 school/day-treatment served63children,17community-school transitions; nearly1000children and families overall is mixed units and not summed.
